title: DRC-U.S. Strategic Partnership: Government Rejects Claims of “Selling Off” National Interests
excerpt: Kinshasa | December 31, 2025 The Government of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has strongly denied allegations that the strategic partnership agreement signed with the United States constitutes a sell-off of the country’s economic or mineral interests. Speaking during a jo
title_en: DRC-U.S. Strategic Partnership: Government Rejects Claims of “Selling Off” National Interests
excerpt_en: Kinshasa | December 31, 2025 The Government of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has strongly denied allegations that the strategic partnership agreement signed with the United States constitutes a sell-off of the country’s economic or mineral interests. Speaking during a jo
body_en:
Kinshasa | December 31, 2025
The Government of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has strongly denied allegations that the strategic partnership agreement signed with the United States constitutes a sell-off of the country’s economic or mineral interests.
Speaking during a joint press briefing on Tuesday, December 30, Deputy Prime Minister in charge of the National Economy, Daniel Mukoko Samba, alongside the Minister of Communication and Media, Patrick Muyaya, sought to clarify the economic component of the Washington Agreement, signed on December 4, 2025, under the auspices of U.S. President Donald Trump.
“This is neither a deal, nor a contract, nor a document intended to sell out the interests of the DRC,” Mukoko Samba stated, responding to widespread criticism circulating in political circles, civil society, and online media.
A Framework Agreement, Not a Transaction
According to the government, the agreement should be understood as a strategic and legal framework for cooperation, rather than a transactional document involving the transfer of assets or concessions.
“This is a technical framework agreement defining areas of cooperation-economy and trade, security, governance, education, science, and technology-without ceding a single mine, designating a single investor, or awarding any contract,” Mukoko emphasized.
He categorically rejected claims of a “fire sale” of Congolese mineral resources, stating that no mining concessions, no preferential pricing, and no derogation from Congolese laws are mentioned in the agreement.
Major Development Projects Highlighted
Mukoko Samba underlined that the partnership aims to support peace, security, and economic development, with the prospect of large-scale job creation. He cited flagship projects included in the cooperation framework, notably:
The Grand Inga hydropower project
The Lobito Corridor
Key national road infrastructure projects
Government officials stressed that the agreement goes beyond the mining sector, encompassing defense, security, and governance reforms, positioning it as a long-term development partnership.
Monitoring and Governance Mechanisms
To ensure transparency and implementation, the Washington Agreement provides for the establishment of a joint steering committee, composed of five representatives from each country. The committee is expected to convene within 90 days of the agreement’s signing, with evaluations scheduled every three years.
In the event of disputes, Mukoko Samba noted that Prime Minister Judith Suminwa would serve as the arbitration authority, providing an institutional mechanism for dialogue and resolution.
Government Pushback Against “Misinformation”
Minister Patrick Muyaya echoed these clarifications, accusing critics of spreading misinformation based on emotional or partial readings of a public and technical document. The executive branch insists that the agreement in no way compromises Congolese sovereignty.
As debates continue within political and civil society circles, the government says it remains committed to transparency and to defending national interests while pursuing strategic international partnerships.

title: Corneille Nangaa Delivers End-of-Year Message, Calls for Unity and Justice in DRC
excerpt: Kinshasa / RDC - December 31, 2025 Corneille Nangaa, coordinator of the Alliance Fleuve Congo (AFC) and M23, addressed the Congolese people in a formal end-of-year message, posted on social media, reflecting on 2025 and outlining priorities for 2026. Speaking from a formal office
title_en: Corneille Nangaa Delivers End-of-Year Message, Calls for Unity and Justice in DRC
excerpt_en: Kinshasa / RDC - December 31, 2025 Corneille Nangaa, coordinator of the Alliance Fleuve Congo (AFC) and M23, addressed the Congolese people in a formal end-of-year message, posted on social media, reflecting on 2025 and outlining priorities for 2026. Speaking from a formal office
body_en:
Kinshasa / RDC - December 31, 2025
Corneille Nangaa, coordinator of the Alliance Fleuve Congo (AFC) and M23, addressed the Congolese people in a formal end-of-year message, posted on social media, reflecting on 2025 and outlining priorities for 2026.
Speaking from a formal office setting with AFC and DRC flags in the background, Nangaa began by paying tribute to fallen fighters and the Congolese Revolutionary Army for their sacrifices in the struggle for freedom. He also thanked AFC political personnel and called for the voluntary return of Congolese refugees, including those recently expelled to Burundi.
He highlighted progress in areas “liberated” under AFC/M23 control, emphasizing:
Restoration of peace and security
Establishment of functional administration
Operational justice system
Resilient local economy and emerging financial institutions
Infrastructure development
Mass return of internally displaced persons
Resumption of agriculture, schools, and hospitals
Nangaa positioned the AFC/M23 as a credible alternative to the current government.
He sharply criticized the Kinshasa government, accusing it of betraying 2025 peace agreements, including joint communiqués, prisoner release mechanisms, and ceasefire monitoring. Key allegations included:
No political prisoners released
Repeated ceasefire violations, including bombardments of civilians
Official promotion of ethnic hate speech, particularly against Kinyarwanda-speaking Tutsis and Swahili speakers
Tribal purges within the army
Massacres, arbitrary arrests, endemic corruption, and looting of natural resources
Nangaa also highlighted mass popular protests across multiple cities and called for national unity, an end to impunity, and sustainable peace based on truth.
Looking ahead to 2026, he pledged continued struggle for freedom, justice, peace, and the reconstruction of the Congolese state. He concluded with New Year wishes, envisioning a united, peaceful, and prosperous Congo.
The message was delivered in a solemn, structured, and presidential tone, underscoring the AFC/M23’s political narrative and priorities for the upcoming year.

title: DRC Condemns Continued Rwandan Occupation and Expansion in the East
excerpt: Kinshasa - The Government of the Democratic Republic of Congo has strongly denounced the continued occupation of parts of its national territory by Rwandan forces, accusing Kigali of progressively expanding its presence in the eastern regions of the country, particularly around U
title_en: DRC Condemns Continued Rwandan Occupation and Expansion in the East
excerpt_en: Kinshasa - The Government of the Democratic Republic of Congo has strongly denounced the continued occupation of parts of its national territory by Rwandan forces, accusing Kigali of progressively expanding its presence in the eastern regions of the country, particularly around U
body_en:
Kinshasa - The Government of the Democratic Republic of Congo has strongly denounced the continued occupation of parts of its national territory by Rwandan forces, accusing Kigali of progressively expanding its presence in the eastern regions of the country, particularly around Uvira and its surrounding areas, with a southward advance.
The condemnation was made public on Wednesday, December 31, in a press release issued by the Ministry of Communication and Media. In the statement, Congolese authorities described the situation as a flagrant violation of the country’s sovereignty, a serious and repeated breach of international law, and a clear disregard for regional and international commitments.
The government further warned that the ongoing occupation is exacerbating an already fragile security and humanitarian situation, leaving civilian populations increasingly exposed to widespread violence and instability in the affected areas.
No immediate response was issued by Rwandan authorities at the time of publication.

title: DRC Government Denounces Repression Ahead of Planned Goma Protest
excerpt: Goma, DRC - January 2, 2026 On the eve of a planned citizens’ march in Goma, scheduled for Friday, January 2, 2026, the Congolese government has denounced what it describes as a climate of repression and intimidation in areas under occupation. In a statement, Patrick Muyaya, Gove
title_en: DRC Government Denounces Repression Ahead of Planned Goma Protest
excerpt_en: Goma, DRC - January 2, 2026 On the eve of a planned citizens’ march in Goma, scheduled for Friday, January 2, 2026, the Congolese government has denounced what it describes as a climate of repression and intimidation in areas under occupation. In a statement, Patrick Muyaya, Gove
body_en:
Goma, DRC - January 2, 2026
On the eve of a planned citizens’ march in Goma, scheduled for Friday, January 2, 2026, the Congolese government has denounced what it describes as a climate of repression and intimidation in areas under occupation.
In a statement, Patrick Muyaya, Government Spokesperson and Minister of Communication and Media, said residents of Goma are facing arbitrary arrests, intimidation, and preventive repression, measures he claims are aimed at preventing any peaceful expression of dissent. According to the minister, these actions have created what he called a “climate of terror.”
Muyaya also pointed to similar incidents in Sake, where several young people reportedly disappeared after participating in demonstrations last December against what he described as Rwandan occupation.
“These events confirm the Congolese people’s total rejection of the occupation,” Muyaya said, adding that civilians are exhausted by what he described as abuses, torture, and massacres. He expressed the government’s solidarity with the victims of repression and with civilian populations living in affected areas.
Despite the reported crackdown, the government spokesperson said the population continues to resist and voice opposition, pledging that such resistance will persist until the withdrawal of all foreign forces from Congolese territory.
Muyaya further accused Rwanda and the M23 of attempting to export methods of repression, intimidation, imprisonment, and the suppression of freedoms into the DRC, stressing that “coercion can generate neither legitimacy nor popular support.”

title: DRC: 73rd Ordinary Cabinet Meeting Focuses on Security and Economic Priorities for 2026
excerpt: Kinshasa, January 2, 2026 Amid persistent tensions in the eastern provinces and as the Democratic Republic of the Congo begins its term on the United Nations Security Council, President Félix Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo on Friday chaired the 73rd ordinary meeting of the Council
title_en: DRC: 73rd Ordinary Cabinet Meeting Focuses on Security and Economic Priorities for 2026
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, January 2, 2026 Amid persistent tensions in the eastern provinces and as the Democratic Republic of the Congo begins its term on the United Nations Security Council, President Félix Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo on Friday chaired the 73rd ordinary meeting of the Council
body_en:
Kinshasa, January 2, 2026
Amid persistent tensions in the eastern provinces and as the Democratic Republic of the Congo begins its term on the United Nations Security Council, President Félix Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo on Friday chaired the 73rd ordinary meeting of the Council of Ministers at the African Union City in Kinshasa.
The government briefing, delivered by the Minister of Communication and Media and government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya Katembwe, outlined the main discussions of the session, which centered on security challenges, economic recovery, and institutional reforms expected to shape the country’s agenda in 2026.
Presidential address: security vigilance and diplomatic engagement
Opening the meeting, President Tshisekedi focused on national sovereignty and the deteriorating security situation in eastern DRC. He strongly condemned repeated ceasefire violations attributed to various armed coalitions, including national forces, militias, and external actors, echoing recent accusations made by the AFC/M23.
The Head of State warned of serious risks facing civilian populations, including Congolese Tutsi communities, and called for urgent international action. He also welcomed the DRC’s new mandate as a non-permanent member of the UN Security Council for 2026-2027, describing it as a strategic opportunity to influence regional security dynamics, particularly ongoing diplomatic efforts involving Rwanda under international facilitation.
President Tshisekedi further stressed the need for deep state reforms in 2026, with priority given to strengthening the justice system, consolidating institutions, and intensifying the fight against corruption in response to governance shortcomings observed in 2025.
Prime Minister’s intervention: assessment and outlook of government action
Prime Minister Judith Suminwa Tuluka presented an update on the implementation of the Government Action Program (2024-2028). She announced that a comprehensive evaluation of government performance would begin in January 2026, with the aim of adjusting priorities to improve effectiveness.
Key highlights included:
Industrialization and economic transformation: Particular emphasis was placed on the Maluku Special Economic Zone, where recent assessments have helped define an industrial roadmap focused on large-scale job creation and economic diversification through local processing of natural resources.
Rural and social development: The government plans to reinforce support for farmers, expand access to low-interest loans for young people and women, and allocate 10% of locally generated revenues to programs targeting these groups.
The Prime Minister also pointed to improved fiscal performance, with tax pressure nearing the African average, while calling for a broader tax base to finance critical infrastructure in roads, energy, and transport.
Information briefings: security, health, and the economy
Several sectoral updates were presented to the Council:
Security: The Minister of Defense reported ongoing military operations against armed groups in Ituri, North Kivu, and South Kivu, including air strikes and actions targeting rebel coalitions. Authorities raised concerns over continued massacres and population displacement, reaffirming the government’s commitment to restoring state authority in occupied areas.
Health and environment: Ministers reviewed the response to ongoing epidemics, including cholera and measles, and urged continued vigilance in the post-Covid context. Discussions also covered cybersecurity and data protection, with plans for the establishment of a national agency.

title: Martin Fayulu Renewes Call for Inclusive Dialogue Amid Deepening Crisis in the DRC
excerpt: Kinshasa | December 31, 2025 - Congolese opposition leader Martin Fayulu has reiterated his call for an inclusive national dialogue, warning that the Democratic Republic of Congo is facing what he described as “one of the most serious crises in its history.” Fayulu made the remar
title_en: Martin Fayulu Renewes Call for Inclusive Dialogue Amid Deepening Crisis in the DRC
excerpt_en: Kinshasa | December 31, 2025 - Congolese opposition leader Martin Fayulu has reiterated his call for an inclusive national dialogue, warning that the Democratic Republic of Congo is facing what he described as “one of the most serious crises in its history.” Fayulu made the remar
body_en:
Kinshasa | December 31, 2025 - Congolese opposition leader Martin Fayulu has reiterated his call for an inclusive national dialogue, warning that the Democratic Republic of Congo is facing what he described as “one of the most serious crises in its history.”
Fayulu made the remarks in a New Year’s message to the Congolese people, published on social media on Wednesday, December 31, 2025. In the message, he urged political leaders to engage in open discussions aimed at restoring stability and national cohesion.
The opposition figure sharply criticized the agreements signed on December 4 in Washington, arguing that they commit the future of the DRC without national debate, transparency, or popular consent. “These agreements are opaque. The people do not know. The people have not decided,” Fayulu said.
According to him, rejecting inclusive dialogue would amount to rejecting peace, stressing that only a broad-based political process can provide a sustainable solution to the country’s ongoing political and security challenges.
DRC Joins UN Security Council, Says Entry Is “a Mission, Not a Reward”
Kinshasa, January 2, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) officially takes its seat on the United Nations Security Council this Friday as a non-permanent member, marking a significant milestone in the country’s diplomatic engagement on the global stage.
Foreign Affairs Minister Thérèse Kayikwamba Wagner underscored the gravity of the moment, stressing that the DRC’s entry into the Council should not be seen as a symbolic achievement, but as a serious responsibility. “By officially joining the United Nations Security Council, our country assumes a major responsibility in the service of international peace and security,” she said. “It is a moment of dignity, but above all, a moment of commitment.”
Drawing on the DRC’s own history, the minister highlighted the country’s understanding of the human cost of conflict and instability. She noted that the Congolese experience gives the nation a unique perspective on the expectations of civilian populations who look to the United Nations in times of war and insecurity.
Thérèse Kayikwamba Wagner outlined the DRC’s mandate on the Council around three core priorities: defending respect for international law, reaffirming the non-negotiable principle of state sovereignty, and amplifying the voices of populations affected by conflict, particularly in Africa.
According to the minister, the DRC approaches its role on the Security Council with a message shaped by lived experience-one rooted in truth, responsibility, and a firm commitment to contributing to lasting solutions to international crises.

title: Kinshasa Press Review: Focus on Tshisekedi-Lourenço Talks on Eastern DRC
excerpt: Kinshasa, Tuesday, January 6, 2026 - The majority of newspapers published in Kinshasa this Tuesday focused on the private meeting held in Luanda between Congolese President Félix Tshisekedi and his Angolan counterpart João Lourenço, who also serves as Chairperson of the African U
title_en: Kinshasa Press Review: Focus on Tshisekedi-Lourenço Talks on Eastern DRC
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, Tuesday, January 6, 2026 - The majority of newspapers published in Kinshasa this Tuesday focused on the private meeting held in Luanda between Congolese President Félix Tshisekedi and his Angolan counterpart João Lourenço, who also serves as Chairperson of the African U
body_en:
Kinshasa, Tuesday, January 6, 2026 - The majority of newspapers published in Kinshasa this Tuesday focused on the private meeting held in Luanda between Congolese President Félix Tshisekedi and his Angolan counterpart João Lourenço, who also serves as Chairperson of the African Union.
According to press reports, the talks took place against a backdrop of a rapidly deteriorating security situation in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo. Before departing for Luanda, President Félix Tshisekedi indicated that the primary objective of his visit was to advance peace efforts in eastern DRC. During the meeting, João Lourenço reportedly presented several proposals that the Congolese head of state described as constructive and capable of contributing significantly to a peaceful resolution of the conflict. Despite these discussions, President Tshisekedi emphasized that the situation on the ground remains “a war imposed upon us.”
The meeting occurred one day after the ratification of the Washington Accords between Kinshasa and Kigali, carried out in the presence of US President Donald Trump, and at a time when fighting continues to intensify in the eastern part of the country.
During his brief stay in Luanda, President Tshisekedi reiterated his determination to accelerate the search for peace through African-led diplomacy. As Chairperson of the African Union, João Lourenço is viewed as a central figure in efforts to revitalize continental mechanisms for conflict prevention and resolution. The discussions in Luanda are presented as complementary to existing diplomatic initiatives, notably those undertaken in Washington and Doha.
For several months, the Congolese authorities have sought to internationalize the crisis in eastern DRC and rally greater political support, denouncing what they describe as a persistent violation of national sovereignty. The repeated reference to an “imposed war” reflects a desire to shift the narrative from chronic internal insecurity to broader regional responsibility.
During the meeting, President Félix Tshisekedi also expressed his gratitude to João Lourenço for his commitment to peace in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, as diplomatic efforts continue amid ongoing instability in the east.

title: DRC Launches Digital Reform to Modernize Foreign Trade Management
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC | December 29, 2025 The Democratic Republic of Congo has taken a major step in modernizing foreign trade with the launch of electronic transmission of documentation packages from the S-ONE system of the Integrated Single Window Operating Company (SEGUCE) to SYDONIA
title_en: DRC Launches Digital Reform to Modernize Foreign Trade Management
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC | December 29, 2025 The Democratic Republic of Congo has taken a major step in modernizing foreign trade with the launch of electronic transmission of documentation packages from the S-ONE system of the Integrated Single Window Operating Company (SEGUCE) to SYDONIA
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC | December 29, 2025
The Democratic Republic of Congo has taken a major step in modernizing foreign trade with the launch of electronic transmission of documentation packages from the S-ONE system of the Integrated Single Window Operating Company (SEGUCE) to SYDONIA World, the automated system of the General Directorate of Customs and Excise (DGDA). The launch was presided over by Prime Minister Judith Suminwa on Monday, December 29.
This historic reform is designed to facilitate import and export operations, improve information flow between stakeholders, and strengthen resource mobilization for the state coffers.
According to Minister of Foreign Trade Julien Paluku, the reform will reduce costs and delays for import, export, and transit operations, ensure complete transparency, guarantee traceability, and enforce standards.
"I want to reassure economic operators that this reform will not hinder trade operations. On the contrary, it will reduce costs and delays, strengthen transparency, and protect agents from harassment," Paluku emphasized.
Prime Minister Suminwa described the initiative as a historic revolution for the DRC, further consolidating its integration into international trade.
“The implementation of electronic transmission marks a decisive step in digital development, in line with the Sustainable Development Goals,” she stated.
Finance Minister Doudou Fwamba highlighted that the reform will simplify procedures and increase public revenue by combating customs fraud.
Beyond technical modernization, the reform also represents a shift in administrative culture, promising reduced processing times, enhanced traceability, increased transparency, and a direct fight against fraud. Mandatory for all users, the new system is seen as a critical lever for improving the business climate, securing public revenue, and integrating the DRC into international trade standards.

title: Mukoko Samba Calls for Regulation of Local Product Supply Chains
excerpt: Kinshasa, January 2, 2026 - The Deputy Prime Minister in charge of the National Economy, Daniel Mukoko Samba, has reiterated the government’s determination to standardize and regulate the local value chain, from production areas to consumer markets, in order to strengthen the sup
title_en: Mukoko Samba Calls for Regulation of Local Product Supply Chains
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, January 2, 2026 - The Deputy Prime Minister in charge of the National Economy, Daniel Mukoko Samba, has reiterated the government’s determination to standardize and regulate the local value chain, from production areas to consumer markets, in order to strengthen the sup
body_en:
Kinshasa, January 2, 2026 - The Deputy Prime Minister in charge of the National Economy, Daniel Mukoko Samba, has reiterated the government’s determination to standardize and regulate the local value chain, from production areas to consumer markets, in order to strengthen the supply of locally produced goods.
He made these remarks following a field visit to the public port of Kinkole in the N’sele commune, as well as the ports of Baramoto and CDI Bwamanda in the Gombe commune of Kinshasa.
The visit began at the fishing port of Kinkole, where the Deputy Prime Minister observed the arrival of sacks of grain from the provinces of Kwilu, Maï-Ndombe, and Kasaï. He also toured the area where cassava chips, unloaded from fishing boats, were being displayed for sale.
The ministerial delegation then proceeded to the port of Baramoto to assess ongoing supply challenges, before concluding the tour at the port of CDI Bwamanda.
At CDI Bwamanda, Daniel Mukoko Samba visited the production plant, which has a combined capacity of 50 tons per day for both the old and new units, bringing the total capacity to 100 tons per day. This output represents more than 10,000 bags of 10 kilograms per day, or approximately 2,500 bags of 25 kilograms, all destined for the Kinshasa market.
CDI Bwamanda, a Partner of the State
On this occasion, Édouard Sangina Toko, Deputy Managing Director of CDI Bwamanda, welcomed the Deputy Prime Minister’s visit, describing it as “very encouraging.”
He recalled that the Bwamanda International Development Center (CDI Bwamanda) has long played a key role in feeding the city of Kinshasa, particularly during the 1980s, 1990s, 2000s, and 2010s. However, as a non-profit organization, the institution has faced a decline in subsidies, which largely explains its current difficulties.
According to him, the main challenges facing the organization include:
access to quality seeds,
insufficient support for farmers, and
the poor state of road infrastructure, which complicates the transport of agricultural produce, even when production levels are adequate.
Despite these constraints, Édouard Sangina Toko stressed that CDI Bwamanda retains significant potential to revive its activities, provided it receives substantial financial support from the government, particularly to strengthen rural development services and build storage silos.
“To date, CDI Bwamanda has adequate infrastructure, with more than seven depots of 2,000 square meters each in Kinshasa, large warehouses in the interior of the country, as well as facilities dedicated to the storage and processing of maize. It is therefore positioned as a reliable partner that the State can support to contribute sustainably to the national food supply,” he affirmed.

title: DRC Launches New Secure Vehicle License Plate System
excerpt: Kinshasa, January 6, 2026 - The General Directorate of Taxes (DGI) is set to officially launch a new secure vehicle license plate this Tuesday, January 6, 2026, in Kinshasa, marking a major step in the modernization of vehicle registration in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
title_en: DRC Launches New Secure Vehicle License Plate System
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, January 6, 2026 - The General Directorate of Taxes (DGI) is set to officially launch a new secure vehicle license plate this Tuesday, January 6, 2026, in Kinshasa, marking a major step in the modernization of vehicle registration in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
body_en:
Kinshasa, January 6, 2026 - The General Directorate of Taxes (DGI) is set to officially launch a new secure vehicle license plate this Tuesday, January 6, 2026, in Kinshasa, marking a major step in the modernization of vehicle registration in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
According to a statement from the DGI, the new license plate-designed in line with international standards-will replace the old system with the aim of improving road safety, harmonizing the national vehicle registration framework, and facilitating traffic controls across the country.
The tax authority informed the general public, particularly vehicle owners and road users, of this government measure, emphasizing its importance for regulatory compliance and better traffic management.
The DGI is urging all concerned parties to promptly obtain the new license plates, noting that widespread adoption is essential to ensure the full harmonization of the registration system.
This initiative, the DGI added, is part of the government’s broader commitment to modernizing public services, strengthening road safety, and enhancing the efficiency and security of vehicle identification in the DRC.

title: Bunia Media Observe Three Days of Radio Silence After Murder of RTNC Journalist
excerpt: Bunia, Ituri Province | December 30, 2025 More than twenty radio stations and online media outlets operating in Bunia, in the eastern province of Ituri, began a three-day suspension of broadcasting and news programs on Tuesday to protest what they describe as repeated attacks aga
title_en: Bunia Media Observe Three Days of Radio Silence After Murder of RTNC Journalist
excerpt_en: Bunia, Ituri Province | December 30, 2025 More than twenty radio stations and online media outlets operating in Bunia, in the eastern province of Ituri, began a three-day suspension of broadcasting and news programs on Tuesday to protest what they describe as repeated attacks aga
body_en:
Bunia, Ituri Province | December 30, 2025
More than twenty radio stations and online media outlets operating in Bunia, in the eastern province of Ituri, began a three-day suspension of broadcasting and news programs on Tuesday to protest what they describe as repeated attacks against journalists and growing threats to press freedom.
The action follows the brutal killing of RTNC journalist Thierry Lole, who was murdered at his home on Sunday night by unidentified armed men, according to local media organizations.
Residents of Bunia woke up on Tuesday to an unusual silence on the airwaves. Several radio stations halted their regular programming entirely, while others suspended news bulletins, airing only music in tribute to their slain colleague.
According to journalists’ rights organizations, the killing highlights ongoing efforts by unknown actors to intimidate and silence the press in a region affected by chronic insecurity since 2017. The coordinated media blackout is intended to pressure authorities to take responsibility for ensuring the effective protection of civilians, including media professionals, in Ituri.
“These three days of radio silence are a strong message to the authorities,” said Constant Same Bagalwa, editor-in-chief of Radio Les Rebâtisseurs and director of the online outlet Bunia News. “They reflect the media’s refusal to continue working under constant threat.”
Ituri Province is home to approximately forty radio stations, several of which operate outside Bunia. A number of these outlets have also announced their intention to join the protest, extending the media blackout across parts of the province.

title: Over 20 Houses Destroyed in Kazumba Following Ethnic Conflict
excerpt: Kazumba, Kasai-Central | December 29, 2025 More than twenty homes were set ablaze overnight from Sunday to Monday in the village of Bena-Bilala, Kazumba Territory, according to local sources. The incident is linked to an ethnic conflict triggered by the death of a local resident.
title_en: Over 20 Houses Destroyed in Kazumba Following Ethnic Conflict
excerpt_en: Kazumba, Kasai-Central | December 29, 2025 More than twenty homes were set ablaze overnight from Sunday to Monday in the village of Bena-Bilala, Kazumba Territory, according to local sources. The incident is linked to an ethnic conflict triggered by the death of a local resident.
body_en:
Kazumba, Kasai-Central | December 29, 2025
More than twenty homes were set ablaze overnight from Sunday to Monday in the village of Bena-Bilala, Kazumba Territory, according to local sources. The incident is linked to an ethnic conflict triggered by the death of a local resident.
The victim, Muyaya Mbombo, a man in his forties, died on Saturday after reportedly consuming excessive alcohol. His family, believing he had been murdered, retaliated by setting fire to surrounding homes, destroying more than twenty thatched houses and two corrugated iron structures, according to Jean-Carré Muyaya, coordinator of the New Congolese Society in Kazumba.
“This tragedy began with Muyaya Mbombo’s celebrations on December 25. Two days later, he drank excessively and died behind the houses of the villagers. His family assumed foul play and set fire to more than twenty houses,” explained Jean-Carré Muyaya.
Calm has been temporarily restored thanks to the intervention of the National Police, but many residents have fled to the bush, fearing further reprisals.
Local authorities are being urged to strengthen security in the area, and calls have been made for the perpetrators to be brought to justice. The incident highlights a resurgence of insecurity in the region, fueled by misunderstandings and ethnic tensions.

title: Journalists in Bunia Protest the Murder of Colleague Thierry Lole
excerpt: Bunia, Ituri, DRC | December 29, 2025 Journalists in Bunia held a march on Monday morning, ending at the Ituri provincial governor's office, to protest the murder of Thierry Lole, a colleague at the Congolese National Radio and Television (RTNC). Lole was killed at his home by as
title_en: Journalists in Bunia Protest the Murder of Colleague Thierry Lole
excerpt_en: Bunia, Ituri, DRC | December 29, 2025 Journalists in Bunia held a march on Monday morning, ending at the Ituri provincial governor's office, to protest the murder of Thierry Lole, a colleague at the Congolese National Radio and Television (RTNC). Lole was killed at his home by as
body_en:
Bunia, Ituri, DRC | December 29, 2025
Journalists in Bunia held a march on Monday morning, ending at the Ituri provincial governor's office, to protest the murder of Thierry Lole, a colleague at the Congolese National Radio and Television (RTNC). Lole was killed at his home by assailants armed with machetes during the night of Sunday to Monday, according to local sources.
Dozens of media professionals demanded a swift investigation during the demonstration.
According to protesters, criminals armed with machetes broke into Lole’s home around 2:00 a.m., striking him severely on the head before fleeing without stealing anything. Lole later died from his injuries at Salama Hospital on Monday morning.
During a meeting with the provincial governor, journalists called for an investigation to identify and bring to justice the perpetrators, requested that funeral expenses be covered, and advocated for a media blackout to highlight the danger facing journalists.
Protesters also cited increasing attacks against journalists in Ituri, referencing a recent kidnapping of a journalist, who was held hostage for four days, followed by the murder of his child by unknown assailants.
Provincial authorities stated that an investigation is underway to apprehend those responsible and promised to cover funeral expenses.

title: DRC - Monkeypox Cases Declining: Around 300 Weekly Reports
excerpt: Kinshasa, January 1, 2026 The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is currently reporting approximately 300 cases of monkeypox per week, a significant decrease compared to previous months, according to Christian Ngandu, coordinator of the Public Health Emergency Operations Center (
title_en: DRC - Monkeypox Cases Declining: Around 300 Weekly Reports
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, January 1, 2026 The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is currently reporting approximately 300 cases of monkeypox per week, a significant decrease compared to previous months, according to Christian Ngandu, coordinator of the Public Health Emergency Operations Center (
body_en:
Kinshasa, January 1, 2026
The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is currently reporting approximately 300 cases of monkeypox per week, a significant decrease compared to previous months, according to Christian Ngandu, coordinator of the Public Health Emergency Operations Center (PHOOC) at the National Institute of Public Health (INSP).
During a press briefing in Kinshasa on December 31, 2025, Ngandu explained that 19 health zones reported cases in December, down from initial expectations of 401 zones between 2024 and November 2025.
“Initially, we were receiving about 2,000 notifications per week, but currently, we have between 250 and 300,” he said, highlighting the encouraging trend in the reduction of new cases.
Most of the reported cases are concentrated in North Kivu and South Kivu, areas affected by insecurity, as well as in Sankuru.
Health authorities continue to monitor the situation closely and urge communities to remain vigilant and follow recommended public health measures to prevent further spread.

title: Displaced Families Spend New Year in Fear and Hunger in Ituri’s Savo Plain
excerpt: Djugu Territory, Ituri | January 1, 2026 - More than a thousand residents from Bulé and neighboring villages in the Djugu territory of Ituri Province spent New Year’s Day in dire conditions after fleeing renewed clashes between the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo
title_en: Displaced Families Spend New Year in Fear and Hunger in Ituri’s Savo Plain
excerpt_en: Djugu Territory, Ituri | January 1, 2026 - More than a thousand residents from Bulé and neighboring villages in the Djugu territory of Ituri Province spent New Year’s Day in dire conditions after fleeing renewed clashes between the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo
body_en:
Djugu Territory, Ituri | January 1, 2026 - More than a thousand residents from Bulé and neighboring villages in the Djugu territory of Ituri Province spent New Year’s Day in dire conditions after fleeing renewed clashes between the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) and militias of the Convention for the Popular Revolution (CRP) led by Thomas Lubanga.
The displaced families have sought refuge in the Savo Plain, located about four kilometers north of Bulé, where they are living in extreme precarity. According to local sources, the most recent group of displaced persons arrived on Wednesday, following intensified fighting in the area.
“For more than a week now, these vulnerable people-mostly women and children-have been sleeping in the open air without food or basic necessities,” said Floribert Dezunga, one of the displaced residents.
Traditional local authorities warn that the continued armed violence in the Bulé region could trigger a major humanitarian catastrophe if urgent assistance is not provided. They are calling on national authorities and humanitarian organizations to open a humanitarian corridor to facilitate aid delivery and prevent further loss of life among the displaced population.

title: DRC Reports Decline in Monkeypox Cases, Around 300 New Infections Weekly
excerpt: Kinshasa | January 1, 2026 - Health authorities in the Democratic Republic of Congo report a notable decline in monkeypox cases, with approximately 250 to 300 new infections recorded each week, according to officials from the National Institute of Public Health (INSP). Speaking a
title_en: DRC Reports Decline in Monkeypox Cases, Around 300 New Infections Weekly
excerpt_en: Kinshasa | January 1, 2026 - Health authorities in the Democratic Republic of Congo report a notable decline in monkeypox cases, with approximately 250 to 300 new infections recorded each week, according to officials from the National Institute of Public Health (INSP). Speaking a
body_en:
Kinshasa | January 1, 2026 - Health authorities in the Democratic Republic of Congo report a notable decline in monkeypox cases, with approximately 250 to 300 new infections recorded each week, according to officials from the National Institute of Public Health (INSP).
Speaking at a press conference held on Wednesday, December 31, 2025, the coordinator of the Public Health Emergency Operations Center (PHOOC), Christian Ngandu, said that only 19 health zones reported monkeypox cases in December 2025, compared to much higher figures earlier in the outbreak.
“Regarding monkeypox, the data is declining,” Ngandu stated. “Initially, we were receiving about 2,000 notifications per week, but currently, the number has dropped to between 250 and 300.”
He noted that between 2024 and November 2025, authorities had anticipated the disease would affect 401 health zones nationwide. However, in December, reports were limited to just 19 zones.
According to Ngandu, a significant number of the affected health zones are located in North Kivu and South Kivu, provinces facing persistent insecurity, as well as in Sankuru Province.
Health officials continue to monitor the situation, warning that insecurity in certain regions remains a challenge to effective disease surveillance and response.

title: FARDC Pays Tribute to Colonel Mamadou Ndala Twelve Years After His Assassination
excerpt: Kinshasa, January 3, 2026 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (FARDC) on Friday paid tribute to Colonel Mamadou Ndala, marking twelve years since his assassination in an ambush on his convoy while he was traveling to Eringeti, in North Kivu. On this day of
title_en: FARDC Pays Tribute to Colonel Mamadou Ndala Twelve Years After His Assassination
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, January 3, 2026 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (FARDC) on Friday paid tribute to Colonel Mamadou Ndala, marking twelve years since his assassination in an ambush on his convoy while he was traveling to Eringeti, in North Kivu. On this day of
body_en:
Kinshasa, January 3, 2026 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (FARDC) on Friday paid tribute to Colonel Mamadou Ndala, marking twelve years since his assassination in an ambush on his convoy while he was traveling to Eringeti, in North Kivu.
On this day of remembrance, the Congolese army reaffirmed its determination to pursue the struggle for which Mamadou Ndala gave his life: the defense of a united, sovereign, and peaceful Democratic Republic of the Congo.
“Honor and glory to General Mamadou Ndala. The grateful nation will never forget you. Long live the FARDC, long live the Democratic Republic of Congo!” the army declared in an official message.
At the time of his death, Colonel Mamadou Ndala was leading military operations against the Ugandan Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) rebels and other armed groups operating in the Beni region.
Widely regarded as a national hero, Mamadou Ndala remains an emblematic figure of courage, loyalty, and supreme sacrifice in the defense of the homeland. A respected commander and exceptional officer, he distinguished himself through his unwavering commitment to the fight for peace, security, and the territorial integrity of the DRC.
According to the FARDC, his leadership on the ground, his close connection with the troops, and his determination in the face of the enemy have left a lasting mark on the history of the Congolese army. His legacy, the military emphasized, remains alive in the hearts of Congolese soldiers and the entire nation.
The commemoration of the 12th anniversary of Colonel Mamadou Ndala’s assassination comes at a time when the FARDC is engaged in ongoing confrontations with AFC/M23 rebels, reportedly supported by the Rwandan army, in the eastern part of the country.

title: Over 450 Measles Cases Reported in Kasai-Oriental in Two Weeks
excerpt: Kasai-Oriental, January 3, 2026 - More than 450 cases of measles have been recorded in Kasai-Oriental province over the past two weeks, raising serious public health concerns. According to health authorities, at least 456 cases have been registered since December 15. Dr. Jean-Pie
title_en: Over 450 Measles Cases Reported in Kasai-Oriental in Two Weeks
excerpt_en: Kasai-Oriental, January 3, 2026 - More than 450 cases of measles have been recorded in Kasai-Oriental province over the past two weeks, raising serious public health concerns. According to health authorities, at least 456 cases have been registered since December 15. Dr. Jean-Pie
body_en:
Kasai-Oriental, January 3, 2026 - More than 450 cases of measles have been recorded in Kasai-Oriental province over the past two weeks, raising serious public health concerns. According to health authorities, at least 456 cases have been registered since December 15.
Dr. Jean-Pierre Sumba, the physician in charge of the measles response, reported that all 19 health zones in the province have been affected. He noted that children aged 0 to 59 months are the most impacted, although no deaths have been recorded so far.
Health officials are urging parents to promptly take any children with fever to the nearest health center for early diagnosis and treatment.
“Cases of measles are present throughout the province. It even resembles an epidemic,” Dr. Sumba warned. “However, we are awaiting an official declaration by the competent authority, namely the provincial governor. Some cases have already been confirmed by laboratory tests at the national level, and we have exceeded the alert thresholds.”
According to Dr. Sumba, the province is preparing to roll out a measles response plan, while also expressing concern over vaccine hesitancy among some parents, which could complicate containment efforts.
“At present, patients are being treated in the various health facilities where they are received. Our intervention plan is already operational,” he said. “In the meantime, targeted and small-scale vaccination campaigns are being organized in certain areas to prevent rapid spread of the disease.”
Health authorities continue to monitor the situation closely as preventive measures are intensified across the province.

title: Insecurity Paralyzes Schools in Masisi I During First Term
excerpt: Masisi, North Kivu, January 3, 2026 - Several schools in the Masisi I subdivision of North Kivu faced serious operational disruptions during the first term of the 2025-2026 school year, as persistent insecurity severely affected teaching and learning conditions. While some school
title_en: Insecurity Paralyzes Schools in Masisi I During First Term
excerpt_en: Masisi, North Kivu, January 3, 2026 - Several schools in the Masisi I subdivision of North Kivu faced serious operational disruptions during the first term of the 2025-2026 school year, as persistent insecurity severely affected teaching and learning conditions. While some school
body_en:
Masisi, North Kivu, January 3, 2026 - Several schools in the Masisi I subdivision of North Kivu faced serious operational disruptions during the first term of the 2025-2026 school year, as persistent insecurity severely affected teaching and learning conditions.
While some schools managed to relocate in order to continue their activities, others saw their operations completely paralyzed. Luc Nyamulinduka, head of the Masisi I subdivision of the Ministry of Primary, Secondary, and Technical Education (EPST), paid tribute to the resilience and courage of both students and teachers amid the ongoing violence.
“Having to interrupt classes at the slightest sound of gunfire, or even move entire schools in an attempt to continue activities elsewhere-this has been the ordeal faced by students in Masisi during this first term,” he said.
According to Nyamulinduka, several schools located along the Buabo road were transferred to Masisi-Centre, a relatively safer area, where they were able to complete the term without major difficulties.
However, the situation remained precarious in other localities. In Nyabiondo, classes were repeatedly interrupted by gunfire, forcing schools to suspend and later resume activities. Along the Burora road, disruptions were more severe: although classes initially started, they could not be completed due to ongoing insecurity.
The education official indicated that in areas where calm has returned, particularly in Buabo, schools are expected to resume classes in their usual locations. He also announced the deployment of school inspectors to assist teachers in recovering lost learning time.
Despite these measures, families continue to hope for a lasting return to peace, which remains the only guarantee of a normal school year. The head of the subdivision expressed concern over the incomplete school calendar and the mass displacement of students caused by the fighting, warning of its long-term impact on education in the region.

title: DRC Government Confirms Suspension of Military Spokesman Over Discriminatory Remarks
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - December 28, 2025 The government of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has confirmed the temporary suspension of the national military spokesman, Major General Sylvain Ekenge Bomusa, following remarks deemed discriminatory against Congolese Tutsi. According to
title_en: DRC Government Confirms Suspension of Military Spokesman Over Discriminatory Remarks
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - December 28, 2025 The government of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has confirmed the temporary suspension of the national military spokesman, Major General Sylvain Ekenge Bomusa, following remarks deemed discriminatory against Congolese Tutsi. According to
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - December 28, 2025
The government of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has confirmed the temporary suspension of the national military spokesman, Major General Sylvain Ekenge Bomusa, following remarks deemed discriminatory against Congolese Tutsi.
According to official sources, the suspension order was signed on December 28, 2025, by the Chief of Staff of the Armed Forces of the DRC (FARDC), Lieutenant General Jules Banza Mwilambwe.
The decision follows comments made by Maj Gen Ekenge on December 27 during a broadcast on state television (RTNC), in which he stated that marrying a Tutsi woman required caution, alleging that interethnic marriages would not result in children. The remarks sparked strong reactions within the country and beyond.
The incident occurred amid accusations that the DRC authorities tolerate or support hate speech targeting Tutsi communities, particularly in the eastern provinces, where atrocities have been reported.
In announcing the suspension, Lt Gen Mwilambwe stated that the comments were not aligned with the values of the national army or state policy. However, critics have questioned the sincerity of this position.
Fanny Kaj Kayemb, a senior finance official within the AFC/M23 alliance, argued that the punishment was symbolic and that the remarks reflected a broader command policy.“The military spokesman does not speak on his own,” Kayemb said. “He follows the line approved by the high command. In the DRC, the Commander-in-Chief is President Félix Tshisekedi.”
Kayemb further described the suspension as an attempt to mislead public opinion and the international community, asserting that the remarks were consistent with what he called a discriminatory political orientation.
Observers also point to past cases, notably statements by MP Justin Bitakwira, who publicly targeted Tutsi, especially Banyamulenge, without facing domestic sanctions, despite being sanctioned by the European Union in 2022.
Additionally, on December 22, 2025, President Félix Tshisekedi received two Congolese nationals living in the United States, including Jean-Claude Mubenga, who has previously made violent statements against Tutsi. The meeting reportedly focused on national unity, drawing further criticism from human rights observers.
According to several sources, verbal attacks against Congolese Tutsi have coincided with airstrikes and drone attacks targeting areas inhabited by Banyamulenge communities since early 2025, raising concerns about ethnic targeting and escalating tensions.

title: Djihad and Co-Defendants Appeal for Provisional Release Before Nyarugenge High Court
excerpt: Kigali, Rwanda - December 29, 2025 The Nyarugenge High Court on Monday heard an appeal filed by Uzabakiriho Cyprien, known as Djihad, and his co-defendants, who are seeking provisional release after being placed in pretrial detention by the Kicukiro Primary Court. The appeal foll
title_en: Djihad and Co-Defendants Appeal for Provisional Release Before Nyarugenge High Court
excerpt_en: Kigali, Rwanda - December 29, 2025 The Nyarugenge High Court on Monday heard an appeal filed by Uzabakiriho Cyprien, known as Djihad, and his co-defendants, who are seeking provisional release after being placed in pretrial detention by the Kicukiro Primary Court. The appeal foll
body_en:
Kigali, Rwanda - December 29, 2025
The Nyarugenge High Court on Monday heard an appeal filed by Uzabakiriho Cyprien, known as Djihad, and his co-defendants, who are seeking provisional release after being placed in pretrial detention by the Kicukiro Primary Court.
The appeal follows the defendants’ dissatisfaction with a decision ordering the temporary detention of Uzabakiriho Cyprien (Djihad), Ishimwe Patrick (Pazzo Man), Ishimwe François Xavier, and Kwizera Nestor (Pappy Nesta).
The four men are charged with distributing explicit videos allegedly showing Yampano engaged in sexual activity with his girlfriend.
During the hearing, all defendants argued that the Kicukiro Primary Court failed to properly consider their defense arguments. Djihad told the court he was dissatisfied that his explanations were dismissed, insisting that no video had ever been shared by him.
He specifically rejected the prosecution’s claim that he posted the videos on his WhatsApp status, arguing that the screenshots presented did not clearly demonstrate that the content originated from his phone number. He further suggested that the prosecution may have confused him with another individual using the same name.
Djihad’s lawyer emphasized that the lower court ignored elements favorable to his client, including the possibility of release on bail, and formally requested the High Court to grant provisional freedom.
Ishimwe François Xavier, who represented himself, also criticized the pretrial detention order, stating that he had demonstrated he was not responsible for distributing the videos. Similar arguments were presented by Ishimwe Patrick (Pazzo Man), who said his detention resulted from the court’s failure to adequately assess his defense.
All defendants, including Kwizera Nestor (Pappy Nesta), requested to be released and prosecuted without detention, stressing that the 30-day detention ordered by the lower court was unjustified.
The prosecution, present at the hearing, defended the decision of the Kicukiro Primary Court, describing it as transparent and lawful, and asked the Nyarugenge High Court to uphold the detention while investigations continue. Prosecutors added that other suspects linked to the alleged distribution of the videos have also been arrested.
After hearing both sides, the presiding judge announced that the court’s ruling on the appeal will be delivered on January 5, 2026.

title: RTNC Suspends Journalist Who Hosted Controversial Interview With Gen. Maj. Ekenge
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - December 29, 2025 The Radio-Télévision Nationale Congolaise (RTNC) has suspended journalist Joseph Oscar Mbal Kahij following the broadcast of remarks deemed discriminatory toward the Tutsi ethnic group during a live program on the state-run television channel. In
title_en: RTNC Suspends Journalist Who Hosted Controversial Interview With Gen. Maj. Ekenge
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - December 29, 2025 The Radio-Télévision Nationale Congolaise (RTNC) has suspended journalist Joseph Oscar Mbal Kahij following the broadcast of remarks deemed discriminatory toward the Tutsi ethnic group during a live program on the state-run television channel. In
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - December 29, 2025
The Radio-Télévision Nationale Congolaise (RTNC) has suspended journalist Joseph Oscar Mbal Kahij following the broadcast of remarks deemed discriminatory toward the Tutsi ethnic group during a live program on the state-run television channel.
In a statement released on December 29, 2025, the RTNC executive board announced that “the head of broadcasting on the television, Oscar Mbal Kahij, has been suspended from his duties for allowing the airing of statements targeting the Tutsi ethnic group by the FARDC Spokesperson, Gen. Sylvain Ekenge Efomi.”
Mbal Kahij hosted Gen. Maj. Sylvain Ekenge on December 27 during the program “Plateau Spécial”, which was initially intended to address the security situation in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, particularly in areas affected by fighting in South Kivu Province.
However, according to RTNC’s internal assessment, the discussion deviated from its stated purpose. Instead of focusing on military developments, the exchange included repeated remarks targeting Rwandans and Congolese Tutsis.
During the broadcast, Gen. Maj. Ekenge made controversial statements, including comments suggesting that marrying a Tutsi woman (Umutsikazi) requires caution, alleging that they refuse to have children with people from other ethnic groups. These remarks sparked widespread criticism both nationally and internationally.
On December 28, the Chief of the General Staff of the FARDC, Lt. Gen. Jules Banza Mwilambwe, announced the temporary suspension of Gen. Maj. Ekenge, citing that his statements were incompatible with military ethics and national policy, following intense public pressure.
Observers and human rights advocates argue that the incident reflects the growing level of ethnic hatred directed at Congolese Tutsis, despite the DRC government’s longstanding position that all citizens are equal before the law.
The suspensions of both the military spokesman and the journalist mark a rare acknowledgment by state institutions of responsibility in the handling of hate speech on public media, though critics continue to question the depth and sincerity of these measures.

Observers and human rights advocates argue that the incident reflects the growing level of ethnic hatred directed at Congolese Tutsis, despite the DRC government’s longstanding position that all citizens are equal before the law.
The suspensions of both the military spokesman and the journalist mark a rare acknowledgment by state institutions of responsibility in the handling of hate speech on public media, though critics continue to question the depth and sincerity of these measures.

title: Court of Cassation Seeks Authorization to Prosecute Tshopo Governor
excerpt: Kisangani, January 5, 2026 - The Court of Cassation has formally requested authorization from the Tshopo Provincial Assembly to initiate legal proceedings against Governor Paulin Lendongolia, who faces allegations of embezzlement of public funds. The request, submitted to the Ass
title_en: Court of Cassation Seeks Authorization to Prosecute Tshopo Governor
excerpt_en: Kisangani, January 5, 2026 - The Court of Cassation has formally requested authorization from the Tshopo Provincial Assembly to initiate legal proceedings against Governor Paulin Lendongolia, who faces allegations of embezzlement of public funds. The request, submitted to the Ass
body_en:
Kisangani, January 5, 2026 - The Court of Cassation has formally requested authorization from the Tshopo Provincial Assembly to initiate legal proceedings against Governor Paulin Lendongolia, who faces allegations of embezzlement of public funds.
The request, submitted to the Assembly’s bureau, seeks permission to bring the governor to trial. The bureau committed to examining the petition in accordance with its internal regulations, a decision adopted during a meeting held on Saturday, January 3, 2026.
During the same meeting, the bureau also discussed the unjustified absence of several provincial deputies from plenary sessions in September 2025, as well as the governor’s recent reinstatement following a ruling by the Constitutional Court.
Speaking after the meeting, Paul Lokesa, rapporteur of the Provincial Assembly, expressed regret over the handling of the case. He noted that, unlike the opposing party, which appeared to have been properly informed, the Assembly was only officially notified of the case’s inclusion on the court docket after the governor’s reinstatement.
An examination of the Attorney General’s indictment revealed a procedural irregularity during the vote to remove the governor: 10 deputies voted in favor of impeachment instead of the required 18. However, according to the bureau, this flaw does not affect the substance of the allegations against Paulin Lendongolia.
“This error does not alter the facts of the case,” Paul Lokesa said. “In accordance with the internal regulations, the bureau will hear from the Attorney General or his representative, as well as from Paulin Lendongolia himself, in order to assess the merits of the allegations and decide whether or not to authorize a judicial investigation.”
Governor Reinstated
Governor Paulin Lendongolia returned to Kisangani on Sunday, January 4, after nearly two months in Kinshasa, and officially resumed his duties following the Constitutional Court’s ruling of November 26. He had been removed from office on October 27 through a vote of no confidence linked to allegations of misappropriation of public funds.
Upon his arrival at Bangoka International Airport, the governor called on all political actors to work together for the development of Tshopo province, amid a political climate still marked by legal and institutional tensions.

title: Two Police Officers Convicted for the Murder of Dr. Emmanuel Nawej in Kolwezi
excerpt: Kolwezi, Lualaba Province, January 5, 2026 - Two officers of the Congolese National Police (PNC) have been convicted for the murder of Dr. Emmanuel Dibu Nawej, who died in police custody in Kolwezi, the capital of Lualaba province. The verdict was delivered last weekend following
title_en: Two Police Officers Convicted for the Murder of Dr. Emmanuel Nawej in Kolwezi
excerpt_en: Kolwezi, Lualaba Province, January 5, 2026 - Two officers of the Congolese National Police (PNC) have been convicted for the murder of Dr. Emmanuel Dibu Nawej, who died in police custody in Kolwezi, the capital of Lualaba province. The verdict was delivered last weekend following
body_en:
Kolwezi, Lualaba Province, January 5, 2026 - Two officers of the Congolese National Police (PNC) have been convicted for the murder of Dr. Emmanuel Dibu Nawej, who died in police custody in Kolwezi, the capital of Lualaba province. The verdict was delivered last weekend following several public hearings.
In total, five defendants-including four police officers and one civilian-were prosecuted on charges of violations of individual rights and freedoms and acts of torture. At the end of the trial, two police officers were found guilty.
Benathar Christian Mwisange was sentenced to 24 months of forced labor, while Virginie Mujinga Kadima received a 12-month sentence. The court also ordered the two convicts to pay the civil party damages equivalent to 25,000 US dollars, in Congolese francs.
The three remaining defendants, including two police officers and one civilian, were acquitted due to insufficient evidence.
In addition, the court ordered the burial of Dr. Emmanuel Nawej, nearly two months after his death, and the release of his remains to his family.
Background
Dr. Emmanuel Dibu Nawej died during the night of November 9-10, 2025, while being held in a cell at the Kolwezi Operations Coordination Center. He had been arrested following a minor traffic incident, in which his vehicle reportedly grazed that of a police officer near a supermarket.
His death sparked public outrage, with witnesses and the provincial coordinator of the National Human Rights Commission (CNDH), Arthur Kabulo, describing the circumstances as highly suspicious and calling for a thorough and transparent investigation.
On November 11, dozens of doctors took to the streets of Kolwezi to protest Dr. Nawej’s death, demanding justice and the prosecution of those responsible.

title: APUKIN Suspends Classes Following Assassination of Professor Abata
excerpt: Kinshasa, January 9, 2026 - The Association of Professors of the University of Kinshasa (APUKIN) has suspended all academic activities until Wednesday, January 14, following the assassination of Professor Matthieu Abata. The decision was made during an extraordinary general assem
title_en: APUKIN Suspends Classes Following Assassination of Professor Abata
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, January 9, 2026 - The Association of Professors of the University of Kinshasa (APUKIN) has suspended all academic activities until Wednesday, January 14, following the assassination of Professor Matthieu Abata. The decision was made during an extraordinary general assem
body_en:
Kinshasa, January 9, 2026 - The Association of Professors of the University of Kinshasa (APUKIN) has suspended all academic activities until Wednesday, January 14, following the assassination of Professor Matthieu Abata. The decision was made during an extraordinary general assembly held on Friday, January 9, at APUKIN headquarters.
The association also announced plans for a sit-in on Monday, January 12, in front of the Ministry of the Interior and Security to demand enhanced protection for faculty and researchers.
David Lubo, President of APUKIN, declared: “No activities will take place on university campuses. We will meet again on Wednesday to assess the situation. APUKIN and allied institutions have decided to organize a sit-in this Monday, January 12, 2026, in front of the offices of the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of the Interior.”
Professor Matthieu Abata was shot dead by armed bandits on Thursday, January 8, during a nighttime raid on his home in the Plateau des Professeurs neighborhood of Lemba, Kinshasa.
APUKIN is calling on the government to cover funeral expenses and ensure the well-being of his widow and children, highlighting the urgent need for better security measures for university staff.

title: FARDC Accuses Close Associates of President Tshisekedi of Leading Mobondo Armed Group
excerpt: Kinshasa / Kwilu, DRC - December 28, 2025 The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have accused individuals close to President Félix Tshisekedi of leading the Mobondo armed group, which has destabilized western parts of the country for nearly three years. The
title_en: FARDC Accuses Close Associates of President Tshisekedi of Leading Mobondo Armed Group
excerpt_en: Kinshasa / Kwilu, DRC - December 28, 2025 The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have accused individuals close to President Félix Tshisekedi of leading the Mobondo armed group, which has destabilized western parts of the country for nearly three years. The
body_en:
Kinshasa / Kwilu, DRC - December 28, 2025
The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have accused individuals close to President Félix Tshisekedi of leading the Mobondo armed group, which has destabilized western parts of the country for nearly three years.
The allegations were made by Captain Anthony Mwalushay, spokesman for military operations in provinces including Kwilu, during a press briefing on December 28, 2025, following weekend clashes in which five FARDC soldiers were killed.
According to Capt. Mwalushay, some individuals who publicly claim allegiance to President Tshisekedi are allegedly involved in commanding Mobondo fighters, while others are said to be collaborating with armed groups operating in eastern DRC.
“We have information about some who are working with armed groups in the east,” Mwalushay said. “For Mobondo, the problem is that many of those who support it are often seen behind the President of the Republic. During the day they appear harmless, but at night they lead Mobondo.”
The FARDC spokesperson stated that during the recent fighting, 15 Mobondo fighters were killed, and several others were arrested. He added that some detainees allegedly identified political and institutional figures as being linked to the group.
“Our institutions are investigating before releasing names,” Mwalushay said. “If Kinshasa supports those who are secretly behind Mobondo for political reasons, we soldiers will continue to do our job with weapons.”
The Mobondo movement, largely composed of members of the Yaka ethnic group, emerged in June 2022, initially targeting the FARDC and the Teke community, primarily over land disputes.
Since then, Mobondo attacks have severely affected security in rural areas surrounding Kinshasa and in neighboring provinces, including Mai-Ndombe, Kwilu, Kongo Central, and Kwango, resulting in thousands of deaths and widespread displacement.
In recent months, Mobondo fighters have reportedly attempted to expand their operations into peri-urban areas of Kinshasa, including Maluku and Kingakati. The government, however, says it has taken strong preventive measures to prevent further deterioration of security in the national capital.

title: FARDC Announces Recapture of Lwanga and Kigongo in South Kivu’s Uvira Territory
excerpt: Uvira, South Kivu | December 30, 2025 The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) announced on Tuesday that they have regained control of the localities of Lwanga and Kigongo in Uvira Territory, South Kivu Province, amid ongoing fighting in the region. According
title_en: FARDC Announces Recapture of Lwanga and Kigongo in South Kivu’s Uvira Territory
excerpt_en: Uvira, South Kivu | December 30, 2025 The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) announced on Tuesday that they have regained control of the localities of Lwanga and Kigongo in Uvira Territory, South Kivu Province, amid ongoing fighting in the region. According
body_en:
Uvira, South Kivu | December 30, 2025
The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) announced on Tuesday that they have regained control of the localities of Lwanga and Kigongo in Uvira Territory, South Kivu Province, amid ongoing fighting in the region.
According to Second Lieutenant Reagan Kalonji, spokesperson for Operation Sokola 2 South in South Kivu, the latest gains follow the recapture of Makobola 1 and Makobola 2 villages earlier this week.
He further stated that at least five armed M23 fighters surrendered to FARDC forces during the operations.
Despite the army’s announcement, local sources in Uvira reported the arrival of M23 reinforcements in the area beginning Tuesday, December 29, raising concerns about a possible escalation of clashes.
On Sunday, December 28, the national military spokesperson, Major General Sylvain Ekenge, confirmed that FARDC had retaken Makobola 1 and Makobola 2 in Fizi Territory, adding that fighting was still ongoing approximately seven kilometers from the town of Uvira.
The security situation in southern South Kivu remains volatile as FARDC continues operations against the M23 rebellion, with control over several strategic localities changing hands in recent days.

title: Tensions Rise in Tushunguti, Kalehe, After Killing Attributed to Wazalendo-Affiliated Fighter
excerpt: Kalehe Territory, South Kivu | December 30, 2025 Tensions remained high on Tuesday in the village of Tushunguti, located in the Ziralo group, Kalehe Territory, following the killing of a local resident allegedly carried out by an armed individual affiliated with the Wazalendo Kir
title_en: Tensions Rise in Tushunguti, Kalehe, After Killing Attributed to Wazalendo-Affiliated Fighter
excerpt_en: Kalehe Territory, South Kivu | December 30, 2025 Tensions remained high on Tuesday in the village of Tushunguti, located in the Ziralo group, Kalehe Territory, following the killing of a local resident allegedly carried out by an armed individual affiliated with the Wazalendo Kir
body_en:
Kalehe Territory, South Kivu | December 30, 2025
Tensions remained high on Tuesday in the village of Tushunguti, located in the Ziralo group, Kalehe Territory, following the killing of a local resident allegedly carried out by an armed individual affiliated with the Wazalendo Kirikicho group, according to local sources.
Early Tuesday morning, angry residents surrounded the residence of the Ziralo group chief, expressing frustration over what they described as persistent insecurity in the area. Demonstrators denounced the silence of the authorities in response to repeated abuses allegedly committed by armed men linked to the Wazalendo, particularly those from the Mai-Mai Kirikicho faction.
A civil society representative reported that these armed elements are frequently accused of theft, violence, and killings. He stated that the victim of Monday evening’s attack was a security guard assigned to protect a depot belonging to the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC).
According to the same source, following the murder, local residents pursued the suspected assailant, who was later killed during the chase. This account was confirmed by notable figures in the region.
Community leaders have since urged South Kivu provincial authorities to take urgent measures to curb the activities of armed groups operating in the area. They called for strict control of weapons and tighter oversight of fighters associated with the Mai-Mai Kirikicho group, warning that continued inaction could further destabilize the region.

body_en:
Rumonge, Burundi | December 2025
A total of 846 Congolese refugees residing in the Rumonge camp in Burundi received humanitarian aid, including food and non-food items, on Thursday. Most of the refugees originate from Uvira, while others fled from Fizi and Baraka, according to camp officials.
The aid, provided by private donors, is described by recipients as a lifeline amid difficult living conditions. Mapenzi Manyebwa, president of the Congolese refugees in Rumonge, expressed gratitude to the benefactors and called on the DRC government to emulate such support.
“We have been here in Rumonge for two weeks, after leaving the territories and cities of Uvira, Fizi, and Baraka. Here, we are starting to receive assistance from local associations and some national members of parliament,” Manyebwa said.
He specifically mentioned MP Justin Bitawira, who donated 140 bags of cornmeal, 1,740 kg of beans, 10 jerrycans of palm oil, 100 tarpaulins, and soap to the camp. The distribution reached 846 registered households, providing essential relief to the refugee population.
“We thank these leaders who continue to think about our difficulties, because we live in such challenging conditions here in Rumonge,” Manyebwa added.

excerpt_en: Rutshuru, North Kivu, DRC | December 28, 2025 The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have accused AFC/M23 rebels of abducting at least 42 women in the Bukombo Centre area of Rutshuru territory, North Kivu. According to Dieudonné Kasereka, communications offi
body_en:
Rutshuru, North Kivu, DRC | December 28, 2025
The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have accused AFC/M23 rebels of abducting at least 42 women in the Bukombo Centre area of Rutshuru territory, North Kivu.
According to Dieudonné Kasereka, communications officer for the 34th Military Region, the abductions occurred on Sunday, December 28, in the Bwito chiefdom. The army reports that the victims were tortured prior to their abduction, citing testimonies from local residents.
“The exact destination or whereabouts of the women remain unclear,” Kasereka added.
The FARDC noted that this is not the first violent act attributed to the AFC/M23 rebels, who have previously targeted civilians in Mushoro (Bwito chiefdom), Pitango and Musinde (Batangi chiefdom), and Kahongole (Katsiru locality).
The Bukombo area remains a high-risk zone, marked by skirmishes between Wazalendo forces of the CMC group and M23 rebels, alongside human rights violations against civilians.
Mass Displacement
Hundreds of families displaced by the clashes are currently living in Mweso, in the Bashali Mokoto area, Masisi territory. According to local sources, these people are housed in schools and churches under precarious conditions, receiving little to no humanitarian aid.
Displaced families are forced to move their belongings each morning to allow classes to resume, often in the rain. This situation is especially dangerous for breastfeeding women and children, who are exposed to the elements.
Local residents are appealing to the humanitarian community for decent shelter and support to enable them to return safely to their home villages.
