title: Police Commander Lynched by Angry Youths in Ilebo, Kasai Province
excerpt: Ilebo, DRC - January 1, 2026 A police commander was brutally killed by angry youths at the Lumbundi camp in the Ilebo territory of Kasai province on Thursday, January 1. The victim, Commander Djuma of the Mapangu police station, was reportedly beaten to death after being accused
title_en: Police Commander Lynched by Angry Youths in Ilebo, Kasai Province
excerpt_en: Ilebo, DRC - January 1, 2026 A police commander was brutally killed by angry youths at the Lumbundi camp in the Ilebo territory of Kasai province on Thursday, January 1. The victim, Commander Djuma of the Mapangu police station, was reportedly beaten to death after being accused
body_en:
Ilebo, DRC - January 1, 2026
A police commander was brutally killed by angry youths at the Lumbundi camp in the Ilebo territory of Kasai province on Thursday, January 1. The victim, Commander Djuma of the Mapangu police station, was reportedly beaten to death after being accused of assaulting a woman in police custody, according to local sources.
Eyewitnesses say the incident began when a woman was arrested and allegedly assaulted by Commander Djuma. In response, a group of youths from the Lumbundi camp intervened, violently attacking the commander.
Following the lynching, the Mapangu police station, with support from the Masongo police station, rushed to the scene to investigate and attempt to restore calm. However, residents of the camp fled into the surrounding bush, fearing reprisals.
Authorities have confirmed that Commander Djuma’s body has been buried in the center of Mapangu. One young man implicated in the attack has already been detained by police.
In the wake of the tragedy, François Malepo, coordinator of the New Civil Society of the Ilebo territory, called on judicial authorities to conduct a thorough investigation. He urged that all individuals responsible for the murder be arrested and prosecuted, emphasizing the need for accountability.
Malepo also denounced acts of looting reportedly committed by some security forces during their intervention at the Lumbundi camp, highlighting concerns over law enforcement conduct in the area.
This incident underscores the growing tensions and challenges facing law enforcement in Kasai province, where community-police relations remain fragile and allegations of abuse can quickly escalate into deadly confrontations.

title: FARDC Honors Colonel Mamadou Ndala, 12 Years After His Assassination
excerpt: Kinshasa/North Kivu, DRC - January 2, 2026 The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) paid tribute on January 2 to Colonel Mamadou Ndala, twelve years after he was assassinated in an ambush while traveling to Eringeti in North Kivu. On this solemn day of remembr
title_en: FARDC Honors Colonel Mamadou Ndala, 12 Years After His Assassination
excerpt_en: Kinshasa/North Kivu, DRC - January 2, 2026 The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) paid tribute on January 2 to Colonel Mamadou Ndala, twelve years after he was assassinated in an ambush while traveling to Eringeti in North Kivu. On this solemn day of remembr
body_en:
Kinshasa/North Kivu, DRC - January 2, 2026
The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) paid tribute on January 2 to Colonel Mamadou Ndala, twelve years after he was assassinated in an ambush while traveling to Eringeti in North Kivu.
On this solemn day of remembrance, the FARDC reaffirmed its determination to continue the fight for which Colonel Ndala sacrificed his life: building a united, sovereign, and peaceful Democratic Republic of Congo.
“Honor and glory to General Mamadou Ndala. The grateful nation will never forget you. Long live the FARDC, long live the Democratic Republic of Congo!” the FARDC wrote on its official account.
At the time of his death, Colonel Ndala was leading military operations against the Ugandan Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) and other armed groups active in the Beni region. His courage, loyalty, and strategic leadership earned him the status of a national hero and an emblematic figure of supreme sacrifice in defense of the homeland.
The FARDC highlighted his enduring legacy:
Leadership on the ground, closely engaging with troops.
Unwavering commitment to peace, security, and territorial integrity.
Determination in the face of the enemy, inspiring generations of Congolese soldiers.
“His legacy remains alive in the hearts of Congolese soldiers and the entire nation,” the army concluded, paying homage to a commander whose life exemplified heroism and dedication.
This 12th anniversary commemoration comes as the Congolese army continues to face ongoing clashes with AFC/M23 rebels, who are reportedly supported by the Rwandan army in eastern DRC.

title: Tragedy in Ango: Two Killed by Police Officer on New Year’s Day
excerpt: Ango, Tshopo Province, DRC - January 1, 2026 A police officer shot and killed two people in the Ango territory on New Year’s Day, plunging the community into shock and grief. Ango is located approximately 500 km north of Kisangani. According to local sources, the victims were cel
title_en: Tragedy in Ango: Two Killed by Police Officer on New Year’s Day
excerpt_en: Ango, Tshopo Province, DRC - January 1, 2026 A police officer shot and killed two people in the Ango territory on New Year’s Day, plunging the community into shock and grief. Ango is located approximately 500 km north of Kisangani. According to local sources, the victims were cel
body_en:
Ango, Tshopo Province, DRC - January 1, 2026
A police officer shot and killed two people in the Ango territory on New Year’s Day, plunging the community into shock and grief. Ango is located approximately 500 km north of Kisangani.
According to local sources, the victims were celebrating the arrival of the new year at a bar in the Ango shopping center when an altercation broke out. Around 8:00 PM, a police jeep arrived at high speed, and two officers disembarked, ordering the crowd to disperse. Moments later, one officer fired point-blank, killing two individuals.
The incident has sparked outrage among residents and local authorities. The interim administrator of Ango territory condemned the use of live ammunition against civilians, urging the police hierarchy to take swift action.
“What I deplore is that the police officers fired live ammunition at the population. I hope, through my report to the governor, that their superiors will authorize their arrest. This would be a good thing, because it is the very wish of the population: that peace reign here above all else,” the administrator stated.
The Vice-President of the Tshopo Provincial Assembly, Antoine Gambolipay, who represents Ango, echoed this call, demanding that both officers be apprehended and brought to justice.
Authorities report that one officer remains at large, while the other is in custody at his camp. Investigations are ongoing as the community awaits accountability.

title: North Kivu: M23 Rebels Launch Offensive to Retake Katoyi
excerpt: Masisi, North Kivu, DRC - January 2, 2026 AFC/M23 rebels launched an offensive early Friday morning in an attempt to regain control of the town of Katoyi, the main town of the sector of the same name in Masisi territory. Local sources confirm that the rebels are seeking to reclai
title_en: North Kivu: M23 Rebels Launch Offensive to Retake Katoyi
excerpt_en: Masisi, North Kivu, DRC - January 2, 2026 AFC/M23 rebels launched an offensive early Friday morning in an attempt to regain control of the town of Katoyi, the main town of the sector of the same name in Masisi territory. Local sources confirm that the rebels are seeking to reclai
body_en:
Masisi, North Kivu, DRC - January 2, 2026
AFC/M23 rebels launched an offensive early Friday morning in an attempt to regain control of the town of Katoyi, the main town of the sector of the same name in Masisi territory. Local sources confirm that the rebels are seeking to reclaim territory they lost at the end of December 2025.
According to reports, the attack targets four positions held by fighters from the Congolese Patriotic Resistance Group (PARECO), an ally of the FARDC. Fighting is concentrated in the village of Kasheke (Nyamaboko 1 group, Osso Banyungu sector), located approximately 7 km from Katoyi town center.
Gunfire was also reported in surrounding villages, including Busurirwa (Ufamandu 1 group), Myole (Mufunyi Kibabi group, Bahunde chiefdom), and Muhairwa (Kibabi 2 group, Katoyi sector).
This marks the second attempt by M23 to retake Katoyi, following an earlier assault last Tuesday. On December 29, 2025, Wazalendo fighters from PARECO/Strike Force recaptured Katoyi and neighboring villages-including Mitimingi, Kahundu, Kasheke, and Kakoka-after intense clashes that left several dead on both sides and resulted in the capture of 28 M23 fighters and 12 weapons, according to military sources.
The town of Katoyi has switched hands multiple times since mid-November 2025, reflecting the ongoing volatility in the Masisi sector and the persistence of M23’s attempts to regain strategic control.

title: North Kivu: Deadly Attacks and Cattle Theft in Rutshuru Over Two Weeks
excerpt: Rutshuru, North Kivu, DRC - January 2, 2026 At least seven people have been killed and four others injured, including two children, in a series of violent incidents attributed to armed groups in Rutshuru territory over the past two weeks, according to local sources. In addition t
title_en: North Kivu: Deadly Attacks and Cattle Theft in Rutshuru Over Two Weeks
excerpt_en: Rutshuru, North Kivu, DRC - January 2, 2026 At least seven people have been killed and four others injured, including two children, in a series of violent incidents attributed to armed groups in Rutshuru territory over the past two weeks, according to local sources. In addition t
body_en:
Rutshuru, North Kivu, DRC - January 2, 2026
At least seven people have been killed and four others injured, including two children, in a series of violent incidents attributed to armed groups in Rutshuru territory over the past two weeks, according to local sources.
In addition to the human toll, over 100 cows were stolen during this period, highlighting the combined impact of violence and economic losses on local communities.
The attacks have been reported in at least seven localities north of the Bwito chiefdom, including the Lusoha-Mirangi road (Kanyabayonga group), Kibirizi-Kibingu road, and Kibirizi-Rwindi road (Mutanda group).
According to the program manager of SOCOLUT-DRC (Community Solidarity Against Tribalism in the DRC), the incidents include:
Kidnappings: three in Lusogha, three in Kyaghala.
Murders and gunshot injuries: in Birundule and along the Kibirizi-Rwindi road.
Cattle theft: 80 cows in Kilombo, 25 cows in Byanderema (Mirangi, Mutanda group).
Looting: two cases in Lusogha (Friday and Saturday nights), two cases on the Kibirizi-Rwindi road, and one on the Kibirizi-Kibingu road.
SOCOLUT-DRC calls for increased protection of civilians, who are routinely targeted during these atrocities, and urges humanitarian partners and peace actors to strengthen security and provide support to victims.
The affected areas, Kanyabayonga and Mutanda, are currently hosting over 20,000 displaced families, many of whom are directly impacted by these recent attacks.

title: Burundi: Congolese Refugees in Dire Conditions Following Uvira-Fizi Clashes
excerpt: Bujumbura, Burundi - January 2, 2026 A recent report highlights the extreme living conditions of Congolese refugees who fled the ongoing conflict between AFC/M23 rebels in the Uvira and Fizi territories of the DRC. Since arriving in Burundi on December 10, 2025, these refugees ha
title_en: Burundi: Congolese Refugees in Dire Conditions Following Uvira-Fizi Clashes
excerpt_en: Bujumbura, Burundi - January 2, 2026 A recent report highlights the extreme living conditions of Congolese refugees who fled the ongoing conflict between AFC/M23 rebels in the Uvira and Fizi territories of the DRC. Since arriving in Burundi on December 10, 2025, these refugees ha
body_en:
Bujumbura, Burundi - January 2, 2026
A recent report highlights the extreme living conditions of Congolese refugees who fled the ongoing conflict between AFC/M23 rebels in the Uvira and Fizi territories of the DRC.
Since arriving in Burundi on December 10, 2025, these refugees have been hosted in transit camps at Rugombo, Rumonge, and Gatumba, where they are enduring severe poverty and lack of basic necessities.
Mapenzi Manyebwa, a representative of the refugees, described the situation:
“In Gatumba, Congolese refugees spent the New Year in anguish, as most could not afford clothes or gifts for their children. We live in unsanitary conditions, and many lack food. It was in this suffering and stress that the majority of Congolese refugees spent the holidays.”
Despite the dire circumstances, Manyebwa expressed gratitude for the opportunity to begin a new year, even amidst hardship.
Aid has been minimal, limited to isolated individual interventions, leaving the majority of refugees without adequate support.
The UNHCR in Burundi is currently resettling refugees in Ruhigi province, approximately 60 km north of Bujumbura, in an effort to improve their living conditions.

title: DRC - Kinshasa: Over 460 Suspected Urban Gang Members Arrested During Operation Ndobo
excerpt: Kinshasa, January 1, 2026 Authorities in Kinshasa reported the arrest of approximately 464 suspected members of urban gangs, locally known as “kulunas”, during end-of-year festivities as part of Operation Ndobo. Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of the Interior and Security, Jac
title_en: DRC - Kinshasa: Over 460 Suspected Urban Gang Members Arrested During Operation Ndobo
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, January 1, 2026 Authorities in Kinshasa reported the arrest of approximately 464 suspected members of urban gangs, locally known as “kulunas”, during end-of-year festivities as part of Operation Ndobo. Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of the Interior and Security, Jac
body_en:
Kinshasa, January 1, 2026
Authorities in Kinshasa reported the arrest of approximately 464 suspected members of urban gangs, locally known as “kulunas”, during end-of-year festivities as part of Operation Ndobo.
Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of the Interior and Security, Jacquemain Shabani Lukoo, announced the figures following inspections of several police stations in the capital.
The breakdown of arrests across Kinshasa districts is as follows:
Masina (Tshangu): 242 arrests
Limete: 56 arrests
Kalamu: 51 arrests
Mont-Ngafula: 45 arrests
Gombe (Camp Lufungula): ~40 arrests
Kintambo: 30 arrests
Total: 464 individuals apprehended
Masina district recorded the highest number of arrests, nearly half of the total, highlighting the scale of gang-related activity in the area.
Operation Ndobo, currently active in 10 of the DRC’s 26 provinces, is part of ongoing efforts by the government to combat urban crime, protect citizens, and safeguard property across the country.
Authorities have emphasized that the operation will continue nationwide to maintain security and public order.

title: DRC Defense Minister Sets Reconquest of Occupied Territories as Top Priority for 2026
excerpt: Kinshasa | January 1, 2026 - The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defense, Guy Kabombo Muadiamvita, has declared the restoration of state authority across the national territory and the reconquest of currently occupied areas as his top priorities for 2026. In a New
title_en: DRC Defense Minister Sets Reconquest of Occupied Territories as Top Priority for 2026
excerpt_en: Kinshasa | January 1, 2026 - The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defense, Guy Kabombo Muadiamvita, has declared the restoration of state authority across the national territory and the reconquest of currently occupied areas as his top priorities for 2026. In a New
body_en:
Kinshasa | January 1, 2026 - The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defense, Guy Kabombo Muadiamvita, has declared the restoration of state authority across the national territory and the reconquest of currently occupied areas as his top priorities for 2026.
In a New Year message addressed to the nation, Kabombo underscored the determination of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) to defend national sovereignty and ensure the protection of civilians throughout the country.
He paid tribute to soldiers who have fallen in the line of duty, praising the FARDC’s continued commitment and loyalty to the national flag. “Darkness will not reign forever,” he said, expressing optimism that 2026 will be a year of hope and renewal for the Congolese people.
The Defense Minister reaffirmed his commitment to peace, security, and development, while calling on citizens to show solidarity, courage, and confidence in the future.
On December 31, a day earlier, Guy Kabombo Muadiamvita carried out a working visit to Kalemie, in Tanganyika Province, where he assessed the operational capacity of the FARDC, with particular attention to military infrastructure.
During the visit, he chaired a closed-door strategic meeting at the headquarters of the 22nd Naval Force Group, in the presence of the Deputy Chief of Staff in charge of Operations and Intelligence. Discussions focused on security challenges and operational issues facing the unit.
The visit concluded with an inspection of logistical and technical facilities, including maintenance and operational support structures, aimed at evaluating working conditions for military personnel and identifying priority needs to strengthen defense capabilities in the region.

body_en:
North Kivu, January 2, 2026 - AFC/M23 rebels launched a new offensive early Friday morning to regain control of the town of Katoyi, the main locality of the Katoyi sector, in Masisi territory, North Kivu, according to local sources.
The attack comes after the AFC/M23 lost Katoyi in late December 2025. Multiple sources indicate that the rebels are attempting to recapture the town, targeting four positions held by fighters of the Congolese Patriotic Resistance Group (PARECO), an ally of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (FARDC).
The fighting is mainly concentrated in the village of Kasheke, within the Nyamaboko 1 group, Osso Banyungu sector, located about seven kilometers from Katoyi’s town center.
However, gunfire was also reported in several surrounding localities, including Busurirwa (Ufamandu 1 group), Myole (Mufunyi Kibabi group, Bahunde chiefdom), and Muhairwa (Kibabi 2 group, Katoyi sector), highlighting the spread of clashes across the area.
On December 29, Wazalendo fighters from the PARECO/Strike Force regained control of Katoyi and neighboring villages-Mitimingi, Kahundu, Kasheke, and Kakoka-following intense fighting. According to military sources, the clashes resulted in several deaths on both sides, as well as the capture of 28 M23 fighters and 12 weapons.
The AFC/M23 had maintained control of the area since mid-November 2025. This latest assault marks the second attempt by the group to retake Katoyi, following an earlier, unsuccessful effort earlier in the week.

title: FARDC Presents Seven Rwandan Soldiers to the Press in Kinshasa
excerpt: Kinshasa, January 3, 2026 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (FARDC) on Saturday presented to the press seven Rwandan soldiers alongside eight civilians from neighboring countries, whom they say were captured during military operations in eastern Congo. Ac
title_en: FARDC Presents Seven Rwandan Soldiers to the Press in Kinshasa
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, January 3, 2026 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (FARDC) on Saturday presented to the press seven Rwandan soldiers alongside eight civilians from neighboring countries, whom they say were captured during military operations in eastern Congo. Ac
body_en:
Kinshasa, January 3, 2026 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (FARDC) on Saturday presented to the press seven Rwandan soldiers alongside eight civilians from neighboring countries, whom they say were captured during military operations in eastern Congo.
According to Lieutenant Colonel Mak Hazukay, Deputy Commander of the FARDC’s Command and Information Service, the arrest of these individuals provides clear evidence of the presence of the Rwandan army on Congolese territory. He strongly criticized what he described as Kigali’s continued and deliberate violation of the Washington Agreement and United Nations Security Council Resolution 2773.
Lieutenant Colonel Mak Hazukay specified that the suspects were apprehended far from the border areas, during operations conducted in North Kivu and South Kivu, undermining claims that Rwanda’s actions are defensive in nature.
“Since the beginning of this war, the DRC has consistently maintained, with supporting evidence, that it is under attack by Rwanda,” he stated. “The FARDC presented seven Rwandan soldiers and eight civilians, nationals of countries in the sub-region, captured during military operations in North and South Kivu. The current occupation of Uvira, located far from the borders, proves that the justification invoked by Kigali is a blatant lie,” he added.
The FARDC official further accused the Kigali regime of manipulating nationals from countries in the sub-region, as well as collaborating with other armed groups, including RED Tabala, in an effort to regionalize the armed conflict.
The presentation of these captives comes amid a renewed security escalation in eastern DRC, as AFC/M23 rebels have launched an offensive to retake control of Katoyi, the main town of the Katoyi sector in Masisi territory, North Kivu.

title: Over 2,000 Displaced People Struggle to Survive at Katanika Site
excerpt: Kalemie, Tanganyika Province, January 3, 2026 - More than 2,000 displaced people, who fled the conflict involving the AFC and M23 in North and South Kivu, are living in extremely precarious conditions at the Katanika displacement site in the city of Kalemie, according to local so
title_en: Over 2,000 Displaced People Struggle to Survive at Katanika Site
excerpt_en: Kalemie, Tanganyika Province, January 3, 2026 - More than 2,000 displaced people, who fled the conflict involving the AFC and M23 in North and South Kivu, are living in extremely precarious conditions at the Katanika displacement site in the city of Kalemie, according to local so
body_en:
Kalemie, Tanganyika Province, January 3, 2026 - More than 2,000 displaced people, who fled the conflict involving the AFC and M23 in North and South Kivu, are living in extremely precarious conditions at the Katanika displacement site in the city of Kalemie, according to local sources.
The displaced families reportedly lack access to medical care, clean water, and other basic necessities, prompting the site management to issue an urgent appeal for humanitarian assistance.
“There is no medical center or pharmacy at the site,” the site manager said. “These displaced people, whose total number is estimated at more than 11,000, are living in very poor shelter conditions, particularly during the rainy season, and are also facing severe shortages of water and food.”
According to the site management, displaced persons who fall ill are often forced to cope on their own, as access to healthcare remains extremely limited. Those who seek treatment at the Kifungo hospital are reportedly turned away, further worsening the humanitarian situation.
One displaced woman described the daily hardships faced by families at the site. “I have seven children. There is no pharmacy or hospital here. We receive no assistance. Malaria is widespread among the displaced. We have neither mosquito nets nor proper shelter. If someone of goodwill could help us…” she said.
The displaced people began settling at the Katanika site in February 2025. According to the site’s leadership, a humanitarian organization has provided tarpaulins and limited financial assistance, but these efforts remain insufficient to meet the growing needs of the population.
As conditions continue to deteriorate, calls are mounting for a scaled-up humanitarian response to prevent further suffering among the displaced communities in Kalemie.

title: Police Officers’ Homes Set Ablaze by Angry Youths in Ango
excerpt: Ango, Bas-Uele Province, January 3, 2026 - Tensions escalated in Ango territory, Bas-Uele province, after the burial of two victims of police violence, leading to acts of retaliation by angry youths who set fire to dozens of homes belonging to police officers. According to local
title_en: Police Officers’ Homes Set Ablaze by Angry Youths in Ango
excerpt_en: Ango, Bas-Uele Province, January 3, 2026 - Tensions escalated in Ango territory, Bas-Uele province, after the burial of two victims of police violence, leading to acts of retaliation by angry youths who set fire to dozens of homes belonging to police officers. According to local
body_en:
Ango, Bas-Uele Province, January 3, 2026 - Tensions escalated in Ango territory, Bas-Uele province, after the burial of two victims of police violence, leading to acts of retaliation by angry youths who set fire to dozens of homes belonging to police officers.
According to local authorities, 38 houses owned by police officers were burned down in one of Ango’s two neighborhoods, following the funerals of the victims, who were shot and killed by police on New Year’s Eve.
After an emergency meeting convened on Saturday, January 3, 2026, the Deputy Territorial Administrator, Alfred Kipa, announced that measures had been taken to prevent a recurrence of such violence.
Calm reportedly returned to the area after the funerals, which the deputy administrator described as dignified. He also confirmed that financial assistance was provided to the bereaved families, following his intervention with the provincial governor.
Despite this, Alfred Kipa strongly condemned the destruction caused by what he described as unemployed youths, noting that nearly all police housing in the affected area had been targeted, including the residence of the group leader.
“Five houses were burned down, including that of the leader, as well as others belonging to police officers who were absent,” he said. “We have decided to reinforce patrols to put an end to these barbaric acts carried out by a handful of unemployed youths.”
Left without shelter, the affected police officers have taken refuge in a building previously donated to the territorial administration by an NGO. Authorities have pledged to allocate land to enable them to rebuild their homes.
The unrest follows the fatal shooting of two civilians by police on the evening of January 1, as residents were celebrating the New Year, an incident that has deeply shaken the local community.

title: Bandits Terrorize Kinzau-Mvuete After Period of Calm
excerpt: Kinzau-Mvuete, Kongo-Central Province, January 3, 2026 - A wave of criminal attacks has shaken the town of Kinzau-Mvuete, in Sekebanza territory, Kongo-Central province, after several homes and businesses were targeted by bandits locally known as “Kulunas.” According to police so
title_en: Bandits Terrorize Kinzau-Mvuete After Period of Calm
excerpt_en: Kinzau-Mvuete, Kongo-Central Province, January 3, 2026 - A wave of criminal attacks has shaken the town of Kinzau-Mvuete, in Sekebanza territory, Kongo-Central province, after several homes and businesses were targeted by bandits locally known as “Kulunas.” According to police so
body_en:
Kinzau-Mvuete, Kongo-Central Province, January 3, 2026 - A wave of criminal attacks has shaken the town of Kinzau-Mvuete, in Sekebanza territory, Kongo-Central province, after several homes and businesses were targeted by bandits locally known as “Kulunas.”
According to police sources, the attacks occurred between December 31, 2025, and the evening of Friday, January 3, 2026, spreading fear and panic among the local population. The assailants reportedly looted valuables and cash, leaving several victims injured.
Sylvain Bakulu, Police Commander of Kinzau-Mvuete, confirmed the incidents and called on the population to cooperate with the police in order to facilitate the arrest of the perpetrators.
Victims reported that the masked and armed attackers operated in groups during the night of December 31 to January 1, mainly targeting the Mobutu and Mbenza Thubi neighborhoods. According to testimonies, the assailants threatened residents with death before ransacking their homes.
In total, around fifteen houses were attacked, and several people were seriously injured, some suffering machete wounds during the assaults.
The police commander noted that the attacks came after a long period of relative calm in the area. He attributed the resurgence of violence to the recent release of several suspected bandits by the prosecutor’s office of the Kinzau-Mvuete Court of First Instance, citing a lack of formal complaints as the reason for their release.
Security forces say investigations are ongoing as authorities seek to restore order and safety in the town.

body_en:
Bujumbura, January 5, 2026 - The Burundian government has begun transferring thousands of Congolese refugees from the Rumonge and Gatumba camps to the Ruhigi refugee camp, located about 60 kilometers north of Bujumbura, according to humanitarian sources.
The displaced Congolese, who fled fighting involving the AFC/M23 in South Kivu, had been living in extremely precarious conditions in the Rumonge and Gatumba camps, where they reportedly survived without sufficient humanitarian assistance.
Authorities said the relocation aims to move the refugees away from the Congolese border, citing security and logistical considerations.
However, conditions at the Ruhigi camp have also drawn concern. Refugees report facing harsh weather conditions and ongoing hardships, raising fears that the humanitarian situation may remain critical despite the transfer.
One refugee described the situation as difficult, underscoring the continued vulnerability of displaced Congolese populations seeking safety in neighboring Burundi.

excerpt_en: Bunia, Ituri, January 4, 2026 - On the occasion of National Independence Martyrs’ Day, observed annually on January 4 in honor of the independence heroes who fell in 1959, the 32nd Military Region of the Armed Forces of the DRC (FARDC) in Bunia issued a call for popular support t
body_en:
Bunia, Ituri, January 4, 2026 - On the occasion of National Independence Martyrs’ Day, observed annually on January 4 in honor of the independence heroes who fell in 1959, the 32nd Military Region of the Armed Forces of the DRC (FARDC) in Bunia issued a call for popular support to help end the ongoing conflicts in North Kivu and Ituri.
Military authorities emphasized that the current violence has claimed many lives, now recognized as martyrs, and urged citizens to contribute to the restoration of peace in the region.
Colonel Emmanuel Libandi, coordinator of the Armed Reserve for Defense and president of the organizing committee, highlighted security improvements over the past six months, particularly in the Djugu territory. He attributed this progress to a combination of military operations and dialogue with local communities, despite continuing threats from Thomas Lubanga’s CRP militia and the widespread proliferation of illegal weapons.
The FARDC reaffirmed its commitment to ongoing operations aimed at achieving lasting peace and called on all citizens to follow the example set by the martyrs in supporting peacebuilding efforts.
The commemoration brought together religious leaders, state representatives, and civil society actors, with plans underway to extend similar events to other territories within Ituri province.

Walungu, South Kivu, January 5, 2026 - At least four civilians were killed and several others wounded during clashes between Wazalendo fighters and AFC-M23 rebels in the Walungu territory of South Kivu.
The fighting, which began on Sunday and continued into Monday, January 5, 2026, affected the villages of Bumbalali, Mwendo, and Cirhavanyi.
Residents reported that several houses were damaged by bombs reportedly dropped by M23 forces, exacerbating the humanitarian impact. One local resident described experiencing extremely difficult conditions over the past 48 hours, highlighting the heavy toll on civilians in the area.

title: ADF Stronghold Dismantled by Joint FARDC-UPDF Operation in Mambasa
excerpt: Mambasa, Ituri, January 5, 2026 - The Armed Forces of the DRC (FARDC), in cooperation with the Ugandan People’s Defence Force (UPDF), dismantled an ADF rebel stronghold last week in Matolo-Kaseni, near the Ituri River. The joint operation was announced on Monday, January 5, durin
title_en: ADF Stronghold Dismantled by Joint FARDC-UPDF Operation in Mambasa
excerpt_en: Mambasa, Ituri, January 5, 2026 - The Armed Forces of the DRC (FARDC), in cooperation with the Ugandan People’s Defence Force (UPDF), dismantled an ADF rebel stronghold last week in Matolo-Kaseni, near the Ituri River. The joint operation was announced on Monday, January 5, durin
body_en:
Mambasa, Ituri, January 5, 2026 - The Armed Forces of the DRC (FARDC), in cooperation with the Ugandan People’s Defence Force (UPDF), dismantled an ADF rebel stronghold last week in Matolo-Kaseni, near the Ituri River. The joint operation was announced on Monday, January 5, during an evaluation meeting in the Babila Bakwanza chiefdom, Mambasa territory. Both forces pledged to continue and intensify operations against the ADF in other villages where the rebels are attempting to regroup and attack local communities.
According to military sources, the nighttime operation, conducted from December 29 to 30, targeted a major ADF stronghold on the border between the Mambasa and Irumu territories.
Provincial deputies and civil society representatives, who accompanied the military delegation to Elake to assess progress, welcomed the efforts but called for the establishment of military positions in Elake, Leta, and Sita Rudi to ensure that local populations can safely access their fields.
Officials in Mambasa also urged that the joint operations be extended westward to Lolwa and Menzimenzi, where ADF fighters are reportedly regrouping in preparation for new attacks.
These measures form part of a months-long collaboration between the FARDC and UPDF aimed at neutralizing ADF activity and protecting civilians in the region.

These measures form part of a months-long collaboration between the FARDC and UPDF aimed at neutralizing ADF activity and protecting civilians in the region.

body_en:
Irumu, Ituri, January 7, 2026 - Approximately 70% of residents who fled ADF (Allied Democratic Forces) attacks in recent months have returned to their villages along National Route 4, on the Komanda-Luna axis in the Irumu territory of Ituri province.
The latest wave of returnees, primarily from Eringeti, Oicha, Beni, and Butembo in North Kivu, arrived on Tuesday, January 6, in Ndalya and Otmaber, in the Walese Vonkutu chiefdom.
Local human rights activists credit the improved security situation, resulting from joint operations by the FARDC and the UPDF, for enabling this return. The rehabilitation of National Route 4 and increased military patrols have made movement safer. Christophe Munyanderu, an activist monitoring the situation, said:“People are returning by motorcycle or car. The reopening of the RN4 national highway and the easing of violence are facilitating their return, thanks to strengthened security measures.”
The return of displaced populations will allow residents to resume agricultural activities and strengthen their resilience following past crises. Joint security efforts are being praised for their role in stabilizing the area and enabling communities to rebuild their livelihoods.

title: Boat Shipwreck in Bolomba: At Least 6 Dead, Several Missing
excerpt: Bolomba, Équateur Province, January 6, 2026 - A tragic boat accident occurred on the night of January 5-6 on the Congo River, between the Dianga chiefdom and the village of Bokuma in Bolomba territory, leaving at least six dead, several missing, and 73 survivors. A significant ca
title_en: Boat Shipwreck in Bolomba: At Least 6 Dead, Several Missing
excerpt_en: Bolomba, Équateur Province, January 6, 2026 - A tragic boat accident occurred on the night of January 5-6 on the Congo River, between the Dianga chiefdom and the village of Bokuma in Bolomba territory, leaving at least six dead, several missing, and 73 survivors. A significant ca
body_en:
Bolomba, Équateur Province, January 6, 2026 - A tragic boat accident occurred on the night of January 5-6 on the Congo River, between the Dianga chiefdom and the village of Bokuma in Bolomba territory, leaving at least six dead, several missing, and 73 survivors. A significant cargo was also lost, and the number of casualties could rise.
According to reports, the disaster was caused by a collision between a motorized pirogue carrying passengers and a whaleboat (registered H/B Zulu). Survivors who reached Mbandaka are facing difficulties returning to Bolomba.
This incident is part of a series of recurring accidents on the Congo River, often caused by overloaded boats, nighttime navigation, and lack of safety equipment.
Tragic Precedents
December 20, 2025: H/B Mbeya Mbeya capsized near Mbandaka, causing 10 deaths. Investigations cited overloading and absence of life jackets.
September 11, 2025: Two accidents in Basankusu and Ngombe resulted in approximately 200 deaths.
April 15, 2025: A fire near Mbandaka led to the disappearance of about 100 people.
Despite government measures such as a ban on nighttime navigation and mandatory life jacket use, authorities admit that enforcement remains weak, leaving river traffic vulnerable to repeated tragedies.

Kinshasa, January 7, 2026 - Lieutenant Colonel Mak Hazukay Mongba has been appointed interim spokesperson for the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), according to a service note signed by the FARDC Chief of Staff.
In addition to this role, he has been named interim commander of the Communication and Information Service of the FARDC (SCIFA) and will carry out the duties of interim spokesperson until further notice.
Lieutenant Colonel Hazukay replaces Major General Sylvain Ekenge, who was suspended following the broadcast of discriminatory remarks about women in a Congolese community on the public television channel RTNC.

title: Late Burial of Civilian Victims Following AFC/M23 Clashes in Walungu
excerpt: Walungu, South Kivu, January 7, 2026 - The bodies of civilians killed during clashes between the AFC-M23 rebels and the Wazalendo militia in the Ikoma region of Walungu territory last Sunday were finally buried two days later. The delay came as residents of Bumbalali fled the vio
title_en: Late Burial of Civilian Victims Following AFC/M23 Clashes in Walungu
excerpt_en: Walungu, South Kivu, January 7, 2026 - The bodies of civilians killed during clashes between the AFC-M23 rebels and the Wazalendo militia in the Ikoma region of Walungu territory last Sunday were finally buried two days later. The delay came as residents of Bumbalali fled the vio
body_en:
Walungu, South Kivu, January 7, 2026 - The bodies of civilians killed during clashes between the AFC-M23 rebels and the Wazalendo militia in the Ikoma region of Walungu territory last Sunday were finally buried two days later.
The delay came as residents of Bumbalali fled the violence, leaving behind the bodies of their neighbors who had been killed by bombs. Upon returning on Tuesday, villagers discovered the corpses still lying on the ground. In total, four civilians lost their lives: three in Bumbalali and one in Mwendo. Residents reported that the bodies were already decomposing.
“Calm had returned on Tuesday, when the M23 left the area. Around 10 a.m., we were forced to go to the site of the massacre. The slain compatriots were buried on Tuesday, the last one after 6 p.m.,” said a resident who requested anonymity.
On Monday, the victims’ bodies remained at the site because the Walungu administrator, under the orders of the AFC-M23, instructed villagers not to bury them before the arrival of Red Cross rescue teams. However, the rescue workers were forced to turn back after hearing gunfire, and the Wazalendo militia later visited the area to assess the situation, firing a few shots before withdrawing.
Large-scale population returns began on Wednesday, though gunfire near the Mugogo market again caused panic, forcing residents to scatter and resulting in the loss of several valuable items.
The incident underscores the ongoing insecurity in Walungu, which continues to disrupt civilian life and local markets.

title: MONUSCO Evacuates Over 150 Civilians from Djugu Conflict Zone
excerpt: Djugu, Ituri, January 9, 2026 - In the past month, MONUSCO has evacuated 152 vulnerable people from the Bule region of Djugu territory to Bunia amid ongoing clashes between the FARDC (Armed Forces of the DRC) and militias of the Convention for the Popular Revolution (CRP) led by
title_en: MONUSCO Evacuates Over 150 Civilians from Djugu Conflict Zone
excerpt_en: Djugu, Ituri, January 9, 2026 - In the past month, MONUSCO has evacuated 152 vulnerable people from the Bule region of Djugu territory to Bunia amid ongoing clashes between the FARDC (Armed Forces of the DRC) and militias of the Convention for the Popular Revolution (CRP) led by
body_en:
Djugu, Ituri, January 9, 2026 - In the past month, MONUSCO has evacuated 152 vulnerable people from the Bule region of Djugu territory to Bunia amid ongoing clashes between the FARDC (Armed Forces of the DRC) and militias of the Convention for the Popular Revolution (CRP) led by Thomas Lubanga.
The commander of the Bangladeshi peacekeepers deployed with MONUSCO reported the operations on Thursday, January 8, during a meeting with a UN mission delegation in Bayo. The evacuated individuals include wounded soldiers, humanitarian workers, priests, medical personnel, teachers, and other at-risk civilians. Evacuations were carried out via vehicle, helicopter, and armored tank.
To strengthen civilian protection, Bangladeshi peacekeepers conducted 152 combat patrols over the past month in the Savo Plain, where thousands of families have been displaced by the conflict.
The fighting, ongoing since December 5, 2025, has severely impacted Bule-Centre in the Badjere chiefdom, which has been largely reduced to a ghost town as FARDC and CRP militias contest control.
Through these operations, MONUSCO reaffirms its support for the FARDC in efforts to restore peace in the region and highlights the continued intensification of patrols to protect civilians in accordance with its mandate.

title: Motorcycle Taxi Drivers Denounce Illegal Roadblocks on Goma-Masisi-Walikale Road
excerpt: Goma, January 8, 2026 - Motorcycle taxi drivers using the Goma-Masisi-Walikale road are raising alarms over repeated looting and the proliferation of illegal roadblocks set up by armed groups along the route. The road passes through a buffer zone, with one portion controlled by t
title_en: Motorcycle Taxi Drivers Denounce Illegal Roadblocks on Goma-Masisi-Walikale Road
excerpt_en: Goma, January 8, 2026 - Motorcycle taxi drivers using the Goma-Masisi-Walikale road are raising alarms over repeated looting and the proliferation of illegal roadblocks set up by armed groups along the route. The road passes through a buffer zone, with one portion controlled by t
body_en:
Goma, January 8, 2026 - Motorcycle taxi drivers using the Goma-Masisi-Walikale road are raising alarms over repeated looting and the proliferation of illegal roadblocks set up by armed groups along the route.
The road passes through a buffer zone, with one portion controlled by the FARDC (Armed Forces of the DRC) and the Wazalendo militia, and another portion occupied by AFC-M23 rebels. Drivers report that these conditions have made travel dangerous and costly.
Lucien Amani Bitaha, spokesperson for the motorcyclists, said that motorcyclists now have to budget at least 200,000 Congolese francs (around 90 US dollars) to transport a single package from Goma to Walikale. He also described repeated looting incidents along the stretch between Kashebere and Miba, controlled by M23 rebels, and in the buffer zone between Kibati and Mikumbi, while the Miba area is under government and Wazalendo control.
“The road is completely dilapidated, with reeds growing in abundance, which only exacerbates the insecurity. Passengers, package owners, and motorcyclists alike continue to suffer these losses,” he added.
A local traditional leader from the Ihana group confirmed that authorities have been informed through official reports, but there has been no visible intervention to date to improve security or remove the illegal roadblocks.

title: Six CRP Militiamen Surrender Amid Fighting with FARDC in Djugu
excerpt: Djugu, Ituri, January 9, 2026 - Six militiamen from the Convention for the Popular Revolution (CRP) surrendered on Friday, January 9, during clashes with the Armed Forces of the DRC (FARDC) in the Nyaka and Lodha localities of Djugu territory. The surrender followed an attack by
title_en: Six CRP Militiamen Surrender Amid Fighting with FARDC in Djugu
excerpt_en: Djugu, Ituri, January 9, 2026 - Six militiamen from the Convention for the Popular Revolution (CRP) surrendered on Friday, January 9, during clashes with the Armed Forces of the DRC (FARDC) in the Nyaka and Lodha localities of Djugu territory. The surrender followed an attack by
body_en:
Djugu, Ituri, January 9, 2026 - Six militiamen from the Convention for the Popular Revolution (CRP) surrendered on Friday, January 9, during clashes with the Armed Forces of the DRC (FARDC) in the Nyaka and Lodha localities of Djugu territory.
The surrender followed an attack by CRP fighters on a FARDC position in the area. Sporadic gunfire had been reported since last Monday around Fataki, where Thomas Lubanga’s CRP militia had unsuccessfully tried to establish a foothold following an incursion into Bule, approximately 15 kilometers away.
These attempts were repeatedly repelled by MONUSCO soldiers, stationed in Djaiba, who maintain regular patrols in the region.
On the morning of Friday, January 9, the CRP attacked a FARDC position near Lodha, which also hosts a camp for internally displaced persons. The FARDC, reinforced in the area, responded vigorously, leading to clashes that continued until mid-afternoon.
MONUSCO peacekeepers intensified patrols along the Fataki-Lodha and Fataki-Sanduku roads to protect civilians, many of whom fled to nearby FARDC positions and the MONUSCO base due to ongoing threats from the militia.
The incident underscores the persistent insecurity in Djugu and the continued efforts by FARDC and MONUSCO to safeguard civilians.

title_en: North Kivu Authorities Recommend Cantonment of FARDC and Wazalendo to Reduce Insecurity in Lubero and Butembo
excerpt_en: Lubero-Butembo, January 10, 2026 - The North Kivu provincial security committee has recommended the cantonment of FARDC soldiers and Wazalendo fighters to demilitarize Lubero commune, reduce tensions, and better protect civilians. The decision was made during a meeting held on Th
body_en:
Lubero-Butembo, January 10, 2026 - The North Kivu provincial security committee has recommended the cantonment of FARDC soldiers and Wazalendo fighters to demilitarize Lubero commune, reduce tensions, and better protect civilians. The decision was made during a meeting held on Thursday, January 8, in Butembo with representatives from both Lubero commune and Butembo city.
The meeting addressed concerns from local communities regarding a recent surge in crime, including urban banditry, looting, and murders. In Lubero, about twenty cases of criminal activity were recorded within a few days, prompting civil society-led general strikes to pressure authorities into action.
In Butembo, insecurity has also resulted in the murder of two people and the theft of several motorcycles by armed bandits.
The provincial security committee, led by Governor Évariste Kakule Somo, met with local representatives to discuss measures aimed at restoring law and order. Jackson Mumbere, a civil society representative in Lubero commune, emphasized the community’s expectations:“Murders, extortion, and looting have been reported, along with numerous other incidents. We met with the provincial governor, who responded favorably to our requests. We will monitor how the proposed solutions are implemented upon returning to Lubero-Centre.”
Authorities also announced that they would cover funeral expenses for the victim murdered on Wednesday evening in Butembo, signaling immediate steps to address the consequences of escalating insecurity.

title_en: Central Bank of Congo Maintains Easing of Monetary Policy
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, January 8, 2026 - The Central Bank of Congo (BCC) announced the continuation of its monetary policy easing during its ordinary session on Thursday, January 8, in Kinshasa. This marks the second decision in three months to maintain the policy initiated in the last quarte
body_en:
Kinshasa, January 8, 2026 - The Central Bank of Congo (BCC) announced the continuation of its monetary policy easing during its ordinary session on Thursday, January 8, in Kinshasa. This marks the second decision in three months to maintain the policy initiated in the last quarter of 2025.
The Monetary Policy Committee, chaired by Governor André Wameso Nkualoloki, explained that the measure aims to create favorable financing conditions for the national economy while preserving macroeconomic stability. In practice, this means gradually lowering borrowing costs to facilitate credit for businesses and households without jeopardizing the financial system.
Governor Nkualoloki stated:“For 2026, the Monetary Policy Committee forecasts controlled price increases, in a context of exchange rate stabilization and sustained economic growth.”
He added that the national economy is expected to benefit from favorable developments in metal prices, particularly copper and cobalt, while remaining influenced by global geopolitical tensions and tariffs. At the domestic level, easing monetary policy is also linked to hopes for reduced conflicts in the eastern regions.
The committee reaffirmed its commitment to closely monitoring economic developments and liquidity, emphasizing that businesses will enjoy better borrowing conditions, encouraging productive investment, and households will have improved access to financing for housing or business activities.

title_en: FARDC and UPDF Intensify Operations Against ADF in Mambasa
excerpt_en: Mambasa, January 9, 2026 - Joint FARDC-UPDF forces continued their offensive against ADF rebels on Friday, January 9, in the Kolo-Kolo and Banju-Banju localities, deep in the forests of Mambasa territory. The operations follow a recent ADF attack on an army position, which report
body_en:
Mambasa, January 9, 2026 - Joint FARDC-UPDF forces continued their offensive against ADF rebels on Friday, January 9, in the Kolo-Kolo and Banju-Banju localities, deep in the forests of Mambasa territory. The operations follow a recent ADF attack on an army position, which reportedly killed around ten FARDC soldiers.
The month-long offensive aims to dismantle ADF strongholds in the Babila Bakwanza chiefdom, allowing civilians to safely access their fields and move freely. For several months, the ADF rebels have established fortified positions in the heart of the chiefdom, approximately 100 kilometers southwest of Bunia, from which they plan attacks on civilians and security forces along National Route 4 on the Komanda-Mambasa axis.
Local sources report that the rebels also impose illegal taxes on farmers, exacerbating the hardships faced by the population.
Security forces have faced heavy casualties, including the loss of about ten soldiers, and some army camps have been burned during ambushes. Reinforcements have since been deployed to continue the dismantling of ADF positions.
Civil society actors in Mambasa have welcomed the interventions, noting that ADF violence has significantly decreased in the region as a result of the joint operations.

excerpt: Bujumbura, January 9, 2026 - Minister of State for Humanitarian Affairs, Eve Bazaïba, visited Bujumbura, Burundi, on Friday, January 9, to strengthen aid coordination and evaluate the humanitarian situation of at least 250,000 Congolese refugees who fled Uvira, South Kivu, after
title_en: Eve Bazaïba Travels to Bujumbura to Assess Humanitarian Crisis Affecting 250,000 Congolese Refugees
excerpt_en: Bujumbura, January 9, 2026 - Minister of State for Humanitarian Affairs, Eve Bazaïba, visited Bujumbura, Burundi, on Friday, January 9, to strengthen aid coordination and evaluate the humanitarian situation of at least 250,000 Congolese refugees who fled Uvira, South Kivu, after
body_en:
Bujumbura, January 9, 2026 - Minister of State for Humanitarian Affairs, Eve Bazaïba, visited Bujumbura, Burundi, on Friday, January 9, to strengthen aid coordination and evaluate the humanitarian situation of at least 250,000 Congolese refugees who fled Uvira, South Kivu, after its fall to AFC-M23 rebels in November 2025.
Humanitarian data indicates that over 101,000 displaced Congolese crossed into Burundi following Uvira’s capture, bringing the total number of Congolese refugees in the country to more than 250,000. Many of these refugees are from North and South Kivu provinces and live in precarious conditions, with approximately 30,000 children out of school, further exacerbating family vulnerabilities.
During her visit, Eve Bazaïba met with Burundian authorities and UNHCR officials to improve the coordination of humanitarian assistance. Priority needs include food, clean water, medical care, and emergency shelter.
The UNHCR has highlighted an alarming health situation, reporting 53 deaths, including 25 from cholera, and estimates that over US$33 million is required to respond adequately to the emergency.
Minister Bazaïba reaffirmed the Congolese government’s commitment, including the systematic registration of refugees to prevent infiltration and ensure proper assistance.

excerpt_en: Mbuji-Mayi, January 10, 2026 - A Congolese National Police officer (PNC) and his child under 10 years old were seriously wounded by gunfire from armed men wearing police uniforms on the night of Friday, January 10, in Bipemba, a commune in Mbuji-Mayi, Kasai-Oriental province. The
body_en:
Mbuji-Mayi, January 10, 2026 - A Congolese National Police officer (PNC) and his child under 10 years old were seriously wounded by gunfire from armed men wearing police uniforms on the night of Friday, January 10, in Bipemba, a commune in Mbuji-Mayi, Kasai-Oriental province. The motive for the attack remains unknown.
One of the assailants was apprehended by local police who arrived on the scene. Residents report that this incident is part of a series of criminal acts terrorizing the commune over several days.
The mayor of Bipemba has called for an increase in police personnel to ensure the safety of the population.
Residents expressed deep concern over the insecurity. Monique Mujinga, a local housewife, said:"At home, we haven't slept since the holidays. We spend the nights outside so we can shout. As soon as the bandits enter a house, they beat the owners, kill them, and steal all their belongings. It's terrible."
Conclusion: A Nation at a Strategic and Security Crossroads
The period between late December 2025 and early January 2026 has been defined by a complex interplay of strategic diplomatic maneuvers, persistent security volatility, and ambitious domestic reforms. As the DRC enters 2026, it faces a critical "refoundation" phase aimed at balancing international partnerships with the urgent need for internal stability.
1. Strategic Diplomacy and Sovereignty A central theme of this period was the government’s defense of the Washington Agreement, a strategic partnership with the United States. Despite domestic criticism alleging a "sell-off" of national resources, the executive branch maintained that the agreement is a technical framework for long-term development in sectors like energy (Grand Inga) and infrastructure (Lobito Corridor) without compromising sovereignty. Simultaneously, the DRC’s entry into the UN Security Council as a non-permanent member on January 1, 2026, signals its intent to internationalize the eastern crisis and demand greater respect for international law.
2. Persistent Security and Humanitarian Challenges The security situation in the eastern provinces remains the nation's most pressing concern. The government continues to condemn what it describes as a "war imposed" by Rwandan forces and the expansion of territory held by AFC/M23. While joint FARDC-UPDF operations have enabled the return of some displaced persons in Irumu, other regions like Masisi and Ituri face ongoing violence, resulting in the displacement of thousands and the paralysis of essential services like education.
3. Internal Governance and Social Unrest Domestically, the government is grappling with issues of governance and human rights. The suspension of military spokesman Major General Sylvain Ekenge over discriminatory remarks highlights the sensitive nature of ethnic tensions and hate speech within the country. Furthermore, a series of criminal acts-including the assassination of a journalist in Bunia and a professor in Kinshasa-has fueled public outcry and demands for better protection of civilians.
4. Economic Modernization and Health Trends On a positive note, the DRC has made strides in digital reform, launching electronic systems to modernize foreign trade and secure vehicle registration to combat fraud and increase state revenue. In public health, there is an encouraging decline in monkeypox cases, though new outbreaks of measles in Kasai-Oriental present a fresh challenge to the health system.
Final Outlook The start of 2026 finds the DRC caught between the hope of economic transformation and the reality of chronic conflict. The success of the "year of refoundation" will likely depend on the government's ability to translate its new international diplomatic standing into tangible security gains on the ground and to foster national unity through inclusive dialogue and transparent governance.
By Glad MUSEMA
Jeff Buleli

title: ICGLR Defense Ministers’ Meeting: DRC Presses for Peace and Tests Regional Credibility
excerpt: Livingstone, January 12, 2026 - The Defense Ministers of ICGLR member states met in an extraordinary session on January 10 in Livingstone, Zambia, to address the humanitarian and security crisis in eastern DRC and across the Great Lakes region, amid ongoing fighting between gover
title_en: ICGLR Defense Ministers’ Meeting: DRC Presses for Peace and Tests Regional Credibility
excerpt_en: Livingstone, January 12, 2026 - The Defense Ministers of ICGLR member states met in an extraordinary session on January 10 in Livingstone, Zambia, to address the humanitarian and security crisis in eastern DRC and across the Great Lakes region, amid ongoing fighting between gover
body_en:
Livingstone, January 12, 2026 - The Defense Ministers of ICGLR member states met in an extraordinary session on January 10 in Livingstone, Zambia, to address the humanitarian and security crisis in eastern DRC and across the Great Lakes region, amid ongoing fighting between government forces and the AFC/M23 rebellion.
The meeting followed earlier sessions of the ICGLR Specialized Committee of Defense Experts and the Chiefs of Staff, the body responsible for overseeing the Non-Aggression Protocol.
A central focus was the performance of the Expanded Joint Verification Mechanism (EJVM), tasked with monitoring and investigating security incidents in the region. The mechanism has faced challenges, including irregular meetings and limited reporting, prompting chiefs of staff to draft recommendations for defense ministers.
The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defense, Guy Kabombo Muadiamvita, stressed that peace cannot be delayed or subordinated to political calculations, calling for regional mechanisms to become credible, operational, and deterrent to protect civilians and end cycles of violence.
He placed particular emphasis on the effective operationalization of the Expanded Joint Verification Mechanism Plus (EJVM+), describing it as a test of credibility for both the ICGLR and the region as a whole.
During the session, ministers officially installed the new commander and deputy commander of the EJVM, based in Goma, reinforcing the regional security framework.
The new roadmap prioritizes the implementation of the Washington and Doha processes, especially the ceasefire mechanism signed on October 14, 2025, between the Congolese government and the AFC/M23 under Qatari mediation. However, implementation on the ground remains difficult, largely because the verification and monitoring mechanism is not yet fully operational.
Revitalizing the EJVM is therefore seen as essential to ensuring effective ceasefire monitoring and restoring the credibility of ongoing peace efforts.
body_fr:
Livingstone, January 12, 2026 - The Defense Ministers of ICGLR member states met in an extraordinary session on January 10 in Livingstone, Zambia, to address the humanitarian and security crisis in eastern DRC and across the Great Lakes region, amid ongoing fighting between government forces and the AFC/M23 rebellion.
The meeting followed earlier sessions of the ICGLR Specialized Committee of Defense Experts and the Chiefs of Staff, the body responsible for overseeing the Non-Aggression Protocol.
A central focus was the performance of the Expanded Joint Verification Mechanism (EJVM), tasked with monitoring and investigating security incidents in the region. The mechanism has faced challenges, including irregular meetings and limited reporting, prompting chiefs of staff to draft recommendations for defense ministers.
The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defense, Guy Kabombo Muadiamvita, stressed that peace cannot be delayed or subordinated to political calculations, calling for regional mechanisms to become credible, operational, and deterrent to protect civilians and end cycles of violence.
He placed particular emphasis on the effective operationalization of the Expanded Joint Verification Mechanism Plus (EJVM+), describing it as a test of credibility for both the ICGLR and the region as a whole.
During the session, ministers officially installed the new commander and deputy commander of the EJVM, based in Goma, reinforcing the regional security framework.
The new roadmap prioritizes the implementation of the Washington and Doha processes, especially the ceasefire mechanism signed on October 14, 2025, between the Congolese government and the AFC/M23 under Qatari mediation. However, implementation on the ground remains difficult, largely because the verification and monitoring mechanism is not yet fully operational.
Revitalizing the EJVM is therefore seen as essential to ensuring effective ceasefire monitoring and restoring the credibility of ongoing peace efforts.

title: Luanda Consults Congolese Religious Leaders
excerpt: The meeting brought together bishops from the National Episcopal Conference of Congo (CENCO) and pastors from the Church of Christ in Congo (ECC). It followed two visits within a week by President Félix Tshisekedi to Luanda for consultations with his Angolan counterpart. The dipl
title_en: Luanda Consults Congolese Religious Leaders
excerpt_en: The meeting brought together bishops from the National Episcopal Conference of Congo (CENCO) and pastors from the Church of Christ in Congo (ECC). It followed two visits within a week by President Félix Tshisekedi to Luanda for consultations with his Angolan counterpart. The dipl
body_en:
The meeting brought together bishops from the National Episcopal Conference of Congo (CENCO) and pastors from the Church of Christ in Congo (ECC). It followed two visits within a week by President Félix Tshisekedi to Luanda for consultations with his Angolan counterpart.
The diplomatic momentum around the eastern DRC crisis has intensified in recent weeks. A telephone exchange reportedly took place between Qatari Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani and Angolan Foreign Minister Tete António, focusing on a peaceful solution between the DRC and Rwanda. Doha reiterated its commitment to dialogue.
These talks come as negotiations on the six protocols meant to complement the first two of the framework agreement between the Congolese government and the AFC/M23 remain stalled, according to informed sources.
Since the start of 2026, Félix Tshisekedi has traveled to Luanda twice in less than a month - an unusual pace in bilateral relations. According to sources within the Congolese presidency, João Lourenço has submitted several proposals, but no immediate decision or new peace process has been officially announced.
After announcing its withdrawal from mediation in the Congolese crisis in March 2025, Angola has made a gradual and discreet return, multiplying consultations with key stakeholders. In this context, former President Joseph Kabila was received in Luanda at the end of December, followed by a visit from a delegation from his camp.
Angolan diplomacy has also engaged with the AFC/M23 political-military movement. Its coordinator, Corneille Nangaa, reportedly sent a letter to President João Lourenço seeking clarification on the nature of Angola’s initiative, particularly regarding a possible new process.
The diplomatic push has expanded to Togo. President Félix Tshisekedi traveled to Lomé for a working session on peace and stabilization in eastern DRC, at the invitation of Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé, President of the Council of the Republic of Togo and AU-appointed mediator. The visit was described as brief.
Togo plans to host a high-level meeting on January 17 aimed at strengthening coordination of peace initiatives in the DRC and the Great Lakes region. This builds on recent international efforts, including the Paris Peace Conference of October 30, 2025, which mobilized more than €1.5 billion for vulnerable populations and supported negotiations led by the United States, Qatar, and the African Union.
Faure Gnassingbé succeeded João Lourenço as the AU-designated mediator for the eastern DRC conflict, following decisions of the joint virtual summit of the East African Community (EAC) and the Southern African Development Community (SADC) held on March 24, 2025.

title: France Calls for Reopening of Goma Airport, Confirms Full Disbursement of €850 Million in Emergency Humanitarian Aid - January 20, 2026
excerpt: France has raised the issue of the reopening of Goma International Airport and confirmed that the entire €850 million in emergency humanitarian aid pledged for the Great Lakes region has already been fully disbursed. France took part in a high-level meeting on the coherence and c
title_en: France Calls for Reopening of Goma Airport, Confirms Full Disbursement of €850 Million in Emergency Humanitarian Aid - January 20, 2026
excerpt_en: France has raised the issue of the reopening of Goma International Airport and confirmed that the entire €850 million in emergency humanitarian aid pledged for the Great Lakes region has already been fully disbursed. France took part in a high-level meeting on the coherence and c
body_en:
France has raised the issue of the reopening of Goma International Airport and confirmed that the entire €850 million in emergency humanitarian aid pledged for the Great Lakes region has already been fully disbursed.
France took part in a high-level meeting on the coherence and consolidation of the peace process in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and the Great Lakes region, held on January 17, 2026, in Lomé, Togo. The meeting brought together facilitators, including former heads of state, leaders of the East African Community (EAC) and the Southern African Development Community (SADC), alongside several international partners. It was convened at the initiative of Faure Gnassingbé, African Union mediator for the crisis in eastern DRC.
During the discussions, France presented an initial progress assessment on the implementation of financial commitments made at the Paris Conference for Peace and Prosperity in the Great Lakes Region, held on October 30, 2025. Of the €1.5 billion pledged by 70 states and international organizations, all emergency humanitarian funding, amounting to €850 million, has already been released.
France reiterated the severity of the humanitarian crisis in eastern DRC, stressing that the funds are intended to meet urgent needs, ensure essential services, and strengthen civilian protection, particularly in areas affected by violence and forced displacement. It also encouraged remaining donors to accelerate their disbursements in the coming weeks.
The French authorities further underlined the urgent need to remove humanitarian obstacles, recalling the commitments made in Paris regarding the humanitarian reopening of Goma airport. France expressed its readiness to contribute, alongside its partners and in coordination with the United Nations, to the logistical and coordination efforts required to reopen the airport for humanitarian flights.
The Paris Conference aimed to mobilize international support to address the humanitarian emergency in the Great Lakes region while backing mediation efforts led by the United States, Qatar, and the African Union. On the margins of the event, discussions also focused on regional economic integration, described as a key pillar for sustainable peace after decades of instability.
At the conclusion of the Paris meetings, two major announcements were made: the mobilization of €1.5 billion in humanitarian aid for the region, and the intention to reopen Goma International Airport, the capital of North Kivu. French President Emmanuel Macron described the reopening of the airport as a concrete and essential signal for the population of North Kivu, calling for swift implementation with the support of international mediators.
However, the announcement sparked strong opposition from the AFC/M23 rebel movement. The group rejected any decision by the Kinshasa authorities to reopen the airport, claiming that the infrastructure lies within what it describes as “liberated territory.” The movement accused Congolese authorities of having looted and sabotaged the facility and insisted that only the AFC/M23 could authorize its reopening.
In the same statement, the group maintained that the dispute between Kinshasa and Kigali does not concern it, asserting that the Congolese government alone bears responsibility for its relations with neighboring states and should resolve its disputes without involving the movement.

title: Opposition Leader Seth Kikuni Goes Into Exile
excerpt: Kinshasa, January 19, 2026 - Opposition leader Seth Kikuni has left the country and is now in exile, following what his political allies describe as a discreet, coordinated, and courageous operation that ensured his safety and preserved his physical and moral integrity. In a stat
title_en: Opposition Leader Seth Kikuni Goes Into Exile
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, January 19, 2026 - Opposition leader Seth Kikuni has left the country and is now in exile, following what his political allies describe as a discreet, coordinated, and courageous operation that ensured his safety and preserved his physical and moral integrity. In a stat
body_en:
Kinshasa, January 19, 2026 - Opposition leader Seth Kikuni has left the country and is now in exile, following what his political allies describe as a discreet, coordinated, and courageous operation that ensured his safety and preserved his physical and moral integrity.
In a statement released Monday, the Consultation Framework for Political and Social Forces said the former 2023 presidential candidate faced an imminent arbitrary political procedure, linked to a letter dated December 15, 2025, from the Auditor General of the Supreme Military Court to the Prosecutor General of the Court of Cassation.
The coalition expressed its deep gratitude to all individuals and organizations involved in what it called a delicate rescue operation, carried out amid serious threats and flagrant violations of fundamental freedoms. It also announced that Mr. Kikuni would address national and international audiences in the coming days to clarify the circumstances of his departure.
Mr. Kikuni was released from Makala Prison on March 1, 2025, after six months of detention, having been sentenced in September 2024 to one year in prison for “incitement to civil disobedience” and “spreading false rumors.”
Upon his return to Kinshasa on October 18, 2025, after attending an opposition summit in Nairobi, he was re-arrested at Ndjili International Airport by individuals presenting themselves as members of the National Intelligence Agency (ANR). His passport, confiscated by the Directorate General of Migration, has not been returned.
On Monday, the opposition leader also strongly criticized the president’s trip to Davos, Switzerland, where he is attending the 56th World Economic Forum.

title: Qatar Backs Togo’s Initiative to Consolidate Peace Process in Eastern DRC
excerpt: Lomé, January 18, 2026 - The State of Qatar, a key mediator in the crisis between the government of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and the AFC/M23 rebellion, has reaffirmed its commitment to the peace process, viewing Togo’s diplomatic initiative as proof of sustained mom
title_en: Qatar Backs Togo’s Initiative to Consolidate Peace Process in Eastern DRC
excerpt_en: Lomé, January 18, 2026 - The State of Qatar, a key mediator in the crisis between the government of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and the AFC/M23 rebellion, has reaffirmed its commitment to the peace process, viewing Togo’s diplomatic initiative as proof of sustained mom
body_en:
Lomé, January 18, 2026 - The State of Qatar, a key mediator in the crisis between the government of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and the AFC/M23 rebellion, has reaffirmed its commitment to the peace process, viewing Togo’s diplomatic initiative as proof of sustained momentum toward stability in the Great Lakes region.
Qatar took part in a high-level meeting on the coherence and consolidation of peace efforts in the DRC and the wider region, held in Lomé, the capital of Togo. The country was represented by Ahmed Essa Al Sulaiti, advisor to the Minister of State at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
Discussions focused on the humanitarian crisis, regional security coordination, de-escalation mechanisms, support for humanitarian operations, and the promotion of economic integration. The meeting followed the signing of the Doha Peace Framework between the Congolese government and the Congo River Alliance (M23 Movement), underscoring continued diplomatic engagement despite the lack of immediate breakthroughs.
Although no new peace initiatives were announced, participants agreed to strengthen African mediation in 2026, relying on five former African heads of state as co-facilitators. Diplomatic missions are planned in the coming days to Kinshasa, Kigali, Kampala, and Gitega to accelerate the implementation of commitments made by the parties.
The final communiqué urged all sides to implement their commitments in good faith, prioritize peaceful conflict resolution, and reaffirmed full support for the Doha process. It also called for the rapid resumption of negotiations on the six remaining protocols and emphasized the need for structured African monitoring of the peace agreements.
With the 39th African Union Summit scheduled for February 11-15, 2026, in Addis Ababa, the Togolese mediator for eastern DRC, Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé, is expected to present a report on the evolving security situation and mediation progress, in line with recent African Union Peace and Security Council decisions.
This diplomatic push comes as the Doha talks, led by the Emir of Qatar, continue to face challenges in translating negotiations into concrete results on the ground. The talks aim to complement the Washington agreements by addressing the root causes of the conflict, including the restoration of state authority and the reintegration of armed groups, but progress remains slow despite the signing of five key instruments.

With the 39th African Union Summit scheduled for February 11-15, 2026, in Addis Ababa, the Togolese mediator for eastern DRC, Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé, is expected to present a report on the evolving security situation and mediation progress, in line with recent African Union Peace and Security Council decisions.
This diplomatic push comes as the Doha talks, led by the Emir of Qatar, continue to face challenges in translating negotiations into concrete results on the ground. The talks aim to complement the Washington agreements by addressing the root causes of the conflict, including the restoration of state authority and the reintegration of armed groups, but progress remains slow despite the signing of five key instruments.
