title: King Philippe Urges Tshisekedi to Launch Inclusive Dialogue, Pledges European Support on DRC Humanitarian Crisis
excerpt: Davos, January 21, 2026 - Belgium’s King Philippe has encouraged President Félix Tshisekedi to organize an inclusive national dialogue in the Democratic Republic of Congo, while pledging to mobilize European partners around the country’s worsening humanitarian situation. The meet
title_en: King Philippe Urges Tshisekedi to Launch Inclusive Dialogue, Pledges European Support on DRC Humanitarian Crisis
excerpt_en: Davos, January 21, 2026 - Belgium’s King Philippe has encouraged President Félix Tshisekedi to organize an inclusive national dialogue in the Democratic Republic of Congo, while pledging to mobilize European partners around the country’s worsening humanitarian situation. The meet
body_en:
Davos, January 21, 2026 - Belgium’s King Philippe has encouraged President Félix Tshisekedi to organize an inclusive national dialogue in the Democratic Republic of Congo, while pledging to mobilize European partners around the country’s worsening humanitarian situation.
The meeting took place on the sidelines of the 56th World Economic Forum Annual Meeting in Davos, where the two leaders discussed the security crisis in eastern DRC and the broader political situation.
Belgian Foreign Minister Maxime Prévot confirmed that Brussels reiterated its support for a national dialogue, long demanded by the opposition and seen as a key step toward addressing the root causes of the country’s multifaceted crisis.
Belgium reaffirmed its commitment to a peaceful resolution of the conflict in eastern DRC and respect for the country’s territorial integrity. King Philippe also pledged to ensure that European governments are fully informed of the dramatic humanitarian conditions facing civilians in areas affected by the M23 rebellion.
“Belgium remains a strategic partner of the DRC, determined to support peace,” Prévot said.
As discussions around a dialogue framework advance, the “Save the DRC” political and social platform, backed by former President Joseph Kabila, has been consulted twice by Angolan President João Lourenço. The platform has indicated it would support abandoning the Doha process with the AFC/M23 only if the proposed dialogue is genuinely inclusive and focused on restoring peace in the east.
Meanwhile, the Catholic bishops (CENCO) and Protestant leaders (ECC) who initiated the dialogue effort were also received by President Lourenço, days after his second meeting in a month with President Tshisekedi in Luanda.
Several opposition figures have likewise met with the current Chairperson of the African Union, as political consultations intensify ahead of a dialogue long awaited by the opposition and civil society.

title: 13th Governors’ Conference in Kwilu: New Dates Pending, Airport Rehabilitation Contract Reassigned
excerpt: Kinshasa, January 22, 2026 - Preparations for the 13th session of the Governors’ Conference, scheduled to take place in Kwilu Province, were reviewed on Wednesday during a working meeting at the Prime Minister’s Office. The meeting, chaired by the Deputy Chief of Staff to the Pri
title_en: 13th Governors’ Conference in Kwilu: New Dates Pending, Airport Rehabilitation Contract Reassigned
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, January 22, 2026 - Preparations for the 13th session of the Governors’ Conference, scheduled to take place in Kwilu Province, were reviewed on Wednesday during a working meeting at the Prime Minister’s Office. The meeting, chaired by the Deputy Chief of Staff to the Pri
body_en:
Kinshasa, January 22, 2026 - Preparations for the 13th session of the Governors’ Conference, scheduled to take place in Kwilu Province, were reviewed on Wednesday during a working meeting at the Prime Minister’s Office.
The meeting, chaired by the Deputy Chief of Staff to the Prime Minister, brought together the Permanent Secretary of the Governors’ Conference, the Vice-Governor of Kwilu, the Director General of the Congolese Agency for Major Works (ACGT), and the Director General of Safrimex.
Discussions focused primarily on the progress of rehabilitation works at the Bandundu and Kikwit airports, particularly the runways and aprons, as well as on urban road projects, pending the announcement of new conference dates by the Head of State.
The Permanent Secretary, currently on mission in Bandundu, reported that urban road works are progressing normally. However, rehabilitation of the Bandundu airport runway and tarmac has been suspended following the termination of the contract between the Roads Authority and the Civil Aviation Authority. The initial contractor reportedly failed to demonstrate sufficient technical and financial capacity to complete the project within the required timeframe.
The contract has now been awarded to Safrimex, while feasibility studies continue under the coordination of the Congolese Agency for Major Works. Authorities emphasized the need to accelerate the process to ensure the mobility of conference participants. Priority will be given to reinforcing the runway and tarmac to allow the conference to proceed, while full airport construction will continue under the same company.
“The studies are complete. It is now up to the government to support Safrimex, the company in charge of the work in Bandundu. The government demands quality work so that Bandundu can have an airport worthy of its status and capable of supporting air traffic development,” said Jean-Rigobert Tshimanga, Permanent Secretary of the Governors’ Conference.
Kwilu Vice-Governor Professor Espoir Masamanki assured the public that preparations on the ground are continuing, particularly in terms of accommodation and site development, and that mobilization remains strong ahead of the announcement of new dates.
“We have explored several options to accelerate the Bandundu airport project so that, during the next visit, the Head of State and his guests can land under optimal conditions. In both Bandundu and Kikwit, the population is highly motivated and eagerly awaiting the new date,” he said.
Construction work at the Bandundu and Kikwit airports has been suspended since December 10, 2025. According to the Roads Authority, completion rates currently stand at 23% in Bandundu and 15% in Kikwit. Meanwhile, concrete work continues on Kwango Avenue near the Central Bank of Congo, along with the construction of drainage ditches, although temporary structures have yet to be installed.

title: Rwanda Warns Against “Uncontrollable Actors” and Reaffirms Commitment to Regional Stability
excerpt: Washington Accords January 23, 2026 - In response to renewed clashes in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, Rwanda has reaffirmed its commitment to the Washington Accords signed with the DRC under U.S. auspices, while calling for the strict implementation of security measures t
title_en: Rwanda Warns Against “Uncontrollable Actors” and Reaffirms Commitment to Regional Stability
excerpt_en: Washington Accords January 23, 2026 - In response to renewed clashes in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, Rwanda has reaffirmed its commitment to the Washington Accords signed with the DRC under U.S. auspices, while calling for the strict implementation of security measures t
body_en:
Washington Accords January 23, 2026 - In response to renewed clashes in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, Rwanda has reaffirmed its commitment to the Washington Accords signed with the DRC under U.S. auspices, while calling for the strict implementation of security measures to prevent escalation and protect civilians.
In an official statement issued on Thursday, January 22, Rwanda’s ambassador to the United States, Mathilde Mukantabana, outlined Kigali’s position on the implementation and implications of the accords.
Rwanda expressed its gratitude to the United States for prioritizing the peace process between Rwanda and the DRC, in coordination with Qatar’s mediation efforts, describing the Washington Accords as a major step toward lasting stability, security, and prosperity in the Great Lakes region.
However, the Rwandan diplomat warned of continued violence in eastern DRC, attributing it to “uncontrollable actors,” including mercenaries, militias supported by certain governments, and elements within the Congolese state. According to her, these actors attempted to undermine the Washington Accords by orchestrating violence in November and December 2025 and shifting blame onto Rwanda.
She also stated that the AFC/M23 rebels had unilaterally withdrawn from Uvira in South Kivu, a move Kigali described as a sign of commitment to de-escalation.
The statement recalls the historical insecurity in the region, particularly linked to the FDLR, which Rwanda accuses of responsibility for atrocities committed since 1994.
Rwanda emphasized that it continues to maintain defensive measures to protect its population against any resurgence of genocidal violence.
“The memory of the genocide survivors, the graves of a million victims, and the documented history of the Abacengezi insurgency compel us to maintain our defense capabilities until credible security guarantees are established and the threat disappears permanently,” the statement said.
On the political and economic front, Rwanda stressed that the Washington Accords are not intended to influence the internal affairs of the DRC, but rather to serve as a framework for regional development.
“The Regional Investment Framework for Peace (REIF) identifies key areas for economic cooperation between Rwanda and the DRC, demonstrating the tangible benefits of peace and creating investment and growth opportunities that directly benefit regional populations,” the statement added.
Rwanda reaffirmed its willingness to continue security coordination, contingent upon the disarmament and neutralization of the FDLR, while also supporting cross-border economic development.
Kigali concluded by reiterating its readiness to work with the DRC, the United States, Qatar, the African Union, and other partners to transform the Washington Accords into lasting peace and inclusive regional development.

excerpt: Uvira DRC January 23, 2026 - Jean Jacques Purusi, governor of South Kivu province, returned to Uvira, the provisional provincial capital, on Friday following the withdrawal of the AFC/M23. On his first day back in the city, which he had left more than 40 days earlier, the governo
title_en: After AFC/M23 Withdrawal, Governor Purusi Calls for Peaceful Coexistence in Uvira
excerpt_en: Uvira DRC January 23, 2026 - Jean Jacques Purusi, governor of South Kivu province, returned to Uvira, the provisional provincial capital, on Friday following the withdrawal of the AFC/M23. On his first day back in the city, which he had left more than 40 days earlier, the governo
body_en:
Uvira DRC January 23, 2026 - Jean Jacques Purusi, governor of South Kivu province, returned to Uvira, the provisional provincial capital, on Friday following the withdrawal of the AFC/M23.
On his first day back in the city, which he had left more than 40 days earlier, the governor delivered a strong message calling for peace, unity, and peaceful coexistence among communities.
“To achieve peace, we must not fall into the enemy’s trap. We must live united; we are all children of the same mother and father,” Governor Purusi declared during a public gathering.
He specifically urged an end to hostile rhetoric against the Banyamulenge and other communities, warning against hate speech and collective punishment.
“Do not fall into the trap of saying, ‘We are going to attack the Banyamulenge, kill them, wound them, or destroy their homes.’ That is the enemy’s strategy. We will find those Banyamulenge families who fled because the enemy contributed to their displacement, because they are our brothers,” he stressed.
The AFC/M23 withdrew from Uvira less than a week ago. Following their departure, the Congolese army and its Wazalendo allies reoccupied the city, allowing state institutions to gradually resume operations.
In addition to the governor, the mayor and several other government officials have also returned to Uvira, marking a step toward the restoration of public administration and stability in the city.

title: Ministry of Finance Defends New Secure License Plates, Denies Opacity and High Costs
excerpt: Kinshasa DRC January 11, 2026 - The Ministry of Finance has rejected allegations surrounding the reform of the vehicle registration system and the introduction of new secure license plates in the Democratic Republic of Congo, insisting that the process is transparent, lawful, and
title_en: Ministry of Finance Defends New Secure License Plates, Denies Opacity and High Costs
excerpt_en: Kinshasa DRC January 11, 2026 - The Ministry of Finance has rejected allegations surrounding the reform of the vehicle registration system and the introduction of new secure license plates in the Democratic Republic of Congo, insisting that the process is transparent, lawful, and
body_en:
Kinshasa DRC January 11, 2026 - The Ministry of Finance has rejected allegations surrounding the reform of the vehicle registration system and the introduction of new secure license plates in the Democratic Republic of Congo, insisting that the process is transparent, lawful, and financially justified.
In a statement, the ministry said it sought to “set the record straight” and counter what it described as confusion and unfounded accusations, reaffirming its commitment to good governance and transparency.
A Reform to Restore Order and Security
According to the ministry, the reform aims to correct serious security flaws and the absence of a clear contractual framework, which had enabled a parallel market to flourish. Authorities reported the circulation of duplicate license plate numbers and the sale of Congolese plates on foreign online platforms.
“Allowing such a situation to continue would have been a grave mistake,” the ministry said, stressing that the reform is intended to restore state authority, strengthen vehicle identification, and protect public finances.
A Relaunched Process After the 2022 Failure
The ministry acknowledged that an earlier project launched in 2022 failed due to technical and legal shortcomings, notably the absence of a required feasibility study and disagreements among potential partners.
The process was subsequently suspended and relaunched under a new legal framework, with approval from the Public Procurement Regulatory Authority (ARMP). Authorities insist this decision was made solely in the public interest.
No Irregular Technical Changes, Government Says
Responding to claims of last-minute technical changes, the ministry said the tender dossier received a no-objection opinion from the Directorate General for Public Procurement Control (DGCMP).
It added that the technical specifications are largely identical to those of the 2022 project and that all three shortlisted companies were invited to submit bids, ensuring equal treatment.
Contract Awarded in Line with Procurement Rules
The ministry denied any opacity or conflict of interest, emphasizing that the project was included in an approved procurement plan and validated by the Prime Minister.
Contrary to some reports, authorities said the contract was awarded through a restricted tender authorized by the DGCMP, not a negotiated procedure. They also noted that the winning bidders were selected before the current Minister of Finance took office.
Clarifying the Cost of License Plates
The ministry rejected claims that the plates cost only $30 to produce, stating that the official price of $65 includes manufacturing, logistics, transport, supplier margins, and system security services.
It also said no private intermediaries are involved in financing and that the share allocated to the public treasury has increased by 14.3%.
The price of license plates, unchanged for more than a decade, has been reduced from $120 to $115, with a further cut to $105 planned for 2027, a move the government says will increase state revenue.
Transition Period and Call for Transparency
Authorities clarified that replacement of old plates is not immediately mandatory and that a one-year transition period is предусмотр, during which old plates remain valid.
The Ministry of Finance said it remains open to audits and dialogue and urged citizens to consult official documents. It called on the public to remain calm and rely on official sources, stating that “access to facts and documents is the best foundation for responsible public debate.”
body_fr:
Kinshasa DRC January 11, 2026 - The Ministry of Finance has rejected allegations surrounding the reform of the vehicle registration system and the introduction of new secure license plates in the Democratic Republic of Congo, insisting that the process is transparent, lawful, and financially justified.
In a statement, the ministry said it sought to “set the record straight” and counter what it described as confusion and unfounded accusations, reaffirming its commitment to good governance and transparency.
A Reform to Restore Order and Security
According to the ministry, the reform aims to correct serious security flaws and the absence of a clear contractual framework, which had enabled a parallel market to flourish. Authorities reported the circulation of duplicate license plate numbers and the sale of Congolese plates on foreign online platforms.
“Allowing such a situation to continue would have been a grave mistake,” the ministry said, stressing that the reform is intended to restore state authority, strengthen vehicle identification, and protect public finances.
A Relaunched Process After the 2022 Failure
The ministry acknowledged that an earlier project launched in 2022 failed due to technical and legal shortcomings, notably the absence of a required feasibility study and disagreements among potential partners.
The process was subsequently suspended and relaunched under a new legal framework, with approval from the Public Procurement Regulatory Authority (ARMP). Authorities insist this decision was made solely in the public interest.
No Irregular Technical Changes, Government Says
Responding to claims of last-minute technical changes, the ministry said the tender dossier received a no-objection opinion from the Directorate General for Public Procurement Control (DGCMP).
It added that the technical specifications are largely identical to those of the 2022 project and that all three shortlisted companies were invited to submit bids, ensuring equal treatment.
Contract Awarded in Line with Procurement Rules
The ministry denied any opacity or conflict of interest, emphasizing that the project was included in an approved procurement plan and validated by the Prime Minister.
Contrary to some reports, authorities said the contract was awarded through a restricted tender authorized by the DGCMP, not a negotiated procedure. They also noted that the winning bidders were selected before the current Minister of Finance took office.
Clarifying the Cost of License Plates
The ministry rejected claims that the plates cost only $30 to produce, stating that the official price of $65 includes manufacturing, logistics, transport, supplier margins, and system security services.
It also said no private intermediaries are involved in financing and that the share allocated to the public treasury has increased by 14.3%.
The price of license plates, unchanged for more than a decade, has been reduced from $120 to $115, with a further cut to $105 planned for 2027, a move the government says will increase state revenue.
Transition Period and Call for Transparency
Authorities clarified that replacement of old plates is not immediately mandatory and that a one-year transition period is предусмотр, during which old plates remain valid.
The Ministry of Finance said it remains open to audits and dialogue and urged citizens to consult official documents. It called on the public to remain calm and rely on official sources, stating that “access to facts and documents is the best foundation for responsible public debate.”

title: DRC Challenges $4 Billion Claim by US Company PayServices
excerpt: Kinshasa/Washington January 14, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is contesting a lawsuit filed by the American firm PayServices, which seeks $4 billion in damages in a US federal court. According to the lawsuit, PayServices alleges it reached an agreement with Congol
title_en: DRC Challenges $4 Billion Claim by US Company PayServices
excerpt_en: Kinshasa/Washington January 14, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is contesting a lawsuit filed by the American firm PayServices, which seeks $4 billion in damages in a US federal court. According to the lawsuit, PayServices alleges it reached an agreement with Congol
body_en:
Kinshasa/Washington January 14, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is contesting a lawsuit filed by the American firm PayServices, which seeks $4 billion in damages in a US federal court.
According to the lawsuit, PayServices alleges it reached an agreement with Congolese public entities to digitize state payments, a project the company claims could have generated over $8 billion annually. The company asserts that the project was never implemented.
The complaint states that initial contacts occurred on December 6, 2023, at the DRC embassy in Washington, D.C., followed by an alleged exclusivity agreement in January 2024 with the Congolese General Savings Bank (CADECO). A payment of $20 million was reportedly expected before March 2024, but was allegedly never released. PayServices claims it attempted mediation before taking legal action.
The lawsuit further alleges breach of contract, pressure tactics, and attempted bribery, citing a supposed €5 million bribe. Several high-ranking officials are named, including the Minister of Portfolio, Julie Mbamubi Shiku; Minister of Finance, Doudou Fwamba Likunde; Chief of Staff to the President, Nkinzo Kamole; Governor of the Central Bank, Andrew Mwema; and CADECO CEO, Mukeba Muntuba.
Kinshasa Denies All Allegations
In a press release dated January 13, 2026, the Congolese Ministry of Portfolio refuted the claims, stating that PayServices never held legal banking status under U.S. law. The release cites a formal decision of the Idaho Department of Finance (October 18, 2024), which revoked all conditional accreditations and prohibited the company from using the term "bank" due to regulatory non-compliance.
The ministry emphasized that administrative checks under the Public Finance Act confirmed that PayServices was neither authorized nor qualified to receive or manage public funds. Consequently, no funds were transferred, and no financial loss occurred. Authorities also noted that no certified financial statements or independent audit were produced to substantiate the company’s claims.
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs stated that the alleged $72 million investment and the supposed contract between PCES Akiba and CADECO are baseless, lacking any legal, budgetary, or accounting foundation. The ministry framed the allegations of corruption and coercion as stemming from Kinshasa’s refusal to pay a company without legal banking status.
DRC Reserves Legal Rights
The statement confirmed that the DRC is cooperating with all competent jurisdictions and reserves the right to pursue legal remedies. The case continues in US courts, where the dispute over PayServices’ banking authority and the alleged damages is ongoing.

title: DRC’s Gécamines to Sell 100,000 Tons of Copper to the US Market
excerpt: Kinshasa/Washington January 14, 2026 - The Congolese state-owned mining company Gécamines announced that it will purchase 100,000 tons of copper from the 2026 production of the Tenke Fungurume Mine (TFM) for direct sale to the US market. According to Gécamines, this marks the fir
title_en: DRC’s Gécamines to Sell 100,000 Tons of Copper to the US Market
excerpt_en: Kinshasa/Washington January 14, 2026 - The Congolese state-owned mining company Gécamines announced that it will purchase 100,000 tons of copper from the 2026 production of the Tenke Fungurume Mine (TFM) for direct sale to the US market. According to Gécamines, this marks the fir
body_en:
Kinshasa/Washington January 14, 2026 - The Congolese state-owned mining company Gécamines announced that it will purchase 100,000 tons of copper from the 2026 production of the Tenke Fungurume Mine (TFM) for direct sale to the US market.
According to Gécamines, this marks the first direct purchase of volumes reserved for the state under one of its mining partnerships, representing 20% of TFM's production, aligned with Gécamines’ stake in the project. The operation is expected to be executed throughout the 2026 fiscal year, in line with provisions of recent agreements between the DRC and the United States.
“This first marketing operation continues our competitive pricing strategy and strengthens the DRC’s position on the global commodities market,” said Guy-Robert Lukama, Chairman of the Board of Gécamines.
CEO Placide Nkala Basadilua added, “This transaction is the culmination of over a year of work to assert the sovereignty of the Congolese state over its natural resources and improve the pricing and taxation of metals produced in the DRC.”
Gécamines highlighted that, since the late 1990s, the marketing of Congolese metals has largely been handled by foreign companies, and that recent competitive bidding processes have led to better prices, increased state revenue, and diversification of buyers.
Looking ahead, Gécamines aims to secure sales rights covering 500,000 tons of copper and 40,000 tons of cobalt. To facilitate this, the company plans to create a trading subsidiary, Gécamines Trading, which will market a portion of production directly. The commodities trading group Mercuria has been selected as a strategic partner, providing financial, logistical, and technical support.
“The creation of Gécamines Trading represents a decisive step for the DRC,” Lukama stated. “It is an instrument of sovereignty, transparency, and resource development for the benefit of the Congolese people.”

title: Artisanal Copper and Cobalt Mining Resumes After Tensions
excerpt: Lualaba, DRC January 15, 2026 - Artisanal mining activities in Lualaba province have resumed following recent clashes between miners and security forces, signaling a return to calm at several mining sites. According to local sources, the entire artisanal mining chain is now opera
title_en: Artisanal Copper and Cobalt Mining Resumes After Tensions
excerpt_en: Lualaba, DRC January 15, 2026 - Artisanal mining activities in Lualaba province have resumed following recent clashes between miners and security forces, signaling a return to calm at several mining sites. According to local sources, the entire artisanal mining chain is now opera
body_en:
Lualaba, DRC January 15, 2026 - Artisanal mining activities in Lualaba province have resumed following recent clashes between miners and security forces, signaling a return to calm at several mining sites.
According to local sources, the entire artisanal mining chain is now operational. Chinese partners, mining cooperatives, and around fifteen processing companies have resumed activities, effectively ending the previous shutdown.
This resumption comes while the commission established by Minister of Mines Louis Watum Kabamba has yet to submit its final report. The commission, headed by Franck Fwamba, is tasked with verifying the legality of companies processing mineral substances from artisanal copper and cobalt mining.
Several institutional actors and stakeholders in Lualaba participated in the commission’s work, including Georges Nyembo Kitungwa, provincial director of SAEMAPE, the provincial director of the Mines Division, Petit Ngombe, and the president of the association of mining cooperatives, alongside representatives of civil society, the provincial government, security services, and other relevant organizations.
Following its visit to Lualaba, the commission is currently meeting in Haut-Katanga province to address similar issues related to artisanal mining there.
While mining activities have resumed, sector stakeholders are awaiting the official conclusions of the mission, which could shape future regulation of artisanal mining in the provinces concerned.

title: President Félix Tshisekedi Highlights DRC as a “Country of Solutions”
excerpt: Davos, Switzerland January 18, 2026 - President Félix Tshisekedi of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) will participate as a guest of honor in the 56th annual meeting of the World Economic Forum (WEF), scheduled from January 19 to 23, 2026. The WEF in Davos, one of the world’
title_en: President Félix Tshisekedi Highlights DRC as a “Country of Solutions”
excerpt_en: Davos, Switzerland January 18, 2026 - President Félix Tshisekedi of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) will participate as a guest of honor in the 56th annual meeting of the World Economic Forum (WEF), scheduled from January 19 to 23, 2026. The WEF in Davos, one of the world’
body_en:
Davos, Switzerland January 18, 2026 - President Félix Tshisekedi of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) will participate as a guest of honor in the 56th annual meeting of the World Economic Forum (WEF), scheduled from January 19 to 23, 2026.
The WEF in Davos, one of the world’s foremost platforms for public-private cooperation, brings together heads of state, business leaders, and civil society representatives to discuss global challenges under the theme: “A Spirit of Dialogue.” This year’s edition expects participation from over 50 world leaders.
According to Tina Salama, spokesperson for President Tshisekedi, the DRC will present itself as a “country of solutions” for Africa and the world. Key areas highlighted include:
Climate solutions, leveraging the DRC’s rich forests and peatlands.
Energy transition, through critical mineral resources and hydroelectric potential.
Human capital, driven by a youthful population of nearly 70%, forming a strategic workforce for AI, technology, and innovation sectors.
The presentation also addresses the security challenges facing the DRC, including Rwandan-backed AFC/M23 rebel occupation in parts of North Kivu and South Kivu, emphasizing mutually beneficial partnerships that respect the country’s sovereignty and contribute to lasting peace.
Organizers of the Forum underscore that the 2026 program will focus on five major global challenges, emphasizing inclusive dialogue, collaboration, and innovation as essential for progress.
Since 1971, the World Economic Forum has served as a platform for geopolitical and economic cooperation, fostering relationships across regions, sectors, and generations to address pressing global issues. Its permanent initiatives continue year-round, translating dialogue into concrete actions.
The WEF is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland, with offices in New York, San Francisco, Beijing, and Tokyo, providing an independent and trusted platform for dialogue and collaboration.

title: Civil Society Gathers to Strengthen Oversight of Mining Revenues
excerpt: Lubumbashi Haut-Katanga, January 24, 2026 - Civil society organizations in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) are stepping up efforts to improve financial governance and transparency in the mining sector. A two-day workshop, held from January 23-24, 2026, brings together memb
title_en: Civil Society Gathers to Strengthen Oversight of Mining Revenues
excerpt_en: Lubumbashi Haut-Katanga, January 24, 2026 - Civil society organizations in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) are stepping up efforts to improve financial governance and transparency in the mining sector. A two-day workshop, held from January 23-24, 2026, brings together memb
body_en:
Lubumbashi Haut-Katanga, January 24, 2026 - Civil society organizations in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) are stepping up efforts to improve financial governance and transparency in the mining sector. A two-day workshop, held from January 23-24, 2026, brings together members of the “Congo Is Not For Sale” (CNPAV) platform and other stakeholders to share best practices in citizen oversight of public fund management.
The workshop focuses on the allocation and management of mining revenues in the provinces of Lualaba, Haut-Uele, and Haut-Katanga, key regions for the DRC’s mineral production. According to Fabien Mayani, a CNPAV steering committee member, the initiative aims to strengthen the ability of civil society to analyze, research, and interact with public authorities, ensuring effective citizen oversight.
“Despite reforms to the mining code and increased revenues from rising mineral prices, poverty remains a pressing reality. Our goal is to ensure that revenues collected by provinces are transparently and effectively managed,” said Mayani.
The workshop highlighted persistent challenges in mining revenue management, including non-compliance with governance rules, lack of transparency, and weak oversight by public bodies. Participants cited EITI data showing that the DRC mobilized over $20 billion in mining revenues between 2018 and 2023, yet questioned how these funds are allocated locally.
“If Haut-Katanga receives $20 million in mining royalties, how are these funds used?” asked Mayani, emphasizing the need for clear reporting and public accountability.
Recommendations emerging from the workshop include:
Strengthening the Court of Auditors and other oversight bodies.
Increasing transparency and public access to financial reports.
Enhancing local authorities’ capacity to mobilize and manage revenue.
Collaborating with the General Inspectorate of Finance (IGF) for better supervision.
Encouraging public accountability, including sanctions for mismanagement.
The CNPAV workshop continues through Saturday, January 24, with organizers aiming to create a structured and effective framework for citizen monitoring of public funds derived from the mining sector.

title: Virunga National Park Welcomes New Mountain Gorilla in Mapuwa Family

excerpt_en: Goma, January 20, 2026 - Virunga National Park announced the birth of a male mountain gorilla to Sebutimbiri, a female in the Mapuwa family. This marks the second birth recorded in the park this year. With this addition, the Mapuwa family now numbers 28 individuals. The birth occ
body_en:
Goma, January 20, 2026 - Virunga National Park announced the birth of a male mountain gorilla to Sebutimbiri, a female in the Mapuwa family. This marks the second birth recorded in the park this year.
With this addition, the Mapuwa family now numbers 28 individuals. The birth occurred in the Mikeno sector, one of the key habitats for mountain gorillas within the park.
The park highlighted the significance of the birth for both social dynamics within gorilla groups and broader conservation programs aimed at supporting this endangered species. International partners, including the European Union and UNESCO, continue to support efforts to protect these primates.
Earlier in January, Virunga National Park reported another milestone: the first twin birth of the year, which occurred on January 3, bringing attention to the park’s ongoing successes in conservation despite challenges.
Virunga National Park, established in 1925 on the border between Rwanda and Uganda, is Africa’s oldest national park and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Covering 7,800 km² in North Kivu province, the park hosts exceptional biodiversity.
The global population of mountain gorillas is estimated at 1,063, with around 350 individuals residing in Virunga, according to 2021 estimates. However, the park faces continued threats from armed clashes between FARDC and AFC/M23 rebels, which endanger both ecosystems and conservation teams.

title: Walikale Faces Severe Shortage of Medicines and Nutritional Products Amid Ongoing Conflict
excerpt: Walikale, North Kivu, January 20, 2026 - Health authorities in Walikale territory are grappling with a critical shortage of medicines and nutritional products, affecting approximately 197,420 residents across Pinga and surrounding health zones. The crisis, exacerbated by the ongo
title_en: Walikale Faces Severe Shortage of Medicines and Nutritional Products Amid Ongoing Conflict
excerpt_en: Walikale, North Kivu, January 20, 2026 - Health authorities in Walikale territory are grappling with a critical shortage of medicines and nutritional products, affecting approximately 197,420 residents across Pinga and surrounding health zones. The crisis, exacerbated by the ongo
body_en:
Walikale, North Kivu, January 20, 2026 - Health authorities in Walikale territory are grappling with a critical shortage of medicines and nutritional products, affecting approximately 197,420 residents across Pinga and surrounding health zones. The crisis, exacerbated by the ongoing conflict between Congolese government forces and the AFC/M23 rebellion, as well as other armed groups, has left local health facilities struggling to provide basic care.
According to a December 2025 UN OCHA report, clashes along the Kalembe-Mpeti-Pinga axis have displaced thousands. On December 6, fighting in Chanjikiro (Kisimba group) triggered mass population movements, while on December 12, residents of Kateku-more than 6,300 people-were forced to flee, seeking refuge in nearby villages such as Kimaka, Miriki, Buleusa, Kayna, and Kanyabayonga.
“This part of the Pinga health zone remains isolated due to physical and security access constraints, limiting the presence and mobility of humanitarian actors,” the report noted. The Pinga General Referral Hospital (HGR) and other local health facilities face acute shortages of essential medicines and nutritional supplies, severely impacting patient care.
OCHA highlighted that the departure of humanitarian partner MEDAIR in April 2025, combined with geographic isolation, has compounded the delivery challenges, leaving residents without consistent medical assistance.
The escalation of violence in North and South Kivu since early 2025 has displaced hundreds of thousands, killed hundreds, and injured thousands, worsening an already dire humanitarian situation. Blocked roads and insecurity continue to hinder aid delivery, despite ongoing efforts by humanitarian organizations to negotiate safe access and provide emergency support.
“The population urgently needs rapid, unimpeded, and safe humanitarian access. All obstacles to aid delivery must be removed,” OCHA emphasized.
Despite high-level mediation initiatives, including the US-led Washington process and Qatar’s role in negotiations with the AFC/M23, on-the-ground conditions remain precarious. Humanitarian and political observers are calling on all parties to uphold their commitments under peace agreements to silence the guns and allow nearly three decades of conflict to end.

title: Four Patients Die in Fire at Masisi General Referral Hospital
excerpt: Masisi, North Kivu, January 20, 2026 - A tragic fire at Masisi General Referral Hospital on the evening of January 19 claimed the lives of four patients, including three children, local medical sources confirmed. According to authorities, the blaze was caused by an electrical mal
title_en: Four Patients Die in Fire at Masisi General Referral Hospital
excerpt_en: Masisi, North Kivu, January 20, 2026 - A tragic fire at Masisi General Referral Hospital on the evening of January 19 claimed the lives of four patients, including three children, local medical sources confirmed. According to authorities, the blaze was caused by an electrical mal
body_en:
Masisi, North Kivu, January 20, 2026 - A tragic fire at Masisi General Referral Hospital on the evening of January 19 claimed the lives of four patients, including three children, local medical sources confirmed.
According to authorities, the blaze was caused by an electrical malfunction. Hospital staff evacuated patients during the night as the fire spread. By the following morning, the hospital had reopened, allowing surviving patients to return to their wards.
The fire caused significant material damage, destroying the hospital’s garage and electrical system. Officials emphasized that the flames were contained before reaching inpatient wards, preventing further casualties.
An official investigation has been launched to determine the exact cause of the incident.

title: Close Associate of Matata Ponyo Transferred to Ndolo Prison After Four Months of Detention
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC, January 11, 2026 - After four months of detention, a close associate of Augustin Matata Ponyo has been transferred to Ndolo Military Prison. The LGD and Allies political coalition announced on Friday the transfer of Professor Pascal Isumbisho Mwapu, political advis
title_en: Close Associate of Matata Ponyo Transferred to Ndolo Prison After Four Months of Detention
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC, January 11, 2026 - After four months of detention, a close associate of Augustin Matata Ponyo has been transferred to Ndolo Military Prison. The LGD and Allies political coalition announced on Friday the transfer of Professor Pascal Isumbisho Mwapu, political advis
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC, January 11, 2026 - After four months of detention, a close associate of Augustin Matata Ponyo has been transferred to Ndolo Military Prison.
The LGD and Allies political coalition announced on Friday the transfer of Professor Pascal Isumbisho Mwapu, political advisor to opposition leader Matata Ponyo, to Ndolo Prison in Kinshasa, after several months of detention at the National Cyber Defense Council (CNC).
In a statement dated January 9, the coalition said the transfer took place on Thursday, January 8, following what it described as “four months of arbitrary and illegal detention” at the CNC. Professor Isumbisho was arrested on September 9, 2025.
LGD and its allies maintain that their founding member is being wrongfully accused of collaborating with the AFC/M23 rebels, accusations they describe as “unfounded and politically motivated.” The coalition denounced what it called “political harassment,” “manipulation of the judicial system,” and the “repression of critical voices.”
The coalition is demanding respect for the rights of the defense, an end to arbitrary detentions, and the “immediate and unconditional release” of Professor Isumbisho, arguing that no legal charges justify his continued detention. It also called on the national and international community and human rights organizations to closely monitor the case.
This development comes amid a realignment of the Congolese opposition. A faction has launched a new political platform, “Save the Democratic Republic of Congo,” led by former President Joseph Kabila.
The platform brings together several opposition figures, including Augustin Matata Ponyo, Franck Diongo, Seth Kikuni, and André Claudel Lubaya, as well as civil society actors. In their final declaration, participants acknowledged the existence of a political and security crisis and called for joint actions in support of national reconciliation.

title: Aubin Minaku, Vice-President of the PPRD, Arrested at His Home
excerpt: Kinshasa, January 18, 2026 - Congolese security forces arrested Aubin Minaku, Vice-President of the People’s Party for Reconstruction and Democracy (PPRD), in the early hours of Sunday morning at his private residence in Kinshasa. The operation was confirmed by several sources cl
title_en: Aubin Minaku, Vice-President of the PPRD, Arrested at His Home
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, January 18, 2026 - Congolese security forces arrested Aubin Minaku, Vice-President of the People’s Party for Reconstruction and Democracy (PPRD), in the early hours of Sunday morning at his private residence in Kinshasa. The operation was confirmed by several sources cl
body_en:
Kinshasa, January 18, 2026 - Congolese security forces arrested Aubin Minaku, Vice-President of the People’s Party for Reconstruction and Democracy (PPRD), in the early hours of Sunday morning at his private residence in Kinshasa.
The operation was confirmed by several sources close to the case, including members of his political entourage and eyewitnesses. The exact reasons for the arrest have not yet been officially disclosed, but the move comes amid rising tensions surrounding figures linked to the former regime of Joseph Kabila.
Mr. Minaku, a former Speaker of the National Assembly and a close ally of the ex-president, was taken to an undisclosed location shortly after midnight. Security sources said the operation proceeded without violence, although the residence was reportedly cordoned off by special forces.
The PPRD has not yet issued an official statement. The arrest follows a series of legal actions targeting former Kabila associates. In recent weeks, Emmanuel Ramazani Shadary, the party’s permanent secretary and unsuccessful candidate in the 2018 presidential election, was also arrested and remains detained at an undisclosed location.
These developments come in the wake of the military court conviction of Joseph Kabila several months ago. The former head of state, now living in exile, was tried in absentia for his alleged role in supporting the AFC/M23 rebellion, which Kinshasa accuses of being backed by Rwanda. Mr. Kabila has been sentenced to death, a verdict his supporters strongly denounce as politically motivated.

title: DRC Ministry of Human Rights Reaffirms Presumption of Innocence in Ilemo Mosengo Nzuzi Case

title_en: DRC Ministry of Human Rights Reaffirms Presumption of Innocence in Ilemo Mosengo Nzuzi Case
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, January 17, 2026 - The Ministry of Human Rights has issued a statement emphasizing the principle of presumption of innocence in the ongoing case of Ilemo Mosengo Nzuzi, which has recently sparked controversy on social media. According to the Ministry, the case has been
body_en:
Kinshasa, January 17, 2026 - The Ministry of Human Rights has issued a statement emphasizing the principle of presumption of innocence in the ongoing case of Ilemo Mosengo Nzuzi, which has recently sparked controversy on social media.
According to the Ministry, the case has been under monitoring by its services since December 20, 2025, and the viral video that circulated on January 14, 2026 is not the trigger for any renewed investigation.
“The liberty of the accused remains a fundamental principle, in accordance with the Constitution, applicable laws, and international human rights standards. Any infringement of this principle constitutes a violation of fundamental rights and freedoms,” the Ministry said in a press release sent to Actualite.CD.

title: Étienne Davignon Faces Hearing in Patrice Lumumba Assassination Case
excerpt: Brussels Belgium, January 20, 2026 - The Brussels Criminal Court held a crucial hearing on Tuesday in the long-standing case surrounding the assassination of Patrice Lumumba, the first Prime Minister of independent Congo. The hearing involved Étienne Davignon, the 93-year-old for
title_en: Étienne Davignon Faces Hearing in Patrice Lumumba Assassination Case
excerpt_en: Brussels Belgium, January 20, 2026 - The Brussels Criminal Court held a crucial hearing on Tuesday in the long-standing case surrounding the assassination of Patrice Lumumba, the first Prime Minister of independent Congo. The hearing involved Étienne Davignon, the 93-year-old for
body_en:
Brussels Belgium, January 20, 2026 - The Brussels Criminal Court held a crucial hearing on Tuesday in the long-standing case surrounding the assassination of Patrice Lumumba, the first Prime Minister of independent Congo. The hearing involved Étienne Davignon, the 93-year-old former Belgian diplomat and industrial strategist, though he was absent from the proceedings.
The hearing marks the first session since the Belgian federal prosecutor requested on June 17-after over a decade of investigation-that Davignon be sent to trial. He faces charges including illegal detention and transfer, violation of the right to a fair trial, and inhuman and degrading treatment inflicted on Lumumba. Charges of attempted murder have not yet been upheld.
Six grandchildren of Patrice Lumumba attended the hearing as civil parties, joining the proceedings to seek accountability for the 1961 assassination of Lumumba, along with Maurice M’Polo and Joseph Okito, in Katanga amidst Cold War tensions and regional secessions.
Davignon, a prominent figure in Belgian diplomacy and politics who later became a European Commissioner and industrial strategist, was stationed in Kinshasa and Brazzaville in the early 1960s. According to prosecutors, his diplomatic position provided him with information regarding Lumumba’s arrest and the conditions of his transfer.
“This is an important step toward redressing a colonial crime,” said Christophe Marchand, lawyer for the Lumumba family, describing the hearing as a “crucial step.”
The reopening of the case follows extensive historical research, particularly by historian Ludo De Witte, who documented Belgian civilian and military involvement in Lumumba’s execution. Davignon is now the last surviving Belgian among the ten individuals named in the 2011 complaint filed by Lumumba’s family for war crimes, torture, and inhumane treatment.
Judicial sources indicate that the case is expected to be adjourned for deliberation, with no decision anticipated for several weeks.

title: Lieutenant General Philémon Yav Rejects Accusations of Treason and Links to Rwanda
excerpt: Kinshasa DRC, January 21, 2026 - Lieutenant General Philémon Yav Irung, former commander of the Third Defense Zone of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), has publicly rejected accusations brought against him by the FARDC’s Auditor General, during a heari
title_en: Lieutenant General Philémon Yav Rejects Accusations of Treason and Links to Rwanda
excerpt_en: Kinshasa DRC, January 21, 2026 - Lieutenant General Philémon Yav Irung, former commander of the Third Defense Zone of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), has publicly rejected accusations brought against him by the FARDC’s Auditor General, during a heari
body_en:
Kinshasa DRC, January 21, 2026 - Lieutenant General Philémon Yav Irung, former commander of the Third Defense Zone of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), has publicly rejected accusations brought against him by the FARDC’s Auditor General, during a hearing at the High Military Court on January 20.
General Yav, whose command covered the strategic provinces of North Kivu, South Kivu, Ituri, Maniema, and Tshopo, faces serious charges, including treason and inciting soldiers to act against duty and discipline, stemming from alleged contacts with Rwandan officials. The accusations date back nearly three years to his arrest in September 2022.
During the hearing, General Yav insisted that he had never received any message from Rwandan officials containing a plot against the country, contrary to claims made by the prosecution. He acknowledged receiving a message from an unknown number but said its content differed entirely from what prosecutors allege and that it was related only to the FDLR, not any plan involving Rwanda’s James Kabarebe.
“I declare that I have never heard of this before. The message the prosecutor is wrongly accusing me of, I did not receive. I never saw it on my phone,” General Yav told the court.
The defense also raised procedural objections, citing lack of jurisdiction, arbitrary arrest, violation of dignity, and irregular reports. While the court deemed the objections admissible, it ruled them unfounded, ordering the investigation to continue.
General Yav, nicknamed “The Tiger”, is among several officers from Greater Katanga whose alleged marginalization under President Félix Tshisekedi has been a point of political contention. The Congolese army maintains that tribal affiliation has no bearing on military service and that all interrogations and arrests are conducted in accordance with military law, according to spokesperson Sylvain Ekenge.
This trial marks a pivotal moment in a high-profile case, highlighting ongoing tensions within the DRC military and allegations of foreign interference in the eastern provinces.

excerpt: Kinshasa DRC, January 21, 2026 - Following his transfer to Ndolo Military Prison, young political activist Nathanaël Onokomba appeared before a magistrate of the High Military Court of Kinshasa/Gombe on Wednesday. According to his lawyer, Godefroid Mwanabwato, the hearing marked
title_en: Political Opponent Nathanaël Onokomba Appears Before High Military Court
excerpt_en: Kinshasa DRC, January 21, 2026 - Following his transfer to Ndolo Military Prison, young political activist Nathanaël Onokomba appeared before a magistrate of the High Military Court of Kinshasa/Gombe on Wednesday. According to his lawyer, Godefroid Mwanabwato, the hearing marked
body_en:
Kinshasa DRC, January 21, 2026 - Following his transfer to Ndolo Military Prison, young political activist Nathanaël Onokomba appeared before a magistrate of the High Military Court of Kinshasa/Gombe on Wednesday.
According to his lawyer, Godefroid Mwanabwato, the hearing marked the first time Onokomba was formally questioned by the court after his detention.
“We assisted our client this morning. He was finally brought before a magistrate of the High Military Court of Kinshasa/Gombe and questioned in the presence of his lawyers,” Mwanabwato said.
The lawyer emphasized irregularities surrounding his arrest, calling for the annulment of official reports Onokomba was allegedly forced to sign under pressure and alleged torture at the National Cyber Defense Council.
The hearing primarily focused on Onokomba’s opinions expressed in public media, particularly a tweet that paraphrased the Washington Agreement. Onokomba clarified that the tweet reflected a satirical interpretation rather than a personal statement.
He also requested provisional release, with his lawyers arguing that he poses no flight risk and that the charges against him relate solely to his exercise of constitutionally guaranteed freedoms as an unarmed civilian.
“There is no flight risk, and even the charges against him, an unarmed civilian, stem from his individual and personal opinions, in the exercise of the rights and freedoms guaranteed to him by the Constitution,” declared Judge Mwanabwato.
The case underscores growing concerns about the treatment of political opponents and freedom of expression in the DRC, particularly amid ongoing tensions surrounding the implementation of international agreements.

title: Three Police Officers Sentenced for Inciting Theft in Viral Song Case
excerpt: Kinshasa, January 22, 2026 - Three police officers, Sindani, Kabamba, and Kiadi, authors of the controversial song “Zua ye tshombo tika ye akende” (“Take his phone and let him go”), have been sentenced to three years of hard labor by the Kinshasa/Ndjili Garrison Military Court. T
title_en: Three Police Officers Sentenced for Inciting Theft in Viral Song Case
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, January 22, 2026 - Three police officers, Sindani, Kabamba, and Kiadi, authors of the controversial song “Zua ye tshombo tika ye akende” (“Take his phone and let him go”), have been sentenced to three years of hard labor by the Kinshasa/Ndjili Garrison Military Court. T
body_en:
Kinshasa, January 22, 2026 - Three police officers, Sindani, Kabamba, and Kiadi, authors of the controversial song “Zua ye tshombo tika ye akende” (“Take his phone and let him go”), have been sentenced to three years of hard labor by the Kinshasa/Ndjili Garrison Military Court. The officers were also ordered to pay court costs of 200,000 Congolese francs.
The sentencing follows a summary hearing on Tuesday, January 20, 2026, in which the court examined the conduct of five officers from the Congolese National Police (PNC) implicated in the case.
The court found Sindani, Kabamba, and Kiadi guilty of insubordination, citing the viral video as evidence. In the footage, several visibly intoxicated officers performed the song in unison outside a Kinshasa police station, prompting national outrage.
One officer, Kasongo, was acquitted of failing to report a crime due to insufficient evidence, while another, Tuzolana, received a suspended sentence of twelve months of hard labor for the same offense.
According to observers on social media, the song highlighted what many perceive as lax recruitment and discipline practices within the police force, raising concerns over officers who are entrusted with public protection but sometimes act as perpetrators of abuse.
The ruling serves as a rare instance of accountability for police misconduct in the DRC, sending a signal that public incitement to criminal acts by law enforcement personnel will not be tolerated.

excerpt_en: Masisi-Walikale, DRC - January 11, 2026 - AFC/M23 rebels have reinforced their positions with fighters and ammunition in Kasopo and Kazinga, located in the Osso Banyungu chiefdom, Masisi territory, North Kivu, on January 9, 2026. Local sources report that these reinforcements cam
body_en:
Masisi-Walikale, DRC - January 11, 2026 - AFC/M23 rebels have reinforced their positions with fighters and ammunition in Kasopo and Kazinga, located in the Osso Banyungu chiefdom, Masisi territory, North Kivu, on January 9, 2026.
Local sources report that these reinforcements came from Nyabiondo and Masisi town, following a regrouping in Kaandja village, a strategic crossroads between Kasopo, Kazinga, and Kashebere.
The move comes one week after clashes resumed between rebel forces and government troops, supported by Wazalendo, in the Katoy sector, where rebels lost several villages.
Traditional leaders of Nyamabiko 1 and 2 (Masisi) and Waloa Yungu (Walikale) have expressed concern over a potential rebel offensive, urging FARDC and Wazalendo forces to remain vigilant.
The reinforcements, particularly in areas hosting displaced populations, indicate that the rebels may be preparing to retake lost territories, intensifying insecurity in North Kivu.

title: DRC Moves to Establish Steering Committee for Washington Accords Implementation
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - January 11, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is taking steps to implement the Washington Accords, signed under the auspices of the Trump administration on December 4, 2025. Prime Minister Judith Suminwa announced at the Council of Ministers meeting on
title_en: DRC Moves to Establish Steering Committee for Washington Accords Implementation
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - January 11, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is taking steps to implement the Washington Accords, signed under the auspices of the Trump administration on December 4, 2025. Prime Minister Judith Suminwa announced at the Council of Ministers meeting on
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - January 11, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is taking steps to implement the Washington Accords, signed under the auspices of the Trump administration on December 4, 2025. Prime Minister Judith Suminwa announced at the Council of Ministers meeting on January 9, 2026, that she had convened a working session on January 8 with ministers responsible for executing these accords.
The session aimed to establish a government-level framework to streamline projects and ensure implementation in line with the President’s policy. A steering committee will be created to develop a roadmap to coordinate government actions and monitor commitments under the accords.
Prime Minister Suminwa also plans to meet with the expanded Economic Situation Committee on January 13, 2026, to harmonize actions and clarify clauses in the agreements.
The Washington Accords, described as historic, reaffirm the DRC-Rwanda peace agreement of June 27, 2025, and aim to foster economic cooperation, regional integration, and lasting peace. They include the Regional Economic Integration Framework (REIF) and multiple bilateral instruments with the United States, including the Strategic Partnership Agreement, the Enhanced Security Partnership, and the US-Rwanda Framework for Shared Economic Prosperity.
Despite government support, the accords face criticism within the DRC. Archbishop Fulgence Muteba Mugalu of Lubumbashi criticized the agreements as a potential “sell-off”, warning that they could sacrifice national development and compromise the future of the Congolese people.

Local sources reported that the Wazalendo attacked rebel positions beginning at 6:00 a.m., with heavy and light weapons fire heard throughout the area. Observers suggest the attack may be intended to preempt a rebel offensive on positions held by government forces and Wazalendo in the Nyamaboko 1 and 2 groups.
This confrontation comes just two days after AFC/M23 reinforced positions in Kazinga and Kasopo, a move previously denounced by local traditional authorities. The situation remains tense, according to local sources.

excerpt_en: Bukama, January 12, 2026 - An attack attributed to suspected Bakata Katanga militiamen left at least eight people dead on Sunday, January 11, in the territory of Bukama, Haut-Lomami province. According to local authorities, six militiamen and two civilians were killed, while seve
body_en:
Bukama, January 12, 2026 - An attack attributed to suspected Bakata Katanga militiamen left at least eight people dead on Sunday, January 11, in the territory of Bukama, Haut-Lomami province.
According to local authorities, six militiamen and two civilians were killed, while several others were wounded during clashes that erupted as FARDC reinforcements were passing through a public area near a market. Civilians were reportedly struck by stray bullets during the exchange of fire.
The clashes lasted for about one hour, involving soldiers who had just arrived from the Kamina military base and armed elements linked to the Bakata Katanga movement. Another FARDC reinforcement unit, composed of around 60 soldiers, was also targeted.
Authorities indicated that military reinforcements were deployed not only in Bukama but also in other territories of Haut-Lomami, including Kabongo, following rising insecurity. Information about the troop movements is believed to have circulated in advance, contributing to the ambush.
The army later confirmed the attack on one of its units, identifying the assailants as members of a group calling itself Mai-Mai Zulu, and reported four militiamen killed and one soldier wounded.

body_en:
Sake, January 12, 2026 - Residents of Sake, in the Kamuronza group (Masisi territory) of North Kivu, are alarmed by a sharp rise in insecurity in this town located about 27 km west of Goma.
Between Monday, January 5, and Thursday, January 8, at least four people were killed. The latest incident occurred on Wednesday evening when armed attackers shot dead two people during a raid in Kimoka, near Sake. A man and his child were reportedly killed by assailants suspected of belonging to the AFC/M23 rebels, who control the area.
According to local accounts, the attackers stormed the family home, shot the victims, looted valuables, and fled while firing into the air.
This attack came just two days after another deadly incident in the same town that left three victims-two dead and one wounded-bringing the total death toll to four in four days. Residents continue to attribute these killings to AFC/M23 fighters.
Faced with this alarming security situation, the population of Sake is calling for urgent reinforcement of security measures in the rebel-held area.

body_en:
Masisi, January 12, 2026 - The villages of Humura and Rutoboko, in the Nyamaboko 1 group (Osso Banyungu sector) of Masisi territory, North Kivu, have been abandoned by residents following clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and the Wazalendo.
Residents began fleeing on Sunday, January 11, after fighting erupted near Kazinga. Fearing for their safety, families moved toward the Waloa Yungu group in Walikale territory.
Several displaced families arrived in Langira and Chumba on Sunday evening and Monday. Many are being sheltered by host families, while others have taken refuge in schools and churches.
According to information from the ground, the humanitarian situation is critical, as most people fled without their belongings. The displaced are urgently appealing for food assistance and temporary shelter to protect them from the elements.

body_en:
Fizi, Monday, January 12, 2026 - Another boat navigating Lake Tanganyika was intercepted on Sunday, January 11, by the FARDC and the Wazalendo in Fizi, South Kivu. The vessel, Super Bus, was reportedly en route to Bujumbura for repairs.
A patrol stopped the boat shortly after it departed from the private port of Kivovo, with 12 crew members on board. It was intercepted by army maritime services and the Wazalendo while patrolling near Makobola.
This interception comes just days after another vessel, Okako 2, was stopped in the village of Mizimu, also in Fizi territory.
Since the capture of Uvira by AFC/M23 rebels, several measures have been implemented to restrict movement in the region, including a ban on traffic between South Kivu and Tanganyika Province via Lake Tanganyika.
In the context of the ongoing conflict between AFC/M23 rebels and the Congolese army, any vessel operating on Lake Tanganyika is now treated with heightened suspicion.

title: DRC Government Humanitarian Mission Moves to Tanzania
excerpt: Dar es Salaam, January 12, 2026 - The humanitarian mission of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) arrived in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, on Sunday, January 11, marking the second leg of its regional tour after Burundi. The delegation is led by Ève Bazaiba Masudi, Minister of Stat
title_en: DRC Government Humanitarian Mission Moves to Tanzania
excerpt_en: Dar es Salaam, January 12, 2026 - The humanitarian mission of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) arrived in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, on Sunday, January 11, marking the second leg of its regional tour after Burundi. The delegation is led by Ève Bazaiba Masudi, Minister of Stat
body_en:
Dar es Salaam, January 12, 2026 - The humanitarian mission of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) arrived in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, on Sunday, January 11, marking the second leg of its regional tour after Burundi. The delegation is led by Ève Bazaiba Masudi, Minister of State in charge of Social Affairs, Humanitarian Action and National Solidarity, and Crispin Mbadu Phanzu, Minister Delegate for Francophonie and the Diaspora.
The mission follows decisions of the Council of Ministers after the occupation of Uvira in South Kivu by the AFC/M23, supported by Rwanda. Its objectives include delivering humanitarian assistance to Congolese refugees in Kigoma, strengthening coordination with Tanzanian and Burundian authorities, and mobilizing international partners in response to the regional humanitarian crisis.
Ève Bazaiba noted that more than 67,000 Congolese had already received assistance at the Busuma site in Burundi, calling it an act of national solidarity. She emphasized that the delegation’s mission is to bring comfort, hope, and moral support to displaced compatriots in Burundi and Tanzania, while working for the return of peace.
Despite the difficult living conditions in displacement camps, she stressed that the Congolese government will spare no effort to support its citizens and remains fully committed to the Doha and Washington peace processes. “Every minute that passes worsens the suffering, not only for Congolese people but also for host communities, the region, and the world,” she said.
The humanitarian situation in Burundi continues to deteriorate following intensified fighting between the AFC/M23 and Congolese government forces in eastern DRC, particularly after the fall of Uvira. These clashes have caused mass displacement, despite the rebels’ announced withdrawal.
The situation has reached a critical threshold, with a massive influx of refugees and asylum seekers fleeing violence in South Kivu. Since early December, more than 84,000 people have crossed into Burundi, bringing the total number of Congolese refugees and asylum seekers there to over 200,000. Transit centers and informal settlements are severely overcrowded, some reaching nearly 200% capacity, plunging hundreds of families into extreme vulnerability. Shortages of clean water, sanitation, shelter, food, and medicine heighten the risk of cholera and other life-threatening diseases.
To ease pressure, the Burundian government has designated a new reception site in Bweru, in Ruyigi Buhumuza province, where nearly 21,000 refugees have been transferred. However, conditions remain harsh, with many families still sleeping outdoors due to a lack of adequate shelter.
Across the border in South Kivu, ongoing violence, drone strikes, and bombings have forced more than 500,000 people to flee their homes, many of them multiple times this year. Dozens of schools have been turned into overcrowded shelters, and the first cholera cases have been reported. Persistent insecurity continues to restrict humanitarian access, limiting the ability of aid workers to reach populations in acute distress.
This humanitarian deterioration comes amid controversy surrounding the announced AFC/M23 withdrawal from Uvira, which Congolese authorities view as an attempt to divert attention and reduce international pressure, particularly on Kigali, considered the main supporter of the rebellion. On the ground, the AFC/M23 continues to consolidate its control, establishing a parallel administration beyond the authority of Kinshasa.
The fall of Uvira, a strategic city in South Kivu, has strengthened the rebellion’s grip on both North and South Kivu, raising fears of a potential advance toward Greater Katanga, regarded as the economic heartland of the DRC.

title_en: AFC/M23 Defends Achievements and Calls for Preservation of Gains
excerpt_en: Doha, January 13, 2026 - The AFC/M23 has reaffirmed its commitment to a peaceful resolution of the conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), highlighting the progress achieved under the Doha peace process and urging that these gains be preserved. In correspondence a
body_en:
Doha, January 13, 2026 - The AFC/M23 has reaffirmed its commitment to a peaceful resolution of the conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), highlighting the progress achieved under the Doha peace process and urging that these gains be preserved.
In correspondence addressed to the Chairperson of the African Union, Corneille Nangaa Yobeluo, Political Coordinator of the AFC/M23, acknowledged messages conveyed through Angola under the leadership of João Lourenço. He praised Angola’s mediation efforts and underscored the importance of the negotiations conducted in Doha, under the auspices of Qatar, with the active involvement of the African Union, the United States, and other partners.
Nangaa recalled that since March 30, 2024, both the Congolese government and the AFC/M23 have been fully engaged in a negotiation process aimed at addressing the root causes of the conflict through political dialogue.
Five Major Agreements Cited
According to Nangaa, the Doha framework has enabled the signing of five major instruments, described as “structuring and irreversible” milestones in the peace process:
Joint Communiqué - April 24, 2025
Declaration of Principles - July 19, 2025
Mechanism for the Release of Detainees - September 10, 2025
Ceasefire Monitoring and Verification Mechanism - October 14, 2025
Doha Framework Agreement for a Comprehensive Peace Agreement - November 15, 2025
He stressed that these agreements represent concrete and recognized progress, achieved through consistent and professional mediation.
Call to Preserve the Doha Framework
Nangaa emphasized that peace processes are inherently complex and require time, patience, and trust-building, arguing that every step forward is a valuable asset that must be protected. He insisted that the Doha agreements should be treated as fundamental and irreversible achievements requiring full implementation and consolidation.
He further noted that neither party has denounced the Doha framework and that both the Congolese government and the AFC/M23 remain formally committed to the process, alongside mediators working toward a comprehensive and lasting peace.
Regional Diplomacy and Ongoing Tensions
The correspondence comes amid renewed diplomatic activity involving Angola, following several meetings between President Félix Tshisekedi and President João Lourenço, who currently chairs the African Union. While these engagements have fueled speculation about a new diplomatic initiative, no official confirmation has been made.
This dynamic unfolds against a backdrop of continued tension between Kinshasa and Kigali, despite the ratification of agreements under the Washington process by Presidents Tshisekedi and Paul Kagame. Mutual accusations persist over alleged failures to honor commitments.
Similarly, the Doha talks, intended to complement the Washington agreements by addressing core issues such as the restoration of state authority and the reintegration of armed groups, are facing difficulties in translating into tangible improvements on the ground. This diplomatic stagnation continues to fuel ongoing clashes between the AFC/M23 and Congolese government forces.

title: Socio-Economic Activities Paralyzed by General Strike
excerpt: Butembo, January 13, 2026 - Socio-economic activities were largely paralyzed in Butembo, North Kivu, following a general strike called by a coalition of citizen movements and pressure groups to denounce persistent insecurity in the city. From early morning, tensions were reported
title_en: Socio-Economic Activities Paralyzed by General Strike
excerpt_en: Butembo, January 13, 2026 - Socio-economic activities were largely paralyzed in Butembo, North Kivu, following a general strike called by a coalition of citizen movements and pressure groups to denounce persistent insecurity in the city. From early morning, tensions were reported
body_en:
Butembo, January 13, 2026 - Socio-economic activities were largely paralyzed in Butembo, North Kivu, following a general strike called by a coalition of citizen movements and pressure groups to denounce persistent insecurity in the city.
From early morning, tensions were reported in the northern districts, particularly in Furu, where tires were burned and barricades were erected, disrupting traffic. Along Boulevard Président de la République, most shops remained closed, and banks suspended operations, serving only a limited number of clients.
Schools and universities were also closed, with no students in attendance. Many parents kept their children at home due to fears of unrest. Only a few students who went to school were later sent back.
In some peripheral neighborhoods, including Rughenda, Mutiri, Vuhira, and Katwa, activities continued at a reduced pace, despite the strike call.
Organizers said the protest aims to demand the removal of the mayor of Butembo, the reinstatement of the police commissioner, the relocation of Wazalendo positions in and around the city, and the opening of independent investigations to ensure justice for victims of insecurity.
They cited ongoing assassinations, armed robberies, home burglaries, and human rights violations, accusing local authorities of ineffectiveness. Protesters also called for stronger measures to remove armed and untrained individuals from the city.
The strike comes amid a deteriorating security situation. In recent days, two civilians and a police officer were killed in separate incidents. Although authorities have announced a ban on armed Wazalendo in the city, critics say the measure has had little impact, as these groups remain present and view themselves as allies of the army.

title: Sexual Violence Used as Weapon of War by Armed Groups

title_en: Sexual Violence Used as Weapon of War by Armed Groups
excerpt_en: Eastern DRC, January 14, 2026 - A recent report reveals that sexual violence is being systematically employed as a weapon of war in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. The violence has been committed by members of at least five non-state armed groups, including the AFC/M23, as
body_en:
Eastern DRC, January 14, 2026 - A recent report reveals that sexual violence is being systematically employed as a weapon of war in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. The violence has been committed by members of at least five non-state armed groups, including the AFC/M23, as well as by soldiers of the Congolese army.
According to the report, survivors of these crimes face a climate of impunity and a health system insufficiently equipped to provide support. Investigations conducted in November 2025 included interviews with 23 survivors in northeastern DRC and four refugees in Uganda.
Authorities and humanitarian actors, including provincial health and justice officials, were consulted, but responses from responsible parties, including the Congolese government and leaders of the M23, were reportedly absent.
The findings underscore the urgent need for accountability, protection of civilians, and support for survivors amid ongoing conflict in the region.

body_en:
Masisi, January 14, 2026 --A relative calm returned Wednesday morning, January 14, 2026, in Kalembe, located in the Bashali Mokoto group of Masisi territory, North Kivu, following overnight clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and the Wazalendo.
Reports indicate that the Wazalendo launched simultaneous attacks around 8:00 p.m., aiming to dislodge the rebels from the town they have occupied for over a year. Loud explosions from heavy weapons were heard, forcing many to remain indoors. The human toll from these clashes is currently unknown.
The town continues to host several displaced families fleeing insecurity in surrounding areas. Recent weeks in the Kalembe region have seen repeated clashes, causing mass displacement and looting of residents’ property, with the most recent major incident reported on December 24, 2025.

title_en: Rusamambu and Buleusa Receive New Displaced Families After Fighting in Kalonge
excerpt_en: Walikale, January 14, 2026 -Fresh waves of displacement have been reported in Walikale territory, North Kivu, as residents flee renewed clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters of the Coalition of Movements for Change (CMC). Since Monday, January 12, population movem
body_en:
Walikale, January 14, 2026 -Fresh waves of displacement have been reported in Walikale territory, North Kivu, as residents flee renewed clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters of the Coalition of Movements for Change (CMC).
Since Monday, January 12, population movements have intensified following fighting in Mulema locality, within the Kisimba group. As a result, residents of Kalonge have sought refuge in Rusamambu and Buleusa, both located in the neighboring Ikobo group, while Kalonge itself remains under AFC/M23 control.
This new displacement wave further deepens the humanitarian crisis in the area, where communities have already been severely affected by prolonged insecurity since the occupation of parts of the Wanianga sector by the rebels.
Local authorities have issued urgent appeals to humanitarian organizations to provide emergency assistance to the displaced families, many of whom fled without belongings, food, or shelter.
Meanwhile, the local population movement monitoring committee has begun registering newly displaced households, adding to those who have been living in the area without aid since February 2025, highlighting the growing strain on host communities and already limited resources.
