title: Confederation of Sahel States Opens First Confederal Council of Ministers Session in Bamako
excerpt: Bamako, December 20, 2025 - The first confederal session of the Council of Ministers of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES) officially opened on Saturday, December 20, 2025, at the Koulouba Palace in Bamako, under the chairmanship of General Assimi Goïta, President of Mali’s
title_en: Confederation of Sahel States Opens First Confederal Council of Ministers Session in Bamako
excerpt_en: Bamako, December 20, 2025 - The first confederal session of the Council of Ministers of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES) officially opened on Saturday, December 20, 2025, at the Koulouba Palace in Bamako, under the chairmanship of General Assimi Goïta, President of Mali’s
body_en:
Bamako, December 20, 2025 - The first confederal session of the Council of Ministers of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES) officially opened on Saturday, December 20, 2025, at the Koulouba Palace in Bamako, under the chairmanship of General Assimi Goïta, President of Mali’s Transition, Head of State, and President of the AES Confederation.
Following the opening ceremony, proceedings continued at the Bamako International Conference Center, where ministerial work is being conducted under the leadership of Major General Abdoulaye Maïga, Prime Minister and Head of Government of Mali.
This landmark confederal session brings together ministers from Burkina Faso, Mali, and Niger for strategic consultations aimed at strengthening the institutional and operational foundations of the newly established Confederation of Sahel States.
Held over two days, the meeting serves as a preparatory step for the second ordinary session of the College of Heads of State of the AES. Ministers are expected to examine several key documents, including:
A draft report on the implementation of the first-year Roadmap of the Confederation;
A draft report on the state of discussions between the AES and ECOWAS;
Draft legal instruments designed to enhance the effectiveness and cohesion of the Confederation.
Presidents Captain Ibrahim Traoré of Burkina Faso and General Abdourahamane Tiani of Niger are expected in Bamako for this high-level gathering, which will culminate in the second session of the College of Heads of State.
The upcoming session will provide an opportunity to assess progress in defense, diplomacy, and development, while outlining new strategic directions to respond to the aspirations of the peoples of the Sahel for peace, security, and shared prosperity.

title: Mali Reaffirms Commitment to Strategic Russia-Africa Partnership at Cairo Ministerial Forum
excerpt: Cairo, December 19, 2025 - Mali has reiterated its commitment to a strategic Russia-Africa partnership grounded in sovereignty, mutual respect, and shared development during the 2nd Ministerial Conference of the Russia-Africa Partnership Forum, held in Cairo. The high-level meeti
title_en: Mali Reaffirms Commitment to Strategic Russia-Africa Partnership at Cairo Ministerial Forum
excerpt_en: Cairo, December 19, 2025 - Mali has reiterated its commitment to a strategic Russia-Africa partnership grounded in sovereignty, mutual respect, and shared development during the 2nd Ministerial Conference of the Russia-Africa Partnership Forum, held in Cairo. The high-level meeti
body_en:
Cairo, December 19, 2025 - Mali has reiterated its commitment to a strategic Russia-Africa partnership grounded in sovereignty, mutual respect, and shared development during the 2nd Ministerial Conference of the Russia-Africa Partnership Forum, held in Cairo.
The high-level meeting, a key milestone in preparations for the Russia-Africa Summit scheduled for 2026, brought together African and Russian officials to strengthen political, economic, and strategic cooperation within a framework described as balanced and mutually beneficial.
In its address, the Malian delegation expressed gratitude to the Arab Republic of Egypt for hosting the conference and to the Russian Federation for what it described as a sustained commitment to a sincere and respectful partnership with African states.
Mali highlighted the forum’s role as a platform for strategic dialogue based on respect for state sovereignty and the pursuit of collective responses to global challenges, against the backdrop of an evolving international order marked by the transition toward multipolarity.
Within this context, Mali underscored Africa’s growing role as a full-fledged global actor, advancing its own visions and proposals. The delegation welcomed the convergence between BRICS principles and African aspirations for greater political, economic, and cultural autonomy.
Addressing ongoing security challenges in the Sahel, Mali recalled the creation of the Confederation of Sahel States (CES), uniting Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger. The initiative was presented as a historic step to reinforce regional solidarity, strengthen the fight against terrorism, and promote an endogenous development model rooted in collective responsibility and sovereignty.
The Mali-Russia partnership was described as a central pillar of Malian foreign policy. In 2025, the two countries marked the 65th anniversary of diplomatic relations, with cooperation deepening across key sectors including security, energy, education, and economic development, yielding tangible outcomes and long-term structural projects.
In conclusion, Mali reaffirmed its full support for the Russia-Africa Partnership, viewing it as a crucial lever for building a fairer, more stable international order that respects state sovereignty. The forum was hailed as a gateway to enhanced cooperation and shared prosperity between Russia and Africa.

The opening ceremony was presided over by General Assimi Goïta, President of Mali’s Transition and current President of the ESA, in the presence of Captain Ibrahim Traoré, President of Burkina Faso, and General Abdourahamane Tiani, President of Niger, underscoring the unity and shared political commitment of the three member states.
The high-level gathering brought together the Prime Minister of Mali, members of the confederal governments, heads of Malian state institutions, former President Dioncounda Traoré, ambassadors accredited to Mali, as well as the President and members of the National Transitional Council (CNT).
In his address, President Ibrahim Traoré praised the resilience and mobilization of Sahelian peoples in the face of what he described as persistent external threats. He called for heightened vigilance and solidarity to safeguard sovereignty gains, warning against a broader regional destabilization project he referred to as a looming “black winter.”
For his part, President Abdourahamane Tiani recalled that the creation of the Confederation of Sahel States on July 6, 2024, in Niamey, marked a historic turning point for the region. He welcomed the progress achieved under Mali’s presidency, citing the establishment of the ESA Unified Force, strengthened confederal diplomatic coordination, and the creation of the Confederation’s Investment Bank.
In his opening speech, President Assimi Goïta reviewed the key achievements of his presidency, structured around three pillars: defense and security, diplomacy, and development. He highlighted the reinforcement of the Unified Force and the growing international recognition of the Confederation.
Goïta also emphasized major ongoing and upcoming projects, including the ESA Investment Bank, the Confederal Central Purchasing Office (currently under construction), and the official launch of AES Television, presented as a strategic tool for information sovereignty. Additional projects under discussion include the creation of a confederal airline, a trans-Saharan highway, and an inter-confederation railway, aimed at deepening integration and connectivity.
Following the session’s deliberations, the Heads of State officially inaugurated the Confederal Investment and Development Bank (BCID-ESA), a key financial institution designed to support strategic investments, strengthen economic sovereignty, and promote sustainable development across the Confederation. The ceremony included a ribbon-cutting and a tour of the facilities in the presence of senior officials from the three countries.
On the sidelines of the summit, President Ibrahim Traoré was welcomed in Bamako by President Assimi Goïta at Modibo Keïta-Sénou International Airport. The two leaders held a closed-door meeting before jointly visiting the headquarters of AES Television, symbolizing the Confederation’s drive toward sovereignty, integration, and coordinated communication.

title: Second Session of the AES College of Heads of State: Bamako at the Center of Confederal Momentum
excerpt: Bamako, December 22-23, 2025 - Bamako hosted the second session of the College of Heads of State of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES) on December 22 and 23, 2025, marking a decisive stage in the consolidation of the political, security, and economic integration process betw
title_en: Second Session of the AES College of Heads of State: Bamako at the Center of Confederal Momentum
excerpt_en: Bamako, December 22-23, 2025 - Bamako hosted the second session of the College of Heads of State of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES) on December 22 and 23, 2025, marking a decisive stage in the consolidation of the political, security, and economic integration process betw
body_en:
Bamako, December 22-23, 2025 - Bamako hosted the second session of the College of Heads of State of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES) on December 22 and 23, 2025, marking a decisive stage in the consolidation of the political, security, and economic integration process between Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger.
The high-level confederal meeting opened against a backdrop of strong popular mobilization and heightened regional security challenges, underscoring the strategic importance of the AES project for the future of the Sahel.
Arrival of the Heads of State and Popular Mobilization
The confederal sequence began on Monday, December 22, 2025, with the arrival in Bamako of General Abdourahamane Tiani, President of the Republic of Niger. He was received at President Modibo Keïta-Sénou International Airport by General Assimi Goïta, President of Mali’s Transition, Head of State, and President of the AES Confederation.
Following a brief private meeting at the presidential pavilion, the two heads of state traveled together to Koulouba Palace. Along the route, large crowds gathered to welcome them, expressing visible support for the confederation project. On several occasions, the presidents stopped their convoy to greet citizens, creating moments of direct interaction marked by enthusiasm and popular fervor.
On Tuesday, December 23, Captain Ibrahim Traoré, President of Burkina Faso, arrived in Bamako to take part in the proceedings. He was also welcomed at the airport by President Assimi Goïta. After a closed-door meeting at the presidential pavilion, the two leaders visited the headquarters of AES Television, presented as a flagship symbol of informational sovereignty and confederal integration.
Inauguration of the Confederal Bank for Investment and Development
One of the highlights of the session was the official inauguration of the Confederal Bank for Investment and Development (BCID-AES) on December 23, 2025, in Bamako. The ceremony was presided over by President Assimi Goïta, in the presence of President Abdourahamane Tiani and President Ibrahim Traoré, as well as senior political and administrative officials from the three member states.
Designed as a strategic financial instrument, the BCID-AES aims to finance structuring projects, promote sustainable development, strengthen economic sovereignty, and support the transformation of the economies of Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger. The inauguration featured the traditional ribbon-cutting ceremony followed by a tour of the facilities, highlighting the confederation’s ambition to build autonomous financial mechanisms.
Official Opening of the College of Heads of State
Later the same day, President Assimi Goïta presided over the official opening ceremony of the second session of the College of Heads of State of the AES at the Bamako International Conference Center (CICB).
The ceremony brought together the Presidents of Burkina Faso and Niger, the Prime Minister of Mali, members of the confederal governments, heads of Malian state institutions, former President Dioncounda Traoré, ambassadors accredited to Mali, the President of the National Transitional Council (CNT), and members of the CNT.
Strong Political Messages and Strategic Orientations
In his address, President Ibrahim Traoré praised the mobilization and resilience of Sahelian populations in the face of external pressures and security threats. He called for vigilance and unity to protect the gains of independence and sovereignty, warning against what he described as a “black winter”-a destabilization agenda targeting West Africa and the Sahel.
President Abdourahamane Tiani recalled that the creation of the Confederation of Sahel States on July 6, 2024, in Niamey, marked a historic turning point for the region. He welcomed the progress achieved under Mali’s leadership of the Confederation, particularly the establishment of the Unified Force, strengthened confederal diplomatic coordination, and the operationalization of the Confederation’s Investment Bank.
In his keynote address, President Assimi Goïta reviewed his presidency of the AES, structured around three core pillars: defense and security, diplomacy, and development. He highlighted the reinforcement of the AES Unified Forces, as well as the growing international visibility and recognition of the Confederation.
The Malian head of state also emphasized major confederal projects, including the Confederal Investment Bank, the Confederal Purchasing Center currently under construction, and the launch of AES Television, described as a strategic tool to ensure information sovereignty.
Looking ahead, President Goïta outlined ambitious integration projects under consideration, such as the creation of a confederal airline, the construction of a trans-Sahelian highway, and the establishment of an inter-confederal railway network, all aimed at strengthening connectivity, economic integration, and regional solidarity.
Toward a Sovereign and Integrated Sahel
At the conclusion of the opening ceremony, the three heads of state reaffirmed their shared commitment to building a sovereign, united, and prosperous Sahel, capable of responding collectively to security challenges and advancing endogenous development models rooted in cooperation and mutual support.
The second session of the AES College of Heads of State thus confirmed Bamako’s central role in the confederal dynamic and marked a new phase in the institutional consolidation of the Confederation of Sahel States.

title: AES College of Heads of State Adopts Motion of Support Amid Terrorism and Sovereignty Challenges
excerpt: Bamako, December 23, 2025 - The College of Heads of State of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES) has adopted a motion of support reaffirming its unity and determination in the face of persistent security threats and what it describes as external attempts to undermine the sove
title_en: AES College of Heads of State Adopts Motion of Support Amid Terrorism and Sovereignty Challenges
excerpt_en: Bamako, December 23, 2025 - The College of Heads of State of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES) has adopted a motion of support reaffirming its unity and determination in the face of persistent security threats and what it describes as external attempts to undermine the sove
body_en:
Bamako, December 23, 2025 - The College of Heads of State of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES) has adopted a motion of support reaffirming its unity and determination in the face of persistent security threats and what it describes as external attempts to undermine the sovereignty of the Sahelian bloc.
Meeting in Bamako on the margins of the second session of the College of Heads of State, the leaders of Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger expressed deep concern over the continuation of multifaceted terrorist acts targeting the Confederation since its establishment. According to the motion, these attacks are aimed at weakening a sovereign political project founded on solidarity, collective security, and endogenous development for the peoples of the Sahel.
Condemnation of Terrorism and External Support
In a strongly worded statement, the College of Heads of State denounced what it described as a dangerous escalation marked by the open involvement and support of foreign states accused of sponsoring destabilization efforts. The leaders stated that such actions have crossed an “unacceptable threshold of indignity,” threatening not only individual member states but the Confederation as a whole.
The AES leadership condemned in the strongest terms all acts of subversion directed against the Republic of Mali, emphasizing that these attacks constitute an assault on the collective security and political cohesion of the entire Confederation of Sahel States.
Support for Niger in Uranium Dispute
The motion also addressed economic and legal challenges facing member states, particularly Niger, which the College says is being subjected to judicial harassment by the French company ORANO. According to the statement, this legal action is linked to Niger’s sovereign management of its uranium resources.
The AES Heads of State described this dispute as an attempt to instrumentalize judicial mechanisms in order to maintain control over strategic mineral resources. They characterized such practices as outdated forms of economic domination, incompatible with the principles of sovereignty and self-determination defended by the Confederation.
Reaffirmation of Sovereignty and Collective Resolve
In response to these security, political, and economic pressures, the College of Heads of State reaffirmed its total and unwavering support for the peoples of the Sahel. The leaders praised their resilience, dignity, and courage in the face of terrorism, external pressure, and economic challenges.
The motion reiterated the Confederation’s firm determination to defeat terrorism, strengthen collective defense mechanisms, and fully exercise sovereign control over natural resources, ensuring that they are managed exclusively in the interest of Sahelian populations.
Call for Unity and International Solidarity
Concluding the motion, the College of Heads of State expressed gratitude to peoples and nations around the world that have shown solidarity with the Sahel. The leaders also congratulated the citizens of the AES member states for their steadfastness in the face of adversity.
Finally, the motion called on Sahelian populations to further strengthen their commitment, mobilization, and cohesion, stressing that unity remains essential to confronting any threat to the sovereignty, stability, and future of the Confederation of Sahel States.
The adoption of this motion underscores the AES’s intention to present a united political front, combining security, economic sovereignty, and popular resilience as pillars of its long-term vision for the Sahel.

title: Second Ordinary Session of the AES College of Heads of State Concludes in Bamako with Major Decisions on Security, Sovereignty, and Integration
excerpt: Bamako, December 23, 2025 - The Second Ordinary Session of the College of Heads of State of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES) concluded on Tuesday in Bamako, marking a decisive milestone in the consolidation of the confederal project uniting Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger. T

excerpt_en: Bamako, December 23, 2025 - The Second Ordinary Session of the College of Heads of State of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES) concluded on Tuesday in Bamako, marking a decisive milestone in the consolidation of the confederal project uniting Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger. T
body_en:
Bamako, December 23, 2025 - The Second Ordinary Session of the College of Heads of State of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES) concluded on Tuesday in Bamako, marking a decisive milestone in the consolidation of the confederal project uniting Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger. The session was held under the chairmanship of General Assimi Goïta, President of the Transition of Mali and outgoing President of the AES.
The meeting brought together Captain Ibrahim Traoré, President of Burkina Faso, and General Abdourahamane Tiani, President of the Republic of Niger. The Heads of State conducted an in-depth review of the political, security, economic, and institutional situation of the Confederation, as well as the level of implementation of decisions adopted since its creation.
Validation of Ministerial Work and Strategic Roadmap
The College welcomed the Summary of Conclusions of the First Confederal Council of Ministers, held on December 20-21, 2025, in Bamako. The opening ceremony of that session was chaired by General Assimi Goïta, while the substantive work was led by Major General Abdoulaye Maïga, Prime Minister of Mali. The Heads of State commended the quality of the document and approved its recommendations.
They also examined and endorsed:
The General Report on the implementation of the AES Year-One Roadmap;
The Synthesis Report on negotiations between AES and ECOWAS.
Strengthening the Institutional Foundations of the Confederation
The College praised the leadership of President Assimi Goïta for the effective implementation of the decisions adopted during the first AES summit held on July 6, 2024, in Niamey, and for advancing the Confederation’s first-year roadmap.
Significant progress was acknowledged in strengthening the identity, visibility, and international recognition of AES, notably through:
The adoption of a flag, logo, anthem, and motto;
The issuance of confederal identity and travel documents;
The launch of AES Television and Radio;
The establishment of the Confederal Investment and Development Bank (BCID-AES), which is set to become fully operational.
On telecommunications, the College urged ministers to accelerate measures facilitating intra-AES communications and connectivity with neighboring states.
Adoption of Key Legal Instruments
To consolidate the three strategic pillars of the Confederation-security, diplomacy, and development-the College adopted several Additional Protocols to the AES Treaty, covering:
Defense and security cooperation;
Coordination of diplomatic action;
Coordination of development policies;
Organization of confederal parliamentary sessions.
The Council of Ministers was instructed to ensure effective implementation of these instruments.
Security, Terrorism, and Geopolitical Challenges
The Heads of State strongly condemned terrorist attacks targeting AES member states, denouncing the involvement of foreign state sponsors, including actors within the region. They reaffirmed their unwavering unity, solidarity, and mutual assistance, emphasizing that any aggression against one member state constitutes an attack against the entire Confederation.
The College also condemned:
Economic and media warfare;
Disinformation campaigns;
Judicial manipulation aimed at undermining AES states and seizing their natural resources.
Ministers were instructed to counter these actions through coordinated communication strategies and the dissemination of reliable, official information.
The Heads of State commended the joint operations of the defense and security forces, noting a significant reduction in terrorist operational capacity. They also welcomed the official presentation of the flag to the Unified Forces of the AES (UF-AES), marking their formal entry into service.
In the legal domain, justice ministers were encouraged to strengthen judicial cooperation within the Confederation and with external partners, in line with AES sovereignty and regional realities.
Diplomatic Coordination and International Positioning
The College highlighted the emergence of AES as a major geopolitical actor in the sub-region. It welcomed the growing practice of pre-consultations before international meetings, enabling the Confederation to speak with one voice and support the candidacies of its member states within international organizations.
Foreign ministers were encouraged to deepen cooperation between diplomatic missions and consular services, while the AES diaspora was recognized as a strategic partner in development and international advocacy.
Development, Economic Sovereignty, and Integration
The Heads of State welcomed progress in economic integration, particularly:
The implementation of the AES Contribution Mechanism (PC-AES);
The creation of the BCID-AES as a tool for endogenous and sustainable financing.
They called for accelerated harmonization of economic policies, including customs, mining, transport, industry, and investment frameworks, as well as the free movement of people and goods.
The College reaffirmed strong support for member states exercising full sovereignty over natural resources, condemning legal harassment linked to such sovereign decisions. Youth and women were identified as central actors in building a resilient and inclusive economic model.
Relations with ECOWAS
The College took note of progress in consultations with ECOWAS and approved the conclusions of the May 22, 2025 meeting in Bamako between AES foreign ministers and the President of the ECOWAS Commission. The Heads of State reiterated their commitment to good-faith negotiations, prioritizing the interests of West African peoples bound by historic ties.
Leadership Transition and Future Outlook
In a key decision, the College appointed Captain Ibrahim Traoré, President of Burkina Faso, as President of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES) for a one-year term.
In his inaugural address, President Traoré paid tribute to General Assimi Goïta’s leadership and outlined the priority areas for the AES’s second-year roadmap, emphasizing continuity, security consolidation, economic sovereignty, and deeper integration.
General Assimi Goïta, in his closing remarks, thanked his peers for their trust and support and congratulated President Traoré on assuming the confederal presidency.
Closing and Acknowledgements
The Heads of State agreed that the next AES summit would be held on a date to be determined through diplomatic channels. Presidents Traoré and Tiani expressed their deep gratitude to the Government and people of Mali for their hospitality and for the successful organization of the session.
The Bamako summit reaffirmed the AES’s ambition to evolve toward a federative framework, anchored in sovereignty, solidarity, and shared prosperity for the peoples of the Sahel.

title: Mali Applies Reciprocity Principle in Response to U.S. Entry Restrictions
excerpt: Bamako, December 30, 2025 The Government of Mali has announced the application of the principle of reciprocity in response to new entry restrictions imposed by the United States on Malian nationals, according to a statement released by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Internat
title_en: Mali Applies Reciprocity Principle in Response to U.S. Entry Restrictions
excerpt_en: Bamako, December 30, 2025 The Government of Mali has announced the application of the principle of reciprocity in response to new entry restrictions imposed by the United States on Malian nationals, according to a statement released by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Internat
body_en:
Bamako, December 30, 2025
The Government of Mali has announced the application of the principle of reciprocity in response to new entry restrictions imposed by the United States on Malian nationals, according to a statement released by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation.
The Ministry said it had taken note of the U.S. decision, announced on December 16, 2025, to tighten conditions for Malian citizens seeking to enter the United States. Malian authorities expressed regret that the measure was adopted without prior consultation, describing it as a far-reaching decision taken unilaterally.
Bamako also rejected the security justification cited by Washington, arguing that it does not reflect the current realities on the ground nor the efforts undertaken by Mali to ensure national and regional security. According to the statement, the government considers the decision unjustified, unfounded, and lacking a factual basis, suggesting that its true motivations lie beyond the stated security concerns.
In response, the Ministry announced that, with immediate effect, Mali will apply the same entry requirements to U.S. citizens as those now imposed on Malian nationals by American authorities, in line with international diplomatic practice.
Despite the dispute, the Ministry reaffirmed Mali’s commitment to maintaining balanced, constructive, and mutually respectful relations with all its international partners, while insisting on respect for Mali’s sovereignty and equal treatment of its citizens.
The move marks a further escalation in diplomatic tensions between Bamako and Washington, amid broader shifts in Mali’s foreign policy posture in recent years.

title: Mali Suspends Entry of U.S. Nationals, Announces Limited Exemptions
excerpt: Koulouba, January 2, 2026 The Government of Mali has clarified the implementation of its recent decision concerning the entry of United States nationals into Malian territory, following its press release issued on December 30, 2025, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Internation
title_en: Mali Suspends Entry of U.S. Nationals, Announces Limited Exemptions
excerpt_en: Koulouba, January 2, 2026 The Government of Mali has clarified the implementation of its recent decision concerning the entry of United States nationals into Malian territory, following its press release issued on December 30, 2025, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Internation
body_en:
Koulouba, January 2, 2026
The Government of Mali has clarified the implementation of its recent decision concerning the entry of United States nationals into Malian territory, following its press release issued on December 30, 2025, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation announced.
In a new statement released from Koulouba, the Malian authorities confirmed that, in line with the principle of reciprocity, the entry of U.S. nationals into the Republic of Mali has been fully suspended, subject to a limited number of exceptions.
According to the Ministry, the suspension does not apply to the following categories:
U.S. citizens who are permanent residents of Mali;
U.S. nationals holding a valid Malian visa;
Specific categories of U.S. citizens, including diplomats, athletes, and any individual whose presence in Mali serves duly established national interests.
The government emphasized that this decision is part of a broader diplomatic response to recent restrictions imposed by the United States on Malian nationals, which Bamako considers unilateral and unjustified.
The Ministry further stated that the measure will be regularly and appropriately reviewed, depending on developments in bilateral relations and the broader diplomatic context. Any changes to the policy will be officially communicated through established government channels.
This clarification comes amid heightened diplomatic tensions between Mali and the United States, as Bamako increasingly asserts its sovereignty and demands equal treatment for its citizens in international relations.

title: Mali-Japan Bilateral Cooperation: TOKTEN Program at the Center of Strategic Exchanges
excerpt: Bamako, December 30, 2025 The Minister for Malians Living Abroad and African Integration, Mossa Ag Attaher, on Tuesday received His Excellency Yukuo Murata, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Japan to Mali, for high-level discussions focused on strengthening bilatera
title_en: Mali-Japan Bilateral Cooperation: TOKTEN Program at the Center of Strategic Exchanges
excerpt_en: Bamako, December 30, 2025 The Minister for Malians Living Abroad and African Integration, Mossa Ag Attaher, on Tuesday received His Excellency Yukuo Murata, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Japan to Mali, for high-level discussions focused on strengthening bilatera
body_en:
Bamako, December 30, 2025
The Minister for Malians Living Abroad and African Integration, Mossa Ag Attaher, on Tuesday received His Excellency Yukuo Murata, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Japan to Mali, for high-level discussions focused on strengthening bilateral cooperation between Mali and Japan.
The Japanese Ambassador was accompanied by Dr. Oussouby Sacko, a Malian architect based in Japan and Executive Director of the Universities of Tokyo, whose presence highlighted the growing role of the Malian diaspora in fostering academic, technical, and development cooperation between the two countries.
At the heart of the discussions was the TOKTEN Program (Transfer of Knowledge Through Expatriate Nationals), an initiative supported by Japan that aims to mobilize skilled professionals from the diaspora to contribute to development efforts in their countries of origin. The program enables highly qualified expatriates to temporarily return home to share expertise in key sectors such as education, technology, urban planning, governance, and innovation.
Minister Mossa Ag Attaher praised Japan’s continued commitment to human capital development and emphasized the strategic importance of the Malian diaspora in national reconstruction and sustainable development. He reaffirmed the government’s determination to create favorable conditions that encourage skilled Malians abroad to actively participate in the country’s transformation.
Ambassador Murata, for his part, reiterated Japan’s willingness to deepen cooperation with Mali, particularly in areas related to capacity building, higher education, and technical expertise transfer. He highlighted the TOKTEN program as a practical and effective framework for strengthening people-to-people ties and promoting mutually beneficial cooperation.
Dr. Oussouby Sacko underscored the importance of academic collaboration and innovation, noting that partnerships between Malian institutions and Japanese universities could significantly contribute to training a new generation of skilled professionals capable of addressing Mali’s development challenges.
The meeting reflects the shared ambition of Bamako and Tokyo to reinforce their bilateral partnership through knowledge exchange, diaspora engagement, and sustainable development initiatives, positioning the TOKTEN program as a key instrument in this cooperation.

excerpt_en: Bamako, December 23, 2025 - AES The Confederal Investment and Development Bank of the Confederation of Sahel States (BCID-AES) was officially inaugurated on Tuesday, December 23, 2025, in Bamako, marking a major step in the implementation of the strategic vision of the AES Confed
body_en:
Bamako, December 23, 2025 - AES
The Confederal Investment and Development Bank of the Confederation of Sahel States (BCID-AES) was officially inaugurated on Tuesday, December 23, 2025, in Bamako, marking a major step in the implementation of the strategic vision of the AES Confederation, which brings together Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger.
The inauguration ceremony was held under the joint chairmanship of General Assimi Goïta, President of the Transition of Mali and President of the Confederation of Sahel States; General Abdourahamane Tiani, President of the Republic of Niger; and Captain Ibrahim Traoré, President of Burkina Faso. Their presence underscored the political unity and shared commitment of the three Sahelian states to building a sovereign and integrated economic space.
Conceived as a key financial pillar of the Confederation, the BCID-AES is designed to mobilize endogenous resources and provide sustainable financing for large-scale, high-impact projects across the AES area. Its mandate includes the financing of strategic infrastructure, support for productive sectors, and the promotion of economic integration among member states.
The Bank will prioritize investments in transport and regional connectivity, energy, agriculture and food security, industrial development, and support to private enterprises, with a particular focus on projects that generate employment and strengthen resilience in the Sahel.
By creating the BCID-AES, the Heads of State reaffirmed their determination to reduce dependence on external financing mechanisms, strengthen economic sovereignty, and lay the foundations for inclusive and sustainable development driven by the needs and aspirations of Sahelian populations.
The inauguration of the BCID-AES represents a structuring milestone in the confederal project and positions the Confederation of Sahel States as a proactive actor in shaping its own development trajectory through solidarity, cooperation, and strategic investment.

title: Media | Young Journalists Network Training Workshop Officially Opens at AMAP
excerpt: Bamako, December 26, 2025 The Young Journalists Network training workshop officially opened on December 26 at the Malian Press and Advertising Agency (AMAP), marking a significant step in promoting responsible and inclusive journalism among children and young people in Mali. The
title_en: Media | Young Journalists Network Training Workshop Officially Opens at AMAP
excerpt_en: Bamako, December 26, 2025 The Young Journalists Network training workshop officially opened on December 26 at the Malian Press and Advertising Agency (AMAP), marking a significant step in promoting responsible and inclusive journalism among children and young people in Mali. The
body_en:
Bamako, December 26, 2025
The Young Journalists Network training workshop officially opened on December 26 at the Malian Press and Advertising Agency (AMAP), marking a significant step in promoting responsible and inclusive journalism among children and young people in Mali.
The opening ceremony was presided over by Mohamed Ag Albachar, Chief of Staff of the Ministry of Communication, Digital Economy, and Administrative Modernization, representing the Minister, Alhamdou Ag Ilyène. His presence highlighted the government’s commitment to strengthening media capacity and fostering ethical journalism from an early age.
Organized by AMAP, with the technical support of UNICEF and financial backing from Germany (BMZ) and Canada, the workshop is part of the “Children and Media” project. It brings together 17 young aspiring journalists for an intensive training program running from December 26 to 29, 2025.
Over the course of four days, participants will receive hands-on training in journalistic techniques, video editing, and media coverage of climate change, key areas identified as essential for addressing contemporary information challenges. The objective is to equip young journalists with practical skills while fostering critical thinking, ethical standards, and a strong sense of social responsibility.
In his address, Mohamed Ag Albachar underlined the strategic importance of investing in youth training to build a new generation of journalists committed to professionalism, accuracy, and ethics. He commended the strong partnership between AMAP and UNICEF, recalling the decisive support provided by the UN agency during AMAP’s relaunch activities in October 2025.
Speaking on behalf of UNICEF, Abdoulaye Guèye, Acting Deputy Representative of the organization in Mali, emphasized the value of children’s active participation, as well as the principles of diversity and inclusion within the Young Journalists Network. He called on mentors and trainers to fully assume their role as role models and custodians of journalistic ethics, guiding young participants toward responsible media practices.
For his part, the Director General of AMAP stressed the crucial role of journalism in shaping societies, noting that early training in responsible information production is essential in a context marked by misinformation and rapid digital transformation. He reaffirmed AMAP’s commitment to supporting initiatives that empower young voices and promote quality journalism.
A particularly moving moment of the ceremony was the testimony of a former child journalist, now a professional at ORTM, who shared his personal journey and highlighted the lasting impact of the program on his career path. His experience illustrated the long-term value of investing in youth media education.
This training workshop forms part of a broader national effort to promote children’s expression, value their perspectives, and strengthen citizen journalism as a tool for social cohesion, civic engagement, and the future development of Mali’s media landscape.

excerpt: Bamako, December 23, 2025 The Heads of State of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES) officially inaugurated AES Television on Tuesday, December 23, 2025, in Bamako, marking a major step in the development of a sovereign confederal media platform serving the Sahel region. The c
title_en: Media | Confederation of Sahel States Launches AES Television in Bamako
excerpt_en: Bamako, December 23, 2025 The Heads of State of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES) officially inaugurated AES Television on Tuesday, December 23, 2025, in Bamako, marking a major step in the development of a sovereign confederal media platform serving the Sahel region. The c
body_en:
Bamako, December 23, 2025
The Heads of State of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES) officially inaugurated AES Television on Tuesday, December 23, 2025, in Bamako, marking a major step in the development of a sovereign confederal media platform serving the Sahel region.
The ceremony was led by Captain Ibrahim Traoré, President of Burkina Faso; General Assimi Goïta, President of the Transition of Mali and President of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES); and General Abdourahamane Tiani, President of the Republic of Niger. It was attended by the Prime Minister of Mali, the President of the National Transitional Council, members of the government, and administrative and municipal authorities of the Bamako District.
During the event, the Heads of State cut the ribbon, officially launching the pilot phase of AES Television, followed by a guided tour of the channel’s technical and administrative facilities.
The Minister of Communication, Digital Economy, and Administrative Modernization of Mali, Alhamdou Ag Ilyène, took part in the ceremony alongside his counterparts from Burkina Faso and Niger, reflecting the joint nature of the project.
The creation of AES Television, initiated by the Ministry of Communication, Digital Economy, and Administrative Modernization of Mali in close coordination with the communication ministries of Burkina Faso and Niger, underscores the collective commitment of the three member states. The project benefited from high-level political support from the President of the Confederation, General Assimi Goïta, whose leadership helped bring this strategic initiative to fruition.
Positioned as a key instrument for institutional communication and regional integration, AES Television aims to serve the peoples of the Sahel and Africa, as well as broader audiences committed to freedom, equality, and progress. The channel seeks to promote the values of solidarity, sovereignty, and resilience, provide reliable and balanced information, support confederal public policies, and strengthen cohesion among the peoples of the Sahel and Southern Africa.
The inauguration, held on the sidelines of the 2nd College of Heads of State of the Confederation of Sahel States, illustrates the determination of AES leaders to advance political, economic, and security integration through the establishment of sovereign media serving the interests and aspirations of the region’s populations.

title: Mali Secures Waiver of Port Penalties for Cargo at Dakar Port
excerpt: Bamako, December 29, 2025 The President of the Malian Shippers’ Council (CMC) has announced that a waiver of port penalties-including demurrage, warehousing, and container detention fees-has been granted to Malian importers and freight forwarders using the Autonomous Port of Daka
title_en: Mali Secures Waiver of Port Penalties for Cargo at Dakar Port
excerpt_en: Bamako, December 29, 2025 The President of the Malian Shippers’ Council (CMC) has announced that a waiver of port penalties-including demurrage, warehousing, and container detention fees-has been granted to Malian importers and freight forwarders using the Autonomous Port of Daka
body_en:
Bamako, December 29, 2025
The President of the Malian Shippers’ Council (CMC) has announced that a waiver of port penalties-including demurrage, warehousing, and container detention fees-has been granted to Malian importers and freight forwarders using the Autonomous Port of Dakar (Senegal).
According to the CMC, the measure was obtained from Senegalese port authorities following a ministerial mission to Senegal held from November 18 to 21, 2025, and is formalized under Note No. 002492-PAD dated November 25, 2025. The decision is part of ongoing efforts to support Malian shippers facing logistical and financial constraints.
As of December 22, 2025, significant progress has been made in clearing Malian cargo stored at DP World Dakar:
Initial stock (November 26, 2025): 2,086 containers
Remaining stock (December 22, 2025): 939 containers
The Malian Shippers’ Council has urged owners of the remaining goods to immediately proceed with their removal, noting that the list of concerned cargo is available at the CMC. The Council has also reaffirmed its readiness to assist importers and freight forwarders throughout the clearance process.
However, the CMC issued a firm warning, reiterating that the three-month deadline for cargo release-set to expire on February 20, 2026-is final and non-negotiable. No extension will be granted beyond this date, the statement emphasized.
The announcement, signed in Bamako on December 24, 2025, was officially published on December 29, 2025, with the Chairman of the Malian Shippers’ Council thanking stakeholders for their cooperation and understanding.

excerpt: Bamako, December 29, 2025 The 14th ordinary session of the Board of Directors of the National Institute for Vocational Training in Building, Transport, and Public Works (INFP/BTP) was held on Monday, December 29, 2025, in Bamako, with a strong focus on institutional performance a
title_en: INFP/BTP Board Holds 14th Ordinary Session, Reviews 2025 Performance and 2026 Budget
excerpt_en: Bamako, December 29, 2025 The 14th ordinary session of the Board of Directors of the National Institute for Vocational Training in Building, Transport, and Public Works (INFP/BTP) was held on Monday, December 29, 2025, in Bamako, with a strong focus on institutional performance a
body_en:
Bamako, December 29, 2025
The 14th ordinary session of the Board of Directors of the National Institute for Vocational Training in Building, Transport, and Public Works (INFP/BTP) was held on Monday, December 29, 2025, in Bamako, with a strong focus on institutional performance and strategic planning for 2026.
The opening of the session was chaired by the Minister of Transport and Infrastructure, in his capacity as Chairman of the Board of Directors of the INFP/BTP. Senior officials, board members, and technical staff of the institute took part in the meeting.
Several key issues were on the agenda, including:
Assessment of the implementation of recommendations adopted during the previous Board session;
Presentation, review, and adoption of the 2025 activity report, highlighting achievements, challenges, and lessons learned in vocational training for the building, transport, and public works sectors;
Examination of the draft budget for the 2026 financial year, aimed at strengthening training capacity, improving infrastructure, and aligning programs with national development priorities.
During the discussions, emphasis was placed on the performance of the institute, the relevance of its training programs to labor market needs, and the role of vocational education in supporting national infrastructure development and employment creation.
Board members also underlined the importance of efficient resource management, enhanced governance, and the continued modernization of training tools and curricula in order to better prepare skilled professionals for the construction, transport, and public works sectors.
The session concluded with commitments to reinforce the implementation of adopted recommendations and to ensure that the 2026 budget effectively supports the INFP/BTP’s mission of developing a qualified workforce aligned with Mali’s economic and infrastructure ambitions.

body_en:
Timbuktu, December 27, 2025
Ms. Oumou Sall Seck, Minister of National Entrepreneurship, Employment, and Vocational Training, and President of the Trait d’Union Movement, led a masterclass on the National Charter for Peace and National Reconciliation at the Ahmed Baba Institute.
The session brought together a high-level audience including regional governors, prominent figures, senior civil servants, administrative and traditional authorities, as well as community representatives, women, and youth from various districts of Timbuktu and from Taoudéni.
In her address, Minister Sall Seck highlighted the importance of endogenous mechanisms for conciliation and mediation as the cornerstone for building a sincere, lasting, and authentically Malian peace. The masterclass served as both a platform for discussion and capacity-building, reinforcing the principles of reconciliation, social cohesion, and national unity in the region.
This initiative reflects the government’s commitment to promoting local solutions for peace and reconciliation, ensuring that cultural legitimacy and community involvement are central to the process of restoring and sustaining peace in Mali.

title_en: 2025 Public Debate Highlights Skills Coordination Among Malians as Minister Attends Diby Festival
excerpt_en: Bamako, December 29, 2025 As part of activities marking the 2025 public debate on the coordination of skills among Malian citizens, the Minister for Malians Living Abroad and African Integration, Mossa Ag Attaher, on Monday December 29, 2025, attended the Diby Festival in Bamako.
body_en:
Bamako, December 29, 2025
As part of activities marking the 2025 public debate on the coordination of skills among Malian citizens, the Minister for Malians Living Abroad and African Integration, Mossa Ag Attaher, on Monday December 29, 2025, attended the Diby Festival in Bamako.
The Diby Festival is a major cultural event celebrating meat cuisine, a cornerstone of Malian culinary heritage. The festival brings together chefs, cultural actors, and citizens around traditional cooking practices, highlighting gastronomy as both a cultural identity marker and an economic opportunity.
The minister’s presence at the event underscored the government’s commitment to promoting Malian know-how (savoir-faire), cultural industries, and the contribution of citizens-both at home and abroad-to national development and social cohesion.
In a related cultural highlight, the “Timbuktu 2025” Arts and Culture Biennial officially came to a close, marking the end of one of Mali’s most significant cultural gatherings. The Bougouni region was crowned overall champion of this edition, which was held under the patronage of the Prime Minister.
The biennial showcased artistic expression, cultural diversity, and creativity from across the country, reinforcing the role of culture as a driver of unity, resilience, and national pride amid ongoing challenges.

The Timbuktu 2025 Biennale of Arts and Culture, held under the theme “Culture, a Pillar of Building the New Mali,” officially came to an end on December 28, 2025, following ten days of artistic and cultural competitions.

The event brought together senior government officials, including the Minister of Crafts, Culture, Hospitality and Tourism, Mamou Daffé, as well as regional governors and numerous national authorities.

The conclusion of the Timbuktu 2025 Biennale marked a significant moment in Mali’s cultural calendar, reinforcing the government’s commitment to promoting arts and culture as drivers of cohesion, resilience, and sustainable development.

title_en: Bamako Hosts Workshop on Drivers’ Collective Bargaining Agreement and Worker Rights
excerpt_en: Bamako, December 26, 2025 A sensitization workshop for transport operators, drivers, and truck drivers opened on Friday, December 26, 2025, at the Bamako International Conference Center (CICB). The session was presided over by Mr. Fassoun Coulibaly, Minister of Labor, Public Serv
body_en:
Bamako, December 26, 2025
A sensitization workshop for transport operators, drivers, and truck drivers opened on Friday, December 26, 2025, at the Bamako International Conference Center (CICB). The session was presided over by Mr. Fassoun Coulibaly, Minister of Labor, Public Service, and Social Dialogue, and attended by Colonel-Major Assa Badiallo Touré, Minister of Health and Social Development.
The workshop aimed to raise awareness among employers and workers in the transport sector about the importance of complying with the drivers’ collective bargaining agreement. Key objectives included:
Ensuring that drivers and truck drivers are registered with the INPS (National Social Security Institute).
Promoting adherence to the AMO (Mandatory Health Insurance) requirements.
Highlighting the legal and social responsibilities of employers and employees in the sector.
By combining regulatory guidance with practical advice, the initiative represents a significant step toward improving road safety, workers’ rights, and social protection for transport sector employees in Mali.

title: Mali Drives Economic Sovereignty with Fisheries Expansion and Judicial Reform
excerpt: Mali, December 2025 Mali is accelerating initiatives to strengthen economic sovereignty and social development. At the 4th Fisheries Days, authorities unveiled a comprehensive plan aimed at increasing the fisheries sector’s contribution to the national economy to over 4% of GDP,
title_en: Mali Drives Economic Sovereignty with Fisheries Expansion and Judicial Reform
excerpt_en: Mali, December 2025 Mali is accelerating initiatives to strengthen economic sovereignty and social development. At the 4th Fisheries Days, authorities unveiled a comprehensive plan aimed at increasing the fisheries sector’s contribution to the national economy to over 4% of GDP,
body_en:
Mali, December 2025
Mali is accelerating initiatives to strengthen economic sovereignty and social development. At the 4th Fisheries Days, authorities unveiled a comprehensive plan aimed at increasing the fisheries sector’s contribution to the national economy to over 4% of GDP, despite ongoing climate challenges. Key measures include:
Modernization of the cold chain to reduce post-harvest losses.
Support for women’s cooperatives, ensuring their active participation in the sector and bolstering food security.
In parallel, a major judicial reform has been launched with the creation of a specialized unit for land law. This initiative aims to:
Resolve protracted land disputes more efficiently.
Digitize the land registry for faster and more transparent access to property information.
To strengthen the justice system further, Mali has launched a competitive examination for magistrates, targeting the recruitment of 140 new magistrates, thus investing in the next generation of legal professionals.
At the regional level, the Alliance of Sahel States (AES) is accelerating industrial integration from Niamey, with a focus on:
Local procurement to promote regional value chains.
Securing logistics corridors to stabilize prices and enhance trade efficiency.
Through these efforts-economic recovery, judicial modernization, and youth development-Mali is charting a path toward sustainable, sovereign growth and greater regional integration.

Kayes, December 26, 2025
On Friday, December 26, 2025, JNIM announced that it had taken full control of a Malian army barracks in Sandaré, located in the Kayes region.
The Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) reported that the assault was carried out by a coordinated armed group comprising JNIM, the Azawad Liberation Front (FLA), and Katibat Ansar Dine of Macina (KAEM). The attack began at 2:02 p.m. and targeted the Sandaré garrison.
According to a statement from the Chief of Staff of the Malian Armed Forces (CEMEGA):
“Faced with the vigorous response of the Malian Armed Forces, the enemy attempted to retreat, leaving behind dead, wounded, and equipment.”
The incident highlights the persistent threat posed by organized extremist groups in the Kayes region, despite military efforts to secure key installations. Local authorities are reportedly assessing the damage and casualties from the engagement.

title: FAMa Neutralize Terrorist Groups Across Multiple Operational Theaters
excerpt: Bamako - December 30, 2025 ; The General Staff of the Armed Forces has released the operational results of the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) for December 30, 2025, reporting a series of successful operations against armed terrorist groups across several regions of the country. In th
title_en: FAMa Neutralize Terrorist Groups Across Multiple Operational Theaters
excerpt_en: Bamako - December 30, 2025 ; The General Staff of the Armed Forces has released the operational results of the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) for December 30, 2025, reporting a series of successful operations against armed terrorist groups across several regions of the country. In th
body_en:
Bamako - December 30, 2025 ; The General Staff of the Armed Forces has released the operational results of the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) for December 30, 2025, reporting a series of successful operations against armed terrorist groups across several regions of the country.
In the Fana region, during a reconnaissance mission, aerial surveillance detected around thirty terrorists on motorcycles moving toward the Soussan forest. The group was subsequently targeted and neutralized in a forested area north of Falako, resulting in the elimination of approximately thirty terrorists and the destruction of several motorcycles.
In the Kidal region, territorial control operations led to the detection of terrorist elements attempting to hide in Amazerakane with the intent of carrying out criminal acts. A precision strike neutralized the group along with its logistical support.
Also in Kidal, terrorists attempting to evade surveillance hid a pickup truck west of Télabit, northwest of the city. Following a detailed search, the vehicle was destroyed. The resulting explosion confirmed the presence of explosives inside the truck.
In the Timbuktu region, an aerial surveillance mission identified and neutralized terrorist elements south of Attara, leading to further losses among the armed groups and the destruction of equipment.
In the Mopti region, FAMa forces successfully neutralized an armed terrorist group northeast of Nouh-Bozo, as well as a second group north of Diafarabe.
The General Staff reaffirmed that the Malian Armed Forces remain on high alert and will continue operations without respite against armed terrorist groups throughout the national territory, in order to safeguard the population and maintain security.

title: 4th Rapid Intervention Battalion Class Trains in Tactical Mobility
excerpt: Koulikoro - December 31, 2025 ; Amid ongoing security challenges, the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) are placing renewed emphasis on the Rapid Intervention Battalions (BIR) to enhance their operational capacity against terrorist threats. In Koulikoro, the 4th graduating class of this
title_en: 4th Rapid Intervention Battalion Class Trains in Tactical Mobility
excerpt_en: Koulikoro - December 31, 2025 ; Amid ongoing security challenges, the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) are placing renewed emphasis on the Rapid Intervention Battalions (BIR) to enhance their operational capacity against terrorist threats. In Koulikoro, the 4th graduating class of this
body_en:
Koulikoro - December 31, 2025 ; Amid ongoing security challenges, the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) are placing renewed emphasis on the Rapid Intervention Battalions (BIR) to enhance their operational capacity against terrorist threats. In Koulikoro, the 4th graduating class of this elite unit is undergoing intensive training to prepare for deployment in complex operational environments.
The creation of the BIR was part of a strategic initiative by Malian authorities to respond swiftly to the resurgence of terrorist attacks, intercommunal violence, and the pressures these pose on civilian populations. These units are designed for rapid deployment across the country, equipped and trained to operate under the diverse conditions encountered in Mali.
Currently stationed at the Boubacar Sada Sy Training Center in Koulikoro, the 4th BIR class is specializing in mobility-focused tactics. Under the supervision of instructors from the National Gendarmerie, trainees are refining skills critical for operational effectiveness, including:
Motorcycle riding in challenging terrains
Obstacle crossing and alignment techniques
Two-wheeled vehicle control
Navigation through chicanes
Emergency braking procedures
While the precise operational deployment of these units has not yet been disclosed, their missions are guided by three core principles: mobility, specialization, and proximity. The BIRs are expected to strengthen national security and pursue armed terrorist groups relentlessly, even into their last strongholds.
Colonel-Major Boubacar Serme, director of the training center, commended the professionalism of the recruits, noting that the BIR program represents a strategic modernization of FAMa in response to an asymmetric and evolving conflict environment. “This fourth graduating class embodies the political will to modernize our army,” he stated.
The training concluded with a demonstration of the operational capabilities acquired by the recruits, highlighting the growing effectiveness and responsiveness of Mali’s elite forces in maintaining national security.

body_en:
Gao - December 31, 2025 ; The Islamic State (IS) in the Sahel province has issued an audio warning to residents in the Aribanda region, located south of the Niger River, instructing them to relocate to the north bank within seven days.
The warning comes amid ongoing clashes between the Islamic State and the Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims (GSIM), which are concentrated in this corridor stretching from Labbezanga-Tessit-Intillit to the outskirts of Doro, passing through Gossi in the Timbuktu region.
Villages directly affected by this warning include: Inachoulagh, Dougui, Morsi, Oussadja, Farfaroudji, Intassalefen, Tiaraghnine, Tinaykaran, Tabkachoum, Abou Ghali, and Ibaray.
Authorities are monitoring the situation closely, given the heightened risk to civilian populations amid the ongoing confrontations between armed groups in the area.

excerpt: Ménaka Region - December 29, 2025 & January 2, 2026 ISIS-Sahel IED Attack (Dec 29, 2025): The Islamic State in the Sahel (ISIS-Sahel) claimed responsibility for an improvised explosive device (IED) attack targeting a patrol near Intaday. The attack reportedly killed and wounded f
title_en: Mali - Security Update, Ménaka Region
excerpt_en: Ménaka Region - December 29, 2025 & January 2, 2026 ISIS-Sahel IED Attack (Dec 29, 2025): The Islamic State in the Sahel (ISIS-Sahel) claimed responsibility for an improvised explosive device (IED) attack targeting a patrol near Intaday. The attack reportedly killed and wounded f
body_en:
Ménaka Region - December 29, 2025 & January 2, 2026
ISIS-Sahel IED Attack (Dec 29, 2025): The Islamic State in the Sahel (ISIS-Sahel) claimed responsibility for an improvised explosive device (IED) attack targeting a patrol near Intaday. The attack reportedly killed and wounded five Malian soldiers and Russian mercenaries from the African Corps.
ISIS-Sahel released images of the targeted vehicle and a Russian mercenary’s helmet, asserting that a helicopter evacuation was observed and emphasizing that the attack directly targeted the Russian presence.
Counteroffensive (Jan 2, 2026): On the morning of January 2, 2026, the Malian army, African Corps units, and local militias advanced toward ISIS-controlled areas near the Niger border.
Clashes occurred in Tin Tadjallaline, lasting about an hour.
After intense fighting, Malian and Russian forces withdrew toward the town, as ISIS maintains control of remote areas where hostages are held.
These operations are considered particularly high-risk, highlighting the challenges of securing isolated regions far from main fronts.
This sequence of events underscores the persistent threat of ISIS-Sahel in Ménaka, combining IED ambushes, Russian involvement, and ongoing territorial control of remote areas.

body_en:
Koussan Commune - January 2-3, 2026
The security situation in the Koussan commune is deteriorating.
On Friday, January 2, 2026, at around 10:00 PM, a terrorist attack targeted a local mining site.
The following day, Saturday, January 3, 2026, at around 6:00 PM, attackers struck again, setting fire to the Forestry and Water Resources office and the Flamana Customs office.
Eyewitnesses reported that the attackers gathered at the Flamana mosque before carrying out the attacks.
No presence of armed forces has been reported in the area, leaving residents vulnerable and raising concerns about further attacks.
This pattern highlights the persistent threat from armed groups in remote areas and the urgent need for security reinforcement.

title_en: Kayes Region - JNIM Ambush on Army Convoy

body_en:
Kayes Region - January 3, 2026
The JNIM (Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims) claimed responsibility for ambushing a convoy of the Malian army and Russian Afrika Korps.
The convoy, tasked with escorting tanker trucks, was attacked on the road between Ksarou and Souribougou on Saturday evening, January 3, 2026.
As a result of the ambush, several tanker trucks were abandoned.
The attackers reportedly distributed the fuel from the trucks to local residents free of charge, signaling a tactical move to gain local support.
This incident underscores the persistent threat posed by JNIM in the Kayes region and the vulnerabilities of supply convoys in conflict zones.

body_en:
Ségou Region - January 3, 2026
The Jama’at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM) announced that it had taken full control of two bases belonging to pro-government militias.
The takeover occurred near the town of Dougoufiri on the morning of Saturday, January 3, 2026.
This development underscores JNIM’s continued operational presence in the Ségou region and its ability to challenge local security forces, destabilizing militia-controlled areas.
Conclusion
The period from late December 2025 to early January 2026 was marked by a decisive drive toward the institutional and strategic consolidation of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES). The second ordinary session of the AES College of Heads of State in Bamako served as a landmark event, resulting in several critical achievements:
Political Leadership and Unity: The appointment of Captain Ibrahim Traoré as the new President of the AES for a one-year term signals a commitment to continued leadership and the rotation of responsibility among member states.
Economic Sovereignty: The official inauguration of the Confederal Investment and Development Bank (BCID-AES) stands as a major step toward financial autonomy, designed to support strategic infrastructure and reduce dependence on external mechanisms.
Defense and Security Integration: The formal entry into service of the AES Unified Forces (UF-AES) and the adoption of new protocols on defense cooperation highlight the bloc’s unified stance against regional terrorist threats and external subversion.
Information and Cultural Sovereignty: The launch of AES Television and the successful hosting of the Arts and Culture Biennial in Timbuktu underscore efforts to promote shared values, national cohesion, and informational independence.
Diplomatic Assertiveness: Mali's application of the reciprocity principle regarding U.S. entry restrictions and its reaffirmed partnership with Russia reflect a foreign policy increasingly centered on sovereignty and the transition toward a multipolar international order.
In summary, this period represents a "new phase" for Mali and its Sahelian partners-transitioning from the conceptualization of the AES toward the operationalization of its core security, economic, and diplomatic pillars. The Bamako summit reaffirmed the ambition to evolve toward a federative framework anchored in solidarity and shared prosperity, even as the region continues to face complex asymmetric threats and external pressures.
By Maïga Sidi Bonkana
(Boukari Zankey Sidi)
Jeff Buleli

title: New Year’s Greetings to the Minister of Foreign Affairs: Staff Reaffirms Commitment to Strengthened Malian Diplomacy
excerpt: Bamako, January 5, 2026 On Monday, January 5, 2026, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation held its official New Year’s greetings ceremony for staff, addressed to His Excellency Abdoulaye Diop, Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation. The
title_en: New Year’s Greetings to the Minister of Foreign Affairs: Staff Reaffirms Commitment to Strengthened Malian Diplomacy
excerpt_en: Bamako, January 5, 2026 On Monday, January 5, 2026, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation held its official New Year’s greetings ceremony for staff, addressed to His Excellency Abdoulaye Diop, Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation. The
body_en:
Bamako, January 5, 2026
On Monday, January 5, 2026, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation held its official New Year’s greetings ceremony for staff, addressed to His Excellency Abdoulaye Diop, Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation.
The ceremony included speeches by the President of the Association of Women in Foreign Affairs, the Secretary General of the Free Union of Foreign Affairs, and the Secretary General of the Ministry, followed by remarks and greetings from Minister Abdoulaye Diop.
The event provided an opportunity to review the achievements of 2025 and to hold frank and constructive discussions on staff working conditions, paving the way for renewed commitment to strengthening Malian diplomacy in 2026.
Minister Diop welcomed the results achieved through teamwork and paid tribute to diplomatic and consular staff, the women of the department, and retirees for their dedication, commitment, and patriotism, which have enhanced Mali’s international influence.
He also addressed the improvement of working conditions and the effectiveness of diplomatic action, particularly through the updating of outdated documents to better respond to the country’s current challenges.
In conclusion, Abdoulaye Diop urged staff to redouble their efforts with honor, dignity, and professionalism to meet the challenges of 2026 and further strengthen Malian diplomacy, extending his wishes for peace, happiness, and prosperity to all employees, their families, and the nation.

The meeting aimed to provide the diplomat with strategic instructions for the effective defense of Mali’s interests in Switzerland.
Previously Director for Europe at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Mr. Cissé will now represent Mali in Geneva.
After the audience, he stated that the Head of State had delivered clear directives, emphasizing that Malian diplomacy is grounded in three constitutional principles: sovereignty, choice of partners, and defense of the interests of the Malian people.
Mr. Cissé also highlighted the cultural and identity dimension of the country’s ongoing restructuring, noting that the President called for promoting the Year of Culture so that every Malian feels fully integrated and enriched by diversity.
The President further reaffirmed the importance of protecting Malians’ interests across all institutions and urged full engagement in the Confederation of Sahel States (CSA), described as a framework forging its own path, free from external influence and aligned with the aspirations of its people.
Addressing upcoming challenges, the ambassador cited international communication as a priority, stressing the need to inform bilateral and multilateral partners accurately, counter disinformation, and clearly explain Mali’s choices.
He concluded by affirming that Mali’s decisions are not directed against anyone, but taken in the interest of the Malian people, and pledged to defend Mali’s interests firmly, loyally, and clearly in a shifting geopolitical landscape.

excerpt: The Confederation of Sahel States (AES) has condemned the US military intervention in Venezuela, which reportedly led to the capture of President Nicolás Maduro and his wife. In a statement, the AES - comprising Burkina Faso, Mali, and Niger - expressed deep concern, describing t
title_en: The Confederation of Sahel States Condemns US Military Operation in VenezuelaBamako, January 8, 2026
excerpt_en: The Confederation of Sahel States (AES) has condemned the US military intervention in Venezuela, which reportedly led to the capture of President Nicolás Maduro and his wife. In a statement, the AES - comprising Burkina Faso, Mali, and Niger - expressed deep concern, describing t
body_en:
The Confederation of Sahel States (AES) has condemned the US military intervention in Venezuela, which reportedly led to the capture of President Nicolás Maduro and his wife.
In a statement, the AES - comprising Burkina Faso, Mali, and Niger - expressed deep concern, describing the operation as the use of armed force against a sovereign state. The organization denounced the action as unacceptable interference and a violation of sovereignty, territorial integrity, and political independence, as enshrined in the Charter of the United Nations.
The Confederation called on the UN Security Council to condemn the US action and to work toward the restoration of international law. It reaffirmed its commitment to multilateralism, sovereign equality of states, and expressed solidarity with the Venezuelan people, whose sovereignty it said had been violated.
This position comes amid mixed international reactions following the operation and the reported capture of Nicolás Maduro in early January, an event criticized by several states as a violation of international law.

Bamako, January 17, 2026 - The President of the Transition, General Assimi Goïta, returned to Bamako on the early evening of January 17, 2026, after attending the inauguration ceremony of his Guinean counterpart, Mamadi Doumbouya, in Conakry.
This diplomatic visit formed part of the bilateral relations between Mali and Guinea and marked Mr. Goïta’s presence among about ten African heads of state at the event.
His return was confirmed by official sources, who indicated his arrival at Bamako airport after spending the day in Guinea attending the swearing-in ceremony of Mr. Doumbouya, who was elected on December 28, 2025, and inaugurated on January 17, 2026.
No official statement has been released by the Malian presidency regarding any bilateral discussions that may have taken place during this trip.

excerpt_en: Conakry, January 17, 2026 - General Assimi Goïta, President of the Transition in Mali, traveled to Conakry on January 17, 2026, to attend the inauguration ceremony of Guinean President Mamadi Doumbouya, alongside other African heads of state. He was accompanied by a delegation in
body_en:
Conakry, January 17, 2026 - General Assimi Goïta, President of the Transition in Mali, traveled to Conakry on January 17, 2026, to attend the inauguration ceremony of Guinean President Mamadi Doumbouya, alongside other African heads of state.
He was accompanied by a delegation including members of his presidential cabinet and several ministers, notably those of Defense and Veterans Affairs, Economy and Finance, Transport and Infrastructure, and Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation. Mr. Goïta departed Bamako in the morning to attend the event.
The inauguration ceremony of Mamadi Doumbouya, who was elected on December 28, 2025, took place at the 50,000-seat General Lansana Conté Stadium in Nongo, marking the end of the transitional period that began after the 2021 coup.
Among the leaders present were Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema (Gabon), Bassirou Diomaye Faye (Senegal), Joseph Nyuma Boakai (Liberia), Adama Barrow (Gambia), Julius Maada Bio (Sierra Leone), Mohamed Ould Cheikh El Ghazouani (Mauritania), and Paul Kagame (Rwanda), demonstrating regional support for the inauguration.
According to Guinean authorities, about ten heads of state and international delegations were expected, amid a flurry of diplomatic activity.

title_en: Mali | Celebration of the Day of Regained Sovereignty in Kati: A Call for Student Responsibility and Commitment
excerpt_en: Kati, January 12, 2026 - As part of efforts to strengthen cooperation and the sharing of experiences among the National Committees and Commissions of the AES Confederation, His Excellency Abdoulaye Diop, Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, held a working se
body_en:
Kati, January 12, 2026 - As part of efforts to strengthen cooperation and the sharing of experiences among the National Committees and Commissions of the AES Confederation, His Excellency Abdoulaye Diop, Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, held a working session on Monday, January 12, 2026, with a delegation from the National Commission of the Confederation of Sahel States of Burkina Faso, led by its President, Bassolma Bazie, during a courtesy and working visit to Mali.
This visit followed the appointment of Captain Ibrahim Traoré, President of Burkina Faso, as head of the AES Confederation, after the inaugural term entrusted to General Assimi Goïta, President of the Transition in Mali.
During fraternal and fruitful discussions, Minister Diop highlighted the challenges encountered in implementing the Confederation, the joint results achieved in applying the roadmap during its first year, the lessons learned from coordinating confederal activities, and the prospects for meeting the aspirations of the people, in line with the shared vision of the three Heads of State.
Given the confederal and ultimately federal nature of the vision, both sides emphasized the priority of meeting the population’s essential needs through concrete actions with a direct impact on living conditions. These include strengthening the free movement of people and promoting socio-economic integration, within a spirit of fraternity, solidarity, pragmatism, shared commitment, and continuity of action.
While acknowledging the significant progress achieved during the first term, the President of the AES Confederation Commission of Burkina Faso requested Mali’s support and assistance to continue the Confederation’s missions under Burkina Faso’s presidency.
Minister Diop stated: “The AES Confederation train has simply changed drivers, but Mali remains on board to reach the agreed destination together.” He concluded by reaffirming the unwavering availability and commitment of the Malian authorities and people to support the shared vision, particularly regarding the security of the Confederation’s territory, the promotion of sustainable development and shared prosperity, within a framework of integration and strengthened diplomacy.
