title: Launch of the Third Edition of Digital Week in Mali
excerpt: Bamako, January 2026 Minister of Communication, Digital Economy, and Administrative Modernization, Alhamdou Ag Ilyène, held a press conference to officially launch the third edition of Digital Week, now scheduled for January 29-31, 2026 due to a busy institutional agenda. This ed
title_en: Launch of the Third Edition of Digital Week in Mali
excerpt_en: Bamako, January 2026 Minister of Communication, Digital Economy, and Administrative Modernization, Alhamdou Ag Ilyène, held a press conference to officially launch the third edition of Digital Week, now scheduled for January 29-31, 2026 due to a busy institutional agenda. This ed
body_en:
Bamako, January 2026
Minister of Communication, Digital Economy, and Administrative Modernization, Alhamdou Ag Ilyène, held a press conference to officially launch the third edition of Digital Week, now scheduled for January 29-31, 2026 due to a busy institutional agenda.
This edition focuses on the theme: “E-Government in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: Opportunities and Challenges for Culture”, highlighting the Malian authorities’ commitment to digital technology as a strategic lever for sovereignty, administrative modernization, and resilience.
The minister emphasized that artificial intelligence is crucial for transforming public services and cultural industries, and that digital technology is now an essential pillar of public performance and citizen inclusion.
Burkina Faso and Niger will participate as guest countries of honor, under the framework of the Confederation of Sahel States, promoting harmonization of digital policies, e-government strategies, and exchange on AI, cybersecurity, and digital identity.
The program includes a ministerial roundtable, thematic discussions on AI, digital public services, artistic creation, ICT financing, and digital identity, and a national digital innovation competition showcasing startups, project leaders, and public services.
The minister called on youth, innovators, and the private sector to make this edition a moment of collective mobilization to build a sovereign, inclusive, and forward-looking digital Mali.

title: Mali | Former OCLEI President Moumouni Guindo Under Investigation
excerpt: Bamako, January 11, 2026 - A mission from the Office of the Auditor General is currently examining the management of Moumouni Guindo, former president of the Central Office for Combating Illicit Enrichment (OCLEI), for the period 2021-2025, marking a first for an independent admi
title_en: Mali | Former OCLEI President Moumouni Guindo Under Investigation
excerpt_en: Bamako, January 11, 2026 - A mission from the Office of the Auditor General is currently examining the management of Moumouni Guindo, former president of the Central Office for Combating Illicit Enrichment (OCLEI), for the period 2021-2025, marking a first for an independent admi
body_en:
Bamako, January 11, 2026 - A mission from the Office of the Auditor General is currently examining the management of Moumouni Guindo, former president of the Central Office for Combating Illicit Enrichment (OCLEI), for the period 2021-2025, marking a first for an independent administrative authority.
The allegations concern the creation of an unauthorized office, unexplained travel, telephone expenses included in salary allowances, the funding of private studies, and an attempt to acquire an armored vehicle, which was rejected by the budget department.
Mr. Guindo is accused of failing to fulfill his duties of raising awareness, conducting investigations, and referring cases to the courts, while OCLEI reportedly spent billions of CFA francs without any significant impact on public finances.
His commitment is described as being more focused on individual harassment than on the public interest, with a final annual report compiling previous data highlighting shortcomings.
His mandate ended on May 31, 2025, after eight years, and a request for a nine-month extension was rejected by the Prime Minister.
This audit is presented as a step toward improving the ethical standards of public officials in the fight against illicit enrichment.

title: Mali | Record Mining Revenues Exceed 1,000 Billion CFA Francs
excerpt: Bamako, January 12, 2026 - Mali has recorded mining revenues of 1,022 billion CFA francs paid to the State, far exceeding initial projections of 400 billion CFA francs. The announcement was made by the President of the Transition, General Assimi Goïta, during the New Year’s greet
title_en: Mali | Record Mining Revenues Exceed 1,000 Billion CFA Francs
excerpt_en: Bamako, January 12, 2026 - Mali has recorded mining revenues of 1,022 billion CFA francs paid to the State, far exceeding initial projections of 400 billion CFA francs. The announcement was made by the President of the Transition, General Assimi Goïta, during the New Year’s greet
body_en:
Bamako, January 12, 2026 - Mali has recorded mining revenues of 1,022 billion CFA francs paid to the State, far exceeding initial projections of 400 billion CFA francs. The announcement was made by the President of the Transition, General Assimi Goïta, during the New Year’s greetings ceremony addressed to Malian civil society.
The results reflect negotiations that led to the recovery of 761 billion CFA francs in arrears from mining companies, an increase of approximately 580 billion CFA francs compared to previous years. These funds were disbursed following a sector audit launched in 2023 and the adoption of a new Mining Code.
The reforms include indexing revenues to world gold prices, replacing fixed payments, and depositing revenues from gold sales in local banks, generating an estimated annual flow of 6 trillion CFA francs for the Malian banking system.

title: Mali | 4th National Day of Restored Sovereignty Celebrated Across the Country and Abroad
excerpt: Bamako, January 14, 2026 - Mali marked the 4th National Day of Restored Sovereignty on Wednesday, January 14, 2026, a historic occasion celebrating the mobilization of the Malian people to assert their sovereignty and reject sanctions deemed illegitimate. The commemoration featur
title_en: Mali | 4th National Day of Restored Sovereignty Celebrated Across the Country and Abroad
excerpt_en: Bamako, January 14, 2026 - Mali marked the 4th National Day of Restored Sovereignty on Wednesday, January 14, 2026, a historic occasion celebrating the mobilization of the Malian people to assert their sovereignty and reject sanctions deemed illegitimate. The commemoration featur
body_en:
Bamako, January 14, 2026 - Mali marked the 4th National Day of Restored Sovereignty on Wednesday, January 14, 2026, a historic occasion celebrating the mobilization of the Malian people to assert their sovereignty and reject sanctions deemed illegitimate. The commemoration featured a series of official, social, and educational activities nationwide and within the diaspora.
In Bamako, the Minister of Health and Social Development, Colonel-Major Assa Badiallo Touré, presented a significant donation of medicines to the Kalaban-Coro Reference Health Center (CSRéf). The equipment included birthing kits, feminine hygiene kits, modern stretchers, and essential injections and tablets, aimed at improving the quality of care and access to healthcare services.
In Nioro du Sahel, the Minister of Livestock and Fisheries, Youba Ba, joined local authorities, school officials, and students in the celebrations, highlighting the government’s emphasis on civic education and patriotism among youth. The day began with a flag-raising ceremony at Kaïmé School, followed by the singing of the national anthem in Bambara and a history lecture for ninth-grade students on the recovery of sovereignty.
The minister and his delegation later visited Maison Rose, where a large crowd continued the celebrations in an atmosphere of patriotic unity and social cohesion.
In Dakar, Senegal, the Minister for Malians Abroad and African Integration, Mossa Ag Attaher, celebrated the day with the Malian community and nationals from other African and Southern African countries, presiding over a flag-raising ceremony and leading a conference on the origin and significance of the historic day.
In Bamako, the Prime Minister, Major General Abdoulaye Maïga, delivered the official commemorative address, calling for national unity and highlighting progress since 2022, particularly the strengthening of state sovereignty and trust between the people and their leaders.
In Timbuktu, the Minister of National Entrepreneurship, Employment, and Training, Oumou Sall Seck, participated in festivities that began on January 13, involving children in educational workshops on sovereignty, and presenting them with symbolic gifts.
The 4th edition of the National Day of Reclaimed Sovereignty was marked by a spirit of patriotism, solidarity, and collective responsibility, reflecting the commitment of the Malian authorities and people to build a sovereign, stable, and prosperous Mali.

title: Mali | Kal Akal 2025 Annual Report Highlights Worsening Human Rights Situation in Azawad
excerpt: Kidal, January 13, 2026 - The Kal Akal Association’s 2025 annual report paints an extremely worrying picture of the human rights situation in the Azawad region. Based on corroborated and verified information, the report highlights widespread and systematic violence perpetrated ag
title_en: Mali | Kal Akal 2025 Annual Report Highlights Worsening Human Rights Situation in Azawad
excerpt_en: Kidal, January 13, 2026 - The Kal Akal Association’s 2025 annual report paints an extremely worrying picture of the human rights situation in the Azawad region. Based on corroborated and verified information, the report highlights widespread and systematic violence perpetrated ag
body_en:
Kidal, January 13, 2026 - The Kal Akal Association’s 2025 annual report paints an extremely worrying picture of the human rights situation in the Azawad region. Based on corroborated and verified information, the report highlights widespread and systematic violence perpetrated against civilian populations.
A total of 573 cases of summary executions and airstrikes were recorded, indiscriminately targeting women, children, and the elderly, particularly in markets and during community gatherings. Additionally, there were 276 cases of abduction, enforced disappearance, and torture, particularly affecting community leaders, which has severely undermined social cohesion and local governance.
The humanitarian consequences are considerable: more than 210 mass displacements, destruction of livelihoods and vital infrastructure, as well as 117 cases of looting and destruction of civilian property. Environmental degradation and restricted access to essential resources further exacerbate the population’s vulnerability. Despite their limited number, the documented cases of sexual violence have lasting consequences for victims and their communities.
Kal Akal concludes that 2025 will be among the darkest years in Azawad’s recent history, marked by the collapse of the social fabric, chronic insecurity, and profound collective trauma. In response, the organization reaffirms its commitment to documenting violations, strengthening the protection of vulnerable populations, and intensifying its actions in 2026 to promote resilience and provide support for victims.

body_en:
Bamako, January 16, 2026 - Mali has taken a radical decision. On January 16, 2026, the Minister of Territorial Administration and Decentralization, Major General Abdoulaye Maïga, signed a decree banning the dissemination, distribution, and sale of the Jeune Afrique newspaper throughout the country.
The drastic measure, effective immediately, cites serious grounds, including accusations of subversion and the glorification of terrorism following articles concerning hydrocarbon supplies. Malian authorities also allege the outlet made “unfounded” accusations, displayed a blatant lack of journalistic objectivity, deliberate bias, and incitement to hatred in its coverage of sensitive topics.
The decision specifically mentions allegations of abuses committed against the authorities and armed forces of member countries of the Confederation of Sahel States. Anyone violating the provisions of the decree is subject to the penalties stipulated by Malian law.

title_en: Mali | Sky Mali Cancels Flights Amid Fuel Shortages and Rising Insecurity
excerpt_en: Bamako, January 6, 2026 - Sky Mali, the national airline, has announced the cancellation of multiple flights and schedule changes over the coming days due to severe fuel shortages in the capital. According to airline management, the situation is beyond their control, stemming fro
body_en:
Bamako, January 6, 2026 - Sky Mali, the national airline, has announced the cancellation of multiple flights and schedule changes over the coming days due to severe fuel shortages in the capital.
According to airline management, the situation is beyond their control, stemming from logistical constraints in the fuel supply chain. Fuel scarcity in Bamako has been described as a critical issue, with panic buying, black market surges, and prolonged shortages affecting residents and businesses alike.
The crisis has been aggravated by the resurgence of attacks by JNIM jihadists, who control key access points to the capital and had previously disrupted fuel deliveries between September and October 2025. Although a temporary lull occurred following a military council agreement in November 2025, the end of the truce on December 5, 2025, led to renewed attacks on fuel convoys and public transportation.
The capital is currently facing power outages lasting from hours to over a day, limited fuel availability, and widespread insecurity in surrounding areas, including Fana, Kassela, Zantiguila, Kita, and Bougouni.
Sky Mali has pledged to reschedule affected flights and keep passengers informed, emphasizing its commitment to safety, service quality, and transparency. Residents, meanwhile, are struggling with daily disruptions, describing their situation as forced resilience amid energy shortages and rising insecurity.

title_en: Mali | MSF Reports on Malian Army Strikes in Dogofry

body_en:
Dogofry, Ségou region, January 6, 2026 - Following an airstrike that hit the market in Dogofry, in the Sokolo district, teams from MSF and the Ministry of Health treated 54 wounded people. Of these, 24 were transferred to the hospital in Niono and 30 to the Dogofry community health center.
The majority of the wounded were children and women, including a pregnant woman who lost her child in the attack. Patients presented with fractures, cervical wounds, and signs of pneumothorax, requiring intensive care in the surgical ward in Niono.
Attacks against civilians have been frequent in the region, notably on December 29 and January 3, particularly in the K2 area, where about ten people were wounded.

Nioro du Sahel, Southwestern Mali - For nearly five months, the town of Nioro du Sahel, located on the Mauritanian border, has been under a blockade imposed by JNIM jihadists. The town is effectively cut off from the world, with roads controlled, movement virtually impossible, and kidnappings threatening anyone who attempts to circumvent the encirclement.
Testimonies from residents report a rapid deterioration in living conditions. Basic necessities are becoming scarce, leading to soaring prices in the markets. The price of some food products has nearly doubled, while livestock farming has become unaffordable for many families. Locals say they are barely surviving and are urging the authorities to strengthen security.
Despite the administrative presence of the state and occasional military operations, the blockade persists. Jihadists accuse the population of supporting Malian authorities, further fueling tensions. In Nioro du Sahel, the wait for improvement continues, while isolation and insecurity weigh increasingly on civilians.

Mali, January 11, 2026 - The General Staff of the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) reported the results of operations conducted nationwide on January 11, 2026.
As part of a territorial surveillance mission, FAMa air assets carried out strikes against three armed terrorist groups:
The first strike, west of Bebelin and south of the Kekoro forest in the Dioïla region, neutralized approximately ten terrorists and destroyed several motorcycles.
The second strike, southeast of Tinkeleni in Dioïla, successfully neutralized several terrorists and destroyed dozens of motorcycles.
The third strike, east of Kidal, targeted a vehicle belonging to armed terrorist groups containing explosives.
Additionally, the Malian Armed Forces thwarted an ambush set by an armed terrorist group in Léré, Timbuktu region, resulting in the neutralization of several terrorists and the recovery of a significant quantity of weapons, ammunition, and motorcycles.

title_en: Mali | JNIM Attacks Tanker Convoy and Seizes Army Post
excerpt_en: San, Ségou Region, January 16, 2026 - The terrorist group JNIM launched a violent attack on a Malian army convoy escorting tanker trucks between San and Bla on Friday morning, January 16, 2026. According to local sources and images released by the group, several Malian soldiers a
body_en:
San, Ségou Region, January 16, 2026 - The terrorist group JNIM launched a violent attack on a Malian army convoy escorting tanker trucks between San and Bla on Friday morning, January 16, 2026. According to local sources and images released by the group, several Malian soldiers and gendarmes were killed, military vehicles seized, and dozens of tanker trucks set on fire after the military escort was neutralized.
Koulikoro Region, January 18, 2026 - The Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims (JNIM) claims to have taken full control of a Malian army post in Nossombougou on Sunday morning, January 18, 2026.
Conclusion
The situation in Mali is characterized by a deepening divide between official state rhetoric of "recovered sovereignty" and a deteriorating reality of economic paralysis and widespread insecurity. While the transitional government celebrates diplomatic milestones and record mining revenues, the civilian population faces a critical energy crisis and escalating violence from multiple armed factions.
1. Geopolitical and Diplomatic Shift
The government has intensified its "paradigm shift" toward absolute national sovereignty, focusing on the defense of Malian interests and the strategic choice of partners like China. This period was marked by:
Regional Integration: Strong commitment to the Confederation of Sahel States (AES), with Mali handing over the rotating presidency to Burkina Faso.
Diplomatic Assertiveness: The AES issued a sharp condemnation of US military actions in Venezuela, signaling a move toward a more vocal, anti-interventionist foreign policy.
Guinean Relations: President Goïta attended the inauguration of Mamadi Doumbouya, reinforcing regional alliances with neighboring transitional authorities.
2. Economic and Infrastructure Crisis
Despite the announcement of record mining revenues exceeding 1,000 billion CFA francs, the domestic economy is struggling with severe logistical failures.
Fuel and Energy Paralysis: Bamako is facing a "critical situation" with fuel shortages that have caused flight cancellations for Sky Mali and Air Burkina and forced residents to wait up to seven hours for gasoline.
Supply Blockades: JNIM's "economic war" has led to a five-month blockade of Nioro du Sahel and the destruction of tanker convoys, driving up the price of basic necessities and causing the closure of businesses like hotels in Ségou.
3. Escalating Conflict and Human Rights Concerns
The security landscape remains volatile, with active combat on multiple fronts:
Insurgent Activity: JNIM and ISIS continue to clash with each other and target the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) and Russian mercenaries (Africa Corps) across the Ségou, Timbuktu, and Sikasso regions.
Military Response: FAMa has increased its use of aerial surveillance and drone strikes, targeting terrorist bases and gold processing facilities in Kidal, Kayes, and Mopti.
Civilian Impact: Human rights reports from the Azawad region describe 2025 as one of the "darkest years," citing 573 cases of summary executions and airstrikes. In Dogofry, a recent airstrike on a market resulted in 54 civilian casualties, the majority being women and children.
4. Domestic Policy and Social Control
The government is tightening control over the national narrative through both celebration and censorship:
Media Restrictions: The banning of Jeune Afrique for "subversion" and "glorifying terrorism" highlights a declining tolerance for external criticism.
Nationalism: The 4th National Day of Restored Sovereignty was used as a platform to promote civic education and patriotism among the youth.
Internal Scrutiny: The audit of the former OCLEI president suggests a push for higher ethical standards, or at least a reorganization of the anti-corruption apparatus.
By Maïga Sidi Bonkana
(Boukari Zankey Sidi)
Jeff Buleli

title: Ambassador Bazivamo Conveys President Kagame’s Message to Rwandans in Brazzaville
excerpt: Brazzaville, Republic of Congo - Sunday, December 28, 2025 The Secretary General of the RPF Inkotanyi, Ambassador Christophe Bazivamo, met with Rwandans living in Brazzaville during a working visit to the Republic of Congo, where he conveyed a message from President Paul Kagame.
title_en: Ambassador Bazivamo Conveys President Kagame’s Message to Rwandans in Brazzaville
excerpt_en: Brazzaville, Republic of Congo - Sunday, December 28, 2025 The Secretary General of the RPF Inkotanyi, Ambassador Christophe Bazivamo, met with Rwandans living in Brazzaville during a working visit to the Republic of Congo, where he conveyed a message from President Paul Kagame.
body_en:
Brazzaville, Republic of Congo - Sunday, December 28, 2025
The Secretary General of the RPF Inkotanyi, Ambassador Christophe Bazivamo, met with Rwandans living in Brazzaville during a working visit to the Republic of Congo, where he conveyed a message from President Paul Kagame.
According to a statement released by the RPF Inkotanyi, Amb. Bazivamo delivered the greetings of President Kagame, wishing the Rwandan diaspora good health and continued progress, while outlining the development programs Rwanda has committed to. He emphasized that Rwandans abroad are expected to play a direct role in contributing to the country’s national development.
The ambassador reaffirmed that Rwanda continues to support its citizens abroad in their development initiatives and remains ready to assist them whenever possible. He encouraged the diaspora to uphold Rwandan values, particularly teamwork and honesty.
Amb. Bazivamo concluded the meeting by extending New Year 2026 wishes to the Rwandan community.
During his stay in Brazzaville, the ambassador also participated in the sixth ordinary congress of the ruling Parti Congolais du Travail (PCT), to which he was officially invited. He highlighted the strong people-centered leadership shared by the PCT and the RPF Inkotanyi, expressing willingness to further strengthen relations between the two political parties and enhance bilateral cooperation between Rwanda and Congo-Brazzaville.
The two countries maintain longstanding diplomatic and political relations, reinforced by Rwanda’s opening of its embassy in Brazzaville in 2016. In 2011, both nations signed several cooperation agreements covering sectors such as air transport, tourism, energy, security, justice, environment, and fisheries.
Bilateral ties deepened further in 2023, when President Denis Sassou Nguesso paid an official visit to Rwanda, shortly after Congo-Brazzaville introduced visa-free entry for Rwandan citizens, allowing visas to be obtained upon arrival and free of charge. During that visit, eight new cooperation agreements were signed, adding to the 25 agreements concluded in April 2022 during President Kagame’s visit to Brazzaville.

excerpt: Kinshasa, January 2, 2026 The AFC/M23 Alliance has sharply criticized President Félix Tshisekedi’s government for attributing the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s ongoing insecurity to foreign actors, calling it a tactic to hide domestic failures. Political Coordinator Corneill
title_en: DRC Conflict: AFC/M23 Criticizes Tshisekedi’s Government for Blaming International Community
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, January 2, 2026 The AFC/M23 Alliance has sharply criticized President Félix Tshisekedi’s government for attributing the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s ongoing insecurity to foreign actors, calling it a tactic to hide domestic failures. Political Coordinator Corneill
body_en:
Kinshasa, January 2, 2026
The AFC/M23 Alliance has sharply criticized President Félix Tshisekedi’s government for attributing the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s ongoing insecurity to foreign actors, calling it a tactic to hide domestic failures.
Political Coordinator Corneille Nangaa said the Kinshasa administration is attempting to shift responsibility for killings, massacres, corruption, ethnic conflicts, urban crime, poverty, and other systemic issues onto the international community instead of addressing the root causes.
“The problems that exist are the Congolese themselves. Trying to blame them on the international community is to focus on the symptoms of the disease without addressing the root of the problem. It is a hypocritical plan by the Kinshasa regime to hide the failure of its government,” Nangaa stated.
He added that efforts to petition other countries will not solve the country’s structural problems, and that the AFC/M23’s approach emphasizes transparency, truth, accountability, and justice.
Nangaa underscored that the movement’s goal is not revenge, but a lasting solution for the Congolese people, based on reconciliation, unity, non-discrimination, and law enforcement.
“The time for deception, lies, and false promises is over. From now on, the Congolese stand firm, determined and with great will. The year 2026 will be the year to strengthen our struggle for liberation, justice, peace, and the reconstruction of the State,” he said.
He also confirmed that Doha-facilitated talks between the DRC government and AFC/M23 have failed to yield a viable solution, and noted that the Tshisekedi administration has refused further negotiations, whether in person or virtually.
This statement highlights the deepening mistrust between the Congolese government and the AFC/M23 Alliance, raising concerns over the prospects for peace and stability in eastern DRC.

title: Sudan Seeks Rwanda’s Expertise in Peacebuilding and Regional Cooperation

title_en: Sudan Seeks Rwanda’s Expertise in Peacebuilding and Regional Cooperation
excerpt_en: Kigali, January 2, 2026 Sudan is looking to Rwanda as a model for peacebuilding and national reconstruction, according to Sudanese Ambassador to Rwanda, Khalid Musa Dafalla. Speaking at the Rwanda Broadcasting Agency (RBA), Ambassador Musa highlighted Sudan’s interest in learning
body_en:
Kigali, January 2, 2026
Sudan is looking to Rwanda as a model for peacebuilding and national reconstruction, according to Sudanese Ambassador to Rwanda, Khalid Musa Dafalla. Speaking at the Rwanda Broadcasting Agency (RBA), Ambassador Musa highlighted Sudan’s interest in learning from Rwanda’s experience in achieving peace, unity, and rapid development.
“Sudan needs Rwanda not only as a development partner, but also as a peacebuilding partner. Rwanda provides peace and has a strong voice in understanding Africanness,” he said.
Ambassador Musa emphasized that Sudan is eager to strengthen regional cooperation and draw on Rwanda’s expertise in managing post-conflict reconstruction, reconciliation, and governance. He praised Rwanda’s leadership under President Paul Kagame, noting its influence in Africa and its ability to guide other nations in conflict resolution.
Sudan also values Rwanda’s hospitality toward Sudanese nationals, including 4,000 individuals who fled the ongoing conflict in Sudan since 2023, and the relocation of the Sudanese University of Medical Sciences and Technology (UMST) to Rwanda. Sudanese investments in Rwanda currently exceed $20 million, spanning agriculture, healthcare, construction, and education.
In sports, Sudanese football teams displaced by the war have also been allowed to compete in the Rwandan First Division Championship, reflecting Rwanda’s commitment to regional solidarity and support.
Ambassador Musa concluded that Rwanda serves as a model of development, unity, and reconciliation, and Sudan is keen to continue building on this partnership for the benefit of both nations and the region.

title: DRC’s Size Used as a Pretext for Tshisekedi’s Failure to Protect Citizens
excerpt: January 4, 2026- The sheer size of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is increasingly being used as a pretext to justify President Félix Tshisekedi’s persistent inability to guarantee security for the Congolese people. As insecurity continues to worsen in eastern DRC, par
title_en: DRC’s Size Used as a Pretext for Tshisekedi’s Failure to Protect Citizens
excerpt_en: January 4, 2026- The sheer size of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is increasingly being used as a pretext to justify President Félix Tshisekedi’s persistent inability to guarantee security for the Congolese people. As insecurity continues to worsen in eastern DRC, par
body_en:
January 4, 2026- The sheer size of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is increasingly being used as a pretext to justify President Félix Tshisekedi’s persistent inability to guarantee security for the Congolese people. As insecurity continues to worsen in eastern DRC, particularly in the Kivu region, senior officials have repeatedly argued that the country’s vast territory is responsible for decades of instability.
A recurring narrative among DRC leaders is that the Congo is simply too large to govern effectively. This argument has been frequently invoked by President Tshisekedi to explain the ongoing violence. In 2022, he publicly claimed that the country’s security challenges stem from its size, insisting that the national army could not be deployed everywhere to fight armed groups such as the ADF, an Islamic State-linked Ugandan militia, and other insurgents operating on Congolese soil.
Despite numbering around 130,000 troops, the FARDC is plagued by low morale, inadequate training, weak command structures, ethnic discrimination, corruption, and the integration of the FDLR, a Rwandan militia responsible for the 1994 genocide against the Tutsis, incorporated under Tshisekedi’s authority.
Tshisekedi’s reliance on Burundian troops, the Wazalendo militia, European mercenaries, and SADC forces has steadily declined, particularly after South Africa, Malawi, and Tanzania withdrew their contingents following military setbacks against the AFC/M23.

title: Togo Moves to Revive Peace Talks Between DRC Government and AFC/M23
excerpt: January 5, 2026 - The government of Togo has initiated efforts to revive peace talks between the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and the AFC/M23 movement, amid renewed violence in eastern DRC. According to diplomatic sources, Lomé was expected to host a high-level mediation me
title_en: Togo Moves to Revive Peace Talks Between DRC Government and AFC/M23
excerpt_en: January 5, 2026 - The government of Togo has initiated efforts to revive peace talks between the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and the AFC/M23 movement, amid renewed violence in eastern DRC. According to diplomatic sources, Lomé was expected to host a high-level mediation me
body_en:
January 5, 2026 - The government of Togo has initiated efforts to revive peace talks between the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and the AFC/M23 movement, amid renewed violence in eastern DRC.
According to diplomatic sources, Lomé was expected to host a high-level mediation meeting on January 17, 2026, aimed at restoring dialogue between the two sides. The initiative was intended to rebuild mutual trust and restart negotiations that have stalled in recent weeks. Other international mediators, including the United States and Qatar, were expected to take part in the meeting.
Relations between the DRC government and the AFC/M23 deteriorated sharply in early December 2025, following intense fighting in South Kivu province, particularly in the Rusizi Valley.
Tensions further escalated when AFC/M23 fighters entered the city of Uvira, claiming they were responding to continued attacks by Congolese government forces on their positions. On December 16, the AFC/M23 announced its decision to withdraw from Uvira, a move that was carried out two days later. However, the DRC government rejected the withdrawal, and its forces reportedly launched fresh attacks from the Fizi area.
In his end-of-year address, AFC/M23 leader Corneille Nangaa Yobeluo disclosed that Qatar had convened two meetings aimed at discussing the implementation of a ceasefire agreement, but said the DRC government declined to attend.
According to Nangaa, Kinshasa deliberately chose to sabotage the peace process, favoring a military option, as it had done in previous conflicts. He reaffirmed that the AFC/M23 remains committed to a genuine and lasting peace, and said the movement continues to place its trust in Qatar’s mediation efforts.

title: DRC Agriculture Minister Criticizes FARDC and Intelligence Services Over War and Media Influence
excerpt: The Minister of Agriculture and Food Security of the Democratic Republic of Congo, Muhindo Nzangi Butondo, has strongly criticized the FARDC and military intelligence services, accusing them of being intimidated by narratives circulating on social media amid the ongoing conflict.
title_en: DRC Agriculture Minister Criticizes FARDC and Intelligence Services Over War and Media Influence
excerpt_en: The Minister of Agriculture and Food Security of the Democratic Republic of Congo, Muhindo Nzangi Butondo, has strongly criticized the FARDC and military intelligence services, accusing them of being intimidated by narratives circulating on social media amid the ongoing conflict.
body_en:
The Minister of Agriculture and Food Security of the Democratic Republic of Congo, Muhindo Nzangi Butondo, has strongly criticized the FARDC and military intelligence services, accusing them of being intimidated by narratives circulating on social media amid the ongoing conflict.
Speaking in an interview on January 5, 2026, the minister argued that the DRC government is losing not only the war on the ground but also the information battle. He said the situation surrounding the fall of Uvira illustrates how misinformation and panic contributed to military failure.
“Take the example of Uvira. They announced its capture while M23 fighters were still in Luvungi, about 30 kilometers away. Once the news spread online, everyone believed Uvira had fallen, and the national army fled the city before the enemy even arrived,” he said.
On December 9, 2025, AFC/M23 fighters entered Uvira, before withdrawing about a week later following international pressure, particularly from the United States, which had assured that peace talks would continue.
According to Minister Muhindo, the AFC/M23 coalition maintains significant military strength, to the extent that, without external intervention, it could have advanced far beyond Uvira.
“I must be honest: if it had not been for a message from Marco Rubio saying, ‘We are not happy! We are not happy!’, they would likely be in Kalemie, in Tanganyika Province, because there was practically nothing stopping them. That message gave us time to prepare,” he stated.
The minister emphasized that the absence of further territorial advances by AFC/M23 should not be interpreted as a lack of military capability, but rather as the result of diplomatic intervention, mainly by the United States.
He concluded by asserting that the only real leverage the DRC government still retains is diplomatic, not military, underscoring the fragility of the country’s security apparatus in the face of organized armed groups.

title: Tshisekedi Turns Away from Doha Mediation, Pushes for New Luanda Talks
excerpt: President Félix Tshisekedi of the Democratic Republic of the Congo is seeking to relaunch peace talks in Luanda, while continuing to distance himself from the Qatari-led mediation process initiated in early 2025. Tshisekedi last traveled to Luanda on December 14, 2025, where he h
title_en: Tshisekedi Turns Away from Doha Mediation, Pushes for New Luanda Talks
excerpt_en: President Félix Tshisekedi of the Democratic Republic of the Congo is seeking to relaunch peace talks in Luanda, while continuing to distance himself from the Qatari-led mediation process initiated in early 2025. Tshisekedi last traveled to Luanda on December 14, 2025, where he h
body_en:
President Félix Tshisekedi of the Democratic Republic of the Congo is seeking to relaunch peace talks in Luanda, while continuing to distance himself from the Qatari-led mediation process initiated in early 2025.
Tshisekedi last traveled to Luanda on December 14, 2025, where he held brief discussions with Angolan President João Lourenço on efforts to restore peace in eastern DRC. The Luanda framework, led by Lourenço, has been stalled since October 2024, when the Congolese government delegation refused to engage in direct dialogue with the AFC/M23 coalition.
The paralysis of the Luanda process coincided with President Lourenço assuming the chairmanship of the African Union (AU). During this period, mediation efforts shifted toward Washington and Doha, though with limited progress. Lourenço is expected to step down from the AU presidency during the AU General Assembly on February 15, 2026, to be replaced by Burundi’s President Évariste Ndayishimiye, potentially freeing him to re-engage fully in mediation efforts.
On January 5, 2026, President Tshisekedi again visited Angola to discuss security developments in eastern DRC. However, the agenda reportedly mirrored discussions already held under the Doha and Washington initiatives.
Although the Congolese presidency maintains that Tshisekedi still formally supports the Doha process, his actions suggest otherwise. The DRC recently declined to send representatives to two meetings organized by Qatar, which were aimed at assessing the implementation of the ceasefire agreement.
Meanwhile, regional tensions around mediation have intensified. Burundi’s foreign minister has publicly accused Qatar of using its diplomatic influence to block potential international sanctions against Rwanda-claims that have been repeatedly denied.
Sources in Kinshasa indicate that Tshisekedi has formally asked President Lourenço to initiate a new round of talks in Luanda, a request the Angolan leader has reportedly accepted. The proposed talks would involve a broad range of Congolese stakeholders, including members of the ruling coalition, political opposition figures, armed groups such as AFC/M23, religious leaders, and civil society representatives.
If launched, the new Luanda talks are expected to resemble the inclusive national dialogue formats previously held in Nairobi, as well as those advocated by religious leaders, particularly the Catholic and Anglican churches.
However, for the AFC/M23, the Luanda framework may lack the leverage of the Doha process. The group argues that broader national dialogues tend to overlook specific issues directly affecting them, such as the release of hundreds of their detained members, which they consider central to any lasting agreement.
As diplomatic maneuvering continues, uncertainty remains over which mediation track-Luanda, Doha, or another format-will ultimately shape the future of peace efforts in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo.

The group argues that broader national dialogues tend to overlook specific issues directly affecting them, such as the release of hundreds of their detained members, which they consider central to any lasting agreement.
As diplomatic maneuvering continues, uncertainty remains over which mediation track-Luanda, Doha, or another format-will ultimately shape the future of peace efforts in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo.

body_en:
Rwandan soldiers serving with the MINUSCA peacekeeping mission in the Bria region of the Central African Republic have been awarded United Nations medals in recognition of their professionalism and contributions to restoring peace.
The awards were presented to soldiers from the RWABG VII battalion and the RWAMED X medical team during a ceremony at the RWABG VII battalion camp in Haute-Kotto prefecture.
The ceremony was attended by Maj Gen Maychel Asmi, Deputy Commander of MINUSCA, and Olivier Kayumba, Rwandan Ambassador to the Central African Republic. Maj Gen Asmi praised the Rwandan troops for their conduct, discipline, and productive work, highlighting their role in the smooth conduct of recent presidential elections won by Faustin Archange Touadéra.
The RWABG VII battalion was recognized for maintaining security in Bria, Ouadda, and Sam-Ouandja, while RWAMED X was commended for providing medical support to both fellow peacekeepers and the local population.
Lt Col Willy Ntagara, Commander of RWABG VII, and Col Dr. Simon R. Nyagasaza, Commander of RWAMED X, noted that the medals would strengthen their commitment to their duties, which include protecting civilians, senior officials, UN personnel, infrastructure, and key installations such as M’Poko International Airport.
Rwandan troops first deployed to the Central African Republic in 2014, and in 2020, special forces were sent as part of the CAR-Rwanda partnership to quell unrest linked to armed groups allegedly supported by former president François Bozizé. Their ongoing mission remains focused on maintaining security and supporting peace in the region.

excerpt_en: The Minister of Finance of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Adolphe Muzito, stated on 8 January that former President Joseph Kabila Kabange should not be considered an enemy of the state, despite a death sentence handed down by the DRC’s High Military Court. Kabila, who led
body_en:
The Minister of Finance of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Adolphe Muzito, stated on 8 January that former President Joseph Kabila Kabange should not be considered an enemy of the state, despite a death sentence handed down by the DRC’s High Military Court.
Kabila, who led the country from 2001 to 2019, has had a strained relationship with current President Félix Tshisekedi. Following accusations that he collaborated with the AFC/M23 rebel group controlling large parts of eastern DRC, Kabila fled to South Africa at the end of 2023.
In September 2025, the High Military Court confirmed Kabila as the leader of AFC/M23, found him guilty of treason, war crimes, crimes against humanity, and membership in an illegal armed group, and sentenced him to death.
During an interview with France 24, Muzito, who has been Finance Minister under Tshisekedi since August 2025, clarified his position:
“He is not an enemy of the DRC. I am not commenting on the court’s decision. We are a country at war, it is a military court that has made a decision. I am not commenting.”
When asked if he believed Tshisekedi would carry out the death sentence if Kabila were arrested, Muzito responded that, to his knowledge, the President would not do so.
Muzito’s remarks come amid ongoing political tensions in the DRC over Kabila’s alleged role with rebel forces and reflect a cautious approach to a highly sensitive issue.

title: DRC: President Tshisekedi Seeks New Kinshasa Peace Talks with AFC/M23
excerpt: Kinshasa/Luanda - 8 January 2026: President Félix Tshisekedi Tshilombo of the Democratic Republic of Congo has requested that new peace talks between his government and the AFC/M23 coalition take place in Kinshasa, signaling a shift from the ongoing Doha mediation led by Qatar. T
title_en: DRC: President Tshisekedi Seeks New Kinshasa Peace Talks with AFC/M23
excerpt_en: Kinshasa/Luanda - 8 January 2026: President Félix Tshisekedi Tshilombo of the Democratic Republic of Congo has requested that new peace talks between his government and the AFC/M23 coalition take place in Kinshasa, signaling a shift from the ongoing Doha mediation led by Qatar. T
body_en:
Kinshasa/Luanda - 8 January 2026: President Félix Tshisekedi Tshilombo of the Democratic Republic of Congo has requested that new peace talks between his government and the AFC/M23 coalition take place in Kinshasa, signaling a shift from the ongoing Doha mediation led by Qatar.
Tshisekedi traveled to Luanda, Angola, on 14 December 2025 and returned on 5 January 2026. On 8 January, he again met Angolan President João Gonçalves Lourenço to discuss strategies for restoring peace and security in eastern DRC. During these discussions, Tshisekedi asked Lourenço to initiate new inclusive talks involving all Congolese affected by the war.
The proposed talks are expected to include:
Government supporters and political opposition
Armed groups, including AFC/M23
Civil society representatives
Religious figures and churches
The Angolan government has reportedly begun contacting several opposition figures who may participate in the new negotiations. Tshisekedi has also agreed, in principle, to the release of some AFC/M23 prisoners, with individual cases reviewed to verify the justification of previous convictions.
Sources in Kinshasa confirm that the President wants the AFC/M23 to declare a ceasefire, with the DRC government taking responsibility for monitoring its implementation.
Tshisekedi continues to reject Doha-based talks despite AFC/M23 leader Corneille Nangaa Yobeluo stating on 31 December 2025 that the DRC government refused to send representatives to two Qatar-led meetings intended to monitor the ceasefire.
The DRC government maintains that AFC/M23 fighters captured the town of Uvira in South Kivu, though the group claims to have withdrawn from the town to resume peace talks under the Doha framework.
These developments indicate that Tshisekedi is pursuing a new, domestically anchored negotiation strategy, potentially sidelining previous international mediation efforts.

excerpt: Livingstone, Zambia - 10 January 2026: Rwanda’s Minister of Defense, Juvenal Marizamunda, participated in a special meeting of the ICGLR (International Conference on the Great Lakes Region) Defense Ministers to discuss security challenges in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (

excerpt_en: Livingstone, Zambia - 10 January 2026: Rwanda’s Minister of Defense, Juvenal Marizamunda, participated in a special meeting of the ICGLR (International Conference on the Great Lakes Region) Defense Ministers to discuss security challenges in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (
body_en:
Livingstone, Zambia - 10 January 2026: Rwanda’s Minister of Defense, Juvenal Marizamunda, participated in a special meeting of the ICGLR (International Conference on the Great Lakes Region) Defense Ministers to discuss security challenges in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).
According to a statement from the Rwandan Ministry of Defense, the meeting focused on ensuring security and facilitating humanitarian operations in the eastern DRC, a region long affected by armed conflict.
The ministerial meeting followed sessions held on 8 January 2026 by the ICGLR Security Expert Group and the Chiefs of Defense of ICGLR member states.
The eastern DRC has experienced decades of conflict, intensified over the past 32 years by former Ex-FAR members and Interahamwe militias, and more recently by clashes between government forces and the AFC/M23 coalition. The region is also threatened by over 260 armed groups, which continue to attack communities, kill civilians, and loot property.
The ICGLR ministers emphasized the need for regional cooperation to stabilize the area and protect civilians while supporting humanitarian operations.

title_en: Angolan and Qatari Foreign Ministers Discuss Rwanda-DRC Peace Efforts
excerpt_en: Doha/Luanda - 10 January 2026: The Foreign Ministers of Angola and Qatar held talks on resolving ongoing issues between Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) through peaceful means. According to a statement from the Qatari Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Sheikh Mohammed
body_en:
Doha/Luanda - 10 January 2026: The Foreign Ministers of Angola and Qatar held talks on resolving ongoing issues between Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) through peaceful means.
According to a statement from the Qatari Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani, Qatar’s Prime Minister and Foreign Minister, spoke by phone with Angolan Foreign Minister Tete Antonio. The discussions focused on peaceful conflict resolution and strengthening international cooperation between the two nations.
The statement emphasized that Qatar supports resolving disputes through dialogue and in accordance with international law to restore peace and security.
Since the deterioration of Rwanda-DRC relations, Qatar has played an active role in mediation. It was first mentioned in reconciliation talks in January 2023, and in March 2025, it helped facilitate meetings between President Paul Kagame of Rwanda and President Félix Tshisekedi of the DRC.
The Qatari-led peace process contributed to the signing of a bilateral peace agreement in Washington, D.C., in December 2025, and Qatar continues to maintain communication between the DRC government and the AFC/M23 rebel movement, which remains in active conflict with the DRC army.

title: DRC Cabinet Issues Warning on Government Communication After Minister Criticizes Army
excerpt: Kinshasa - 8 January 2026: Following critical remarks about the DRC army and intelligence by Minister of Agriculture and Food Security Muhindo Nzangi Butondo, President Félix Tshisekedi and Prime Minister Judith Suminwa have issued strict instructions to government officials rega
title_en: DRC Cabinet Issues Warning on Government Communication After Minister Criticizes Army
excerpt_en: Kinshasa - 8 January 2026: Following critical remarks about the DRC army and intelligence by Minister of Agriculture and Food Security Muhindo Nzangi Butondo, President Félix Tshisekedi and Prime Minister Judith Suminwa have issued strict instructions to government officials rega
body_en:
Kinshasa - 8 January 2026: Following critical remarks about the DRC army and intelligence by Minister of Agriculture and Food Security Muhindo Nzangi Butondo, President Félix Tshisekedi and Prime Minister Judith Suminwa have issued strict instructions to government officials regarding public communication.
At a Cabinet meeting on 8 January, Prime Minister Suminwa emphasized that all government statements must be reliable, properly supervised, and aligned with official policy, particularly on sensitive topics such as military operations, security, public unity, and foreign affairs. She warned that violations of this communication protocol would not be tolerated.
Suminwa stressed that any statements or media appearances by ministers should first be reviewed in coordination with the Minister of Information and relevant offices of the Presidency and Prime Minister to avoid insecurity or diplomatic issues.
The Cabinet meeting followed remarks by Minister Butondo on 5 January 2026, in an interview on the Bosolo na Politik YouTube channel, in which he criticized the FARDC (Armed Forces of the DRC) for fleeing before AFC/M23 forces took Uvira. He stated:
"Give me an example of the capture of Uvira. They announced the capture of Uvira but M23 was still in Luvungi. They tweeted, everyone heard that Uvira had been captured, they left Uvira while the enemy was still 30 kilometers away."
President Tshisekedi and Prime Minister Suminwa indicated that government officials must exercise caution in public comments and ensure all statements reflect a positive image of the country and align with their responsibilities.

title: Rwanda Launches One Stop Center Website to Streamline Investment Services
excerpt: Kigali, January 2, 2026 The Rwanda Development Board (RDB) announced that its One Stop Center (OSC) website will officially launch on January 5, 2026, consolidating a wide range of investment and trade services online to improve accessibility, speed, and transparency. The OSC web
title_en: Rwanda Launches One Stop Center Website to Streamline Investment Services
excerpt_en: Kigali, January 2, 2026 The Rwanda Development Board (RDB) announced that its One Stop Center (OSC) website will officially launch on January 5, 2026, consolidating a wide range of investment and trade services online to improve accessibility, speed, and transparency. The OSC web
body_en:
Kigali, January 2, 2026
The Rwanda Development Board (RDB) announced that its One Stop Center (OSC) website will officially launch on January 5, 2026, consolidating a wide range of investment and trade services online to improve accessibility, speed, and transparency.
The OSC website, accessible at http://onestopcentre.rdb.rw, will allow users to apply for permits, track applications, and access services previously scattered across multiple institutions.
RDB Director General Jean-Guy Afrika said the initiative will integrate over 460 services from 24 institutions, covering areas such as construction permits and agricultural processing licenses, with more services expected to be added in the coming months.
“RDB is on a journey to modernize the way it provides services through the One Stop Center. The goal is to simplify service delivery, reduce application processing times, and increase transparency,” Afrika said.
The move builds on a 2023 revamp of the One Stop Center, which aimed to centralize service provision, and reflects Rwanda’s continued commitment to fostering a favorable business environment for investors.
According to RDB, Rwanda recorded $3.2 billion (over Rwf 4,528 billion) in new investments in 2024, up from $2.4 billion in 2023, reinforcing the country’s position as a leading investment destination in the region.
By consolidating services digitally, the OSC website is expected to facilitate investor engagement, reduce bureaucracy, and accelerate project implementation across the country.

title: Funding Secured for Major Expansion of Karenge Waterworks in Rwanda
excerpt: Rwamagana, January 3, 2026 The Rwamagana District Administration has announced that funding has been fully secured for the expansion and distribution project of the Karenge Waterworks, with the first phase of construction already reaching a satisfactory level of completion. The K
title_en: Funding Secured for Major Expansion of Karenge Waterworks in Rwanda
excerpt_en: Rwamagana, January 3, 2026 The Rwamagana District Administration has announced that funding has been fully secured for the expansion and distribution project of the Karenge Waterworks, with the first phase of construction already reaching a satisfactory level of completion. The K
body_en:
Rwamagana, January 3, 2026
The Rwamagana District Administration has announced that funding has been fully secured for the expansion and distribution project of the Karenge Waterworks, with the first phase of construction already reaching a satisfactory level of completion.
The Karenge Waterworks is a strategic infrastructure project expected to significantly increase water supply to Rwamagana town, the district’s industrial zone, and parts of Kigali City. Under the expansion plan, the plant’s production capacity will rise from 12,000 cubic meters per day to 48,000 cubic meters, a fourfold increase.
The initial agreement for the expansion was signed between Rwanda and Hungary. More recently, on November 28, 2025, the Cabinet approved the final ratification of a financing agreement between the Government of Rwanda and the Abu Dhabi Fund for Economic Development, which is providing a loan of 34.7 billion Rwandan francs to support the expansion of the water transportation and distribution system linked to the Karenge plant.
Rwamagana District Mayor Mbonyumuvunyi Radjab confirmed that construction works are underway and progressing well. He explained that once operational, water from the Karenge plant will be shared between Kigali City and Rwamagana District, with part directed to the industrial area and the remainder distributed to households.
The Abu Dhabi-funded component of the project will focus on the construction of water reservoirs and the installation of large transmission pipelines, covering more than 40 kilometers, to ensure water reaches different sectors of the district. These pipelines will connect to secondary distribution networks serving residential areas.
According to the mayor, the project is planned over three years, with the first year nearing completion. Trial distribution of water to the population is expected to begin within the coming months.
Currently, 93% of Rwamagana District’s population has access to clean water. Local authorities say the ultimate goal of the Karenge Waterworks expansion is to achieve universal access to safe drinking water across the district.

title: Rwanda’s Jet Fuel Storage Reaches 12 Million Liters
excerpt: On January 5, 2026, the Rwanda Energy Corporation (REG) announced that Rwanda’s jet fuel storage capacity now stands at 12 million liters, a figure that reflects the country’s broader position in terms of petroleum storage capacity. Overall, Rwanda has petroleum storage facilitie
title_en: Rwanda’s Jet Fuel Storage Reaches 12 Million Liters
excerpt_en: On January 5, 2026, the Rwanda Energy Corporation (REG) announced that Rwanda’s jet fuel storage capacity now stands at 12 million liters, a figure that reflects the country’s broader position in terms of petroleum storage capacity. Overall, Rwanda has petroleum storage facilitie
body_en:
On January 5, 2026, the Rwanda Energy Corporation (REG) announced that Rwanda’s jet fuel storage capacity now stands at 12 million liters, a figure that reflects the country’s broader position in terms of petroleum storage capacity.
Overall, Rwanda has petroleum storage facilities totaling 118 million liters, combining both government-owned and private storage facilities across the country.
The government’s oil storage facilities in Gatsata have a capacity of 7,200,000 liters, while private oil storage facilities in Kabuye (Kigali City) can store 3,100,000 liters. In Rwabuye (Huye District), government tanks hold 1,900,000 liters, and in Bigogwe (Nyabihu District), government facilities store 3,000,000 liters.
Additional private fuel tanks in Jabana (Kigali City) have a capacity of 10,000,000 liters, while government-owned tanks in Rusororo can store up to 20,000,000 liters. Altogether, Rwanda’s fuel tanks have a combined storage capacity of 45,200,000 liters.
Rwanda’s fuel storage infrastructure includes government-owned tanks in Gatsata with a capacity of 6,700,000 liters and private tanks in Kabuye holding 2,700,000 liters. There are also government fuel oil tanks in Rwabuye with a capacity of 1,900,000 liters, fuel oil tanks in Bigogwe holding 2,000,000 liters, and private fuel oil tanks in Jabana with a capacity of 10,000,000 liters.
In addition, the government operates fuel oil tanks in Rusororo with a capacity of 36,000,000 liters, bringing the total fuel oil storage capacity to 59,300,000 liters. There are also government-owned kerosene tanks in Gatsata with a capacity of 1,500,000 liters.
Regarding aviation fuel, Rwanda operates government-owned jet fuel storage facilities in Rusororo with a capacity of 10,000,000 liters, as well as another facility in Kanombe holding 2,000,000 liters, for a total jet fuel storage capacity of 12 million liters.
By location, Gatsata has a total capacity of 15,400,000 liters of petroleum products, Kabuye holds 5,800,000 liters, Rwabuye stores 3,800,000 liters, and Bigogwe has 5,000,000 liters. Jabana accounts for 20,000,000 liters, Rusororo for 66,000,000 liters, and Kanombe for 2,000,000 liters, together reaching a national storage capacity of 118,000,000 liters.
In March 2025, the Minister of Trade and Industry, Prudence Sebahizi, stated that Rwanda’s petroleum storage capacity exceeded 110 million liters, with plans to expand it to 320 million liters within two years.
He recalled that in 2017, Rwanda consumed around 600,000 liters of petroleum products per day, while storage capacity stood at 111 million liters, enough to last six months. Today, however, due to the increase in vehicles and industrial activity, daily consumption has risen to at least two million liters, meaning current reserves can last no more than two months.
He warned that this situation could become critical in the event of disruptions along regional supply routes, which is why the government is pursuing a strategy to expand national fuel reserves.
Rwanda sources its petroleum products primarily from Arab countries, while also importing from East Africa, with Tanzania as the main regional supplier, and smaller volumes coming from Kenya.

title: Aterian Plc Posts Rwf210.5 Million Profit from Rwanda Operations in Q4 2025
excerpt: British mining company Aterian Plc has reported a profit of Rwf210.5 million (approximately USD 145,000) from its mining operations in Rwanda for the fourth quarter ended December 31, 2025. In a statement released on January 5, 2026, the company said its business in Rwanda contin
title_en: Aterian Plc Posts Rwf210.5 Million Profit from Rwanda Operations in Q4 2025
excerpt_en: British mining company Aterian Plc has reported a profit of Rwf210.5 million (approximately USD 145,000) from its mining operations in Rwanda for the fourth quarter ended December 31, 2025. In a statement released on January 5, 2026, the company said its business in Rwanda contin
body_en:
British mining company Aterian Plc has reported a profit of Rwf210.5 million (approximately USD 145,000) from its mining operations in Rwanda for the fourth quarter ended December 31, 2025.
In a statement released on January 5, 2026, the company said its business in Rwanda continues to grow, alongside ongoing mineral exploration and research activities in the country.
Aterian noted that the volume of minerals traded fell short of government targets, explaining that the company prioritized compliance with international standards over production volumes.
Commenting on the results, Aterian CEO Charles Bray said the fourth-quarter performance reflects the company’s solid business position and expressed confidence in continued growth in 2026.
“We believe that the results achieved in the fourth quarter of 2025 demonstrate the opportunities in the company’s business and provide a foundation for what can be done in 2026, depending on the available capital and the market situation,” Bray said.
He added that the company will remain focused on meeting international regulatory requirements governing the trade of precious metals, as well as the expectations of global buyers and regulators.
Aterian Plc also confirmed that it identified lithium deposits in Rwanda following exploration activities that began in 2023. This discovery led Rio Tinto and Mining Exploration, in partnership with Aterian, to commit USD 7.5 million to lithium mining projects.
According to national data, Rwanda’s mining sector generated USD 1.6 billion in revenue in the 2024/2025 period, driven by strong exports of tin, tungsten, tantalum, and gold to international markets.

excerpt_en: Kigali, 9 January 2026: GTBank (Rwanda) Plc, in partnership with Rswitch, has introduced a new technology platform designed to make it easier for traders to access loans without collateral, supporting Rwanda’s ongoing push for digital payments and cashless transactions. The new s
body_en:
Kigali, 9 January 2026: GTBank (Rwanda) Plc, in partnership with Rswitch, has introduced a new technology platform designed to make it easier for traders to access loans without collateral, supporting Rwanda’s ongoing push for digital payments and cashless transactions.
The new system, called ‘M-Pay’, enables merchants to receive payments directly into their GTBank accounts without any fees, while also providing collateral-free loans of up to 2 million Rwandan francs. Repayment is structured over 12 months at an interest rate of 3.99%.
Through the M-Pay system:
Customers can pay merchants using a USSD code (18212USSD Code#) with the payment going directly to the merchant’s account.
Merchants, such as hotel owners, can set up multiple payment methods without risking theft.
Customers do not need a GTBank account to make payments.
GTBank account holders can pay via 6005#, sending money directly to the merchant’s M-Pay code without deductions for either party.
GTBank says the platform aligns with Rwanda’s national direction to promote digital payments, reduce reliance on cash, and provide financial services to small and medium-sized traders more efficiently.
This innovation is expected to empower businesses, facilitate safer transactions, and improve access to credit across the country.
Social and Health

title_en: Rwanda - Rubavu District Distributes Over 12,000 Cows to Fight Poverty
excerpt_en: Rubavu, December 31, 2025 The Rubavu District Administration has announced that more than 12,000 cows have been distributed to local residents under the Girinka program since 2006, as part of ongoing efforts to combat poverty and promote self-sufficiency. During a program visit i
body_en:
Rubavu, December 31, 2025
The Rubavu District Administration has announced that more than 12,000 cows have been distributed to local residents under the Girinka program since 2006, as part of ongoing efforts to combat poverty and promote self-sufficiency.
During a program visit in Kanzenze Sector, Kirerema Cell, 30 cows were handed over to beneficiaries, highlighting the district’s commitment to improving livelihoods.
Mayor Mulindwa Prosper described a cow as a “factory” for households, explaining that it provides fertilizer, milk for nutrition, income from sales, and contributes to overall economic growth. “We ask those who have cows to feed them well, clean them, and insure them so they provide a good yield,” he said.
The Mayor also emphasized the broader economic potential of the program, urging residents not to focus solely on raising cows but to exploit business opportunities, including the foreign market, to maximize benefits.
According to the Ministry of Local Government, Rubavu District has helped 49.7% of residents escape poverty in the last three years, compared to the national average of 62.4%.
Since the launch of the Girinka program in Rwanda in 2006, 12,647 cows have been distributed in Rubavu, with 5,986 received as donations, bringing the total number of cows in the district to 32,645.

title_en: Kigali - First Day of 2026 Sees Quiet Streets and Limited Activities
excerpt_en: Kigali, January 1, 2026 The first day of 2026 in Kigali was marked by unusually low activity and sparse crowds, as many residents chose to spend the day quietly following New Year celebrations. Unlike the chaotic closing and opening nights of the previous year, streets and commer
body_en:
Kigali, January 1, 2026
The first day of 2026 in Kigali was marked by unusually low activity and sparse crowds, as many residents chose to spend the day quietly following New Year celebrations. Unlike the chaotic closing and opening nights of the previous year, streets and commercial areas were largely empty, with few people and vehicles moving around the city.
In neighborhoods such as Nyamirambo and the city center, residents explained that the first day of the year is often dedicated to visiting family and friends, or resting after late-night festivities. Church attendance was modest, as many had already spent the night in prayer and returned home in the morning.
Eric Twizerimana, who spent New Year’s Eve in church, said he planned to spend the day socializing with friends and family while keeping his faith central: “Everyone celebrates holidays in general. I started the last year in church and will start this year in the same spirit. This new year, I have many resolutions, but the Lord will enable us.”
Business owners also noted the quiet day. Jean Pierre Maniraghuha, a household appliance seller in Nyamirambo, said customers were slowly returning, but he went to work regardless: “We started the year in church at night, but our daily lives are sustained by work. Even one customer is worth attending to, and this year I am planning to innovate and expand my business.”
Typically busy areas, such as Downtown Station, were almost empty, with many shops remaining closed. Some churches, particularly Catholic parishes, held services to start the new year, with families participating in baptisms and masses that emphasized love, faith, and community.
Evening gatherings also brought some activity, as certain churches combined worship with entertainment, attracting small crowds, but overall the first day of 2026 in Kigali was calm, reflecting a mix of religious devotion, family visits, and rest after the New Year celebrations.

title_en: Rwanda: Eight Fatal Accidents Recorded During Christmas and New Year Holidays
excerpt_en: Kigali, January 2, 2026 Rwanda National Police (RNP) reported eight serious accidents over the Christmas and New Year period, spanning December 24, 2025, to January 2, 2026. Police Spokesperson ACP Boniface Rutikanga noted that these incidents occurred despite the generally smoot
body_en:
Kigali, January 2, 2026
Rwanda National Police (RNP) reported eight serious accidents over the Christmas and New Year period, spanning December 24, 2025, to January 2, 2026. Police Spokesperson ACP Boniface Rutikanga noted that these incidents occurred despite the generally smooth and secure conduct of festivities across the country.
“It was a week filled with travel, concerts, and entertainment. Security was good, and residents were able to enjoy the celebrations safely,” ACP Rutikanga said, emphasizing that minor incidents linked to drunkenness did not disrupt the overall festivities.
The accidents were evenly split between the holiday periods: four serious accidents occurred on December 24-25, 2025, and four more between December 31, 2025, and January 1, 2026. While exact casualty figures were not disclosed, these accidents contributed to the holiday’s tragic toll.
In addition to accidents, the police arrested 95 people nationwide for driving under the influence of alcohol, with 75% of offenders operating motorcycles or bicycles. Bunani recorded the highest number of arrests, with 47 individuals detained.
RNP reminded the public that Rwanda’s traffic laws impose fines of 150,000 Rwf, vehicle impoundment up to seven days, and possible imprisonment from seven days to two months for driving under the influence.
ACP Rutikanga also highlighted that road safety remains a significant concern in Rwanda, citing that 41,164 accidents occurred between 2022 and October 2025, resulting in 2,907 deaths, often caused by speeding, distracted driving, and driving under the influence.
“We urge residents to comply with traffic safety programs to prevent accidents and ensure public safety,” he concluded.

title: Rwanda Launches Home-Based Cervical Cancer Screening Program
excerpt: Kigali, January 4, 2026 - Rwanda has officially launched a home-based cervical cancer screening program, enabling women to self-test at home without visiting a health facility. The initiative, announced by the Rwanda National Cancer Institute (RNCI), aims to expand access to scre
title_en: Rwanda Launches Home-Based Cervical Cancer Screening Program
excerpt_en: Kigali, January 4, 2026 - Rwanda has officially launched a home-based cervical cancer screening program, enabling women to self-test at home without visiting a health facility. The initiative, announced by the Rwanda National Cancer Institute (RNCI), aims to expand access to scre
body_en:
Kigali, January 4, 2026 - Rwanda has officially launched a home-based cervical cancer screening program, enabling women to self-test at home without visiting a health facility. The initiative, announced by the Rwanda National Cancer Institute (RNCI), aims to expand access to screening and remove barriers that have long limited early detection.
Under the program, women use a self-sampling device at home. The sample is then collected and analyzed at a specialized laboratory to detect human papillomavirus (HPV), the leading cause of cervical cancer. Once results are available, women are informed by a health professional, and those who test positive for HPV are referred for further medical evaluation or treatment.
The screening is free of charge and targets women aged 30 and above, including those without symptoms. Health officials stress that cervical cancer often develops silently, making early screening essential for prevention and survival.
Although the program was piloted six months ago, initial uptake was limited. Authorities say the home-based approach is designed to overcome challenges such as shame, embarrassment, fear of examinations, and limited access to doctors, while remaining as reliable as conventional clinical screening.
Participating private health facilities include Legacy Clinic, DMC Carrefour, Good Life, Bien Naitre, Bwiza Medical, MBC Hospital, Polyclinic Medico-Social, and Saint Jean Polyclinique in Nyarugenge.
According to national cancer data, between 600 and 800 new cervical cancer cases are diagnosed each year in Rwanda, with around 600 deaths annually, highlighting the urgency of prevention efforts.
Rwanda aims to eliminate cervical cancer by 2027, in line with the WHO 90-70-90 strategy, which targets:
90% HPV vaccination coverage among girls aged 13-15,
70% screening of women aged 29-49, and
90% treatment for women diagnosed with early-stage disease.
Health authorities emphasize that early detection saves lives and that the new program empowers women to take control of their health while accelerating progress toward national elimination goals.

title_en: Rwanda: RadioTV10 Journalist Arrested After Assault at Kigali Concert
excerpt_en: Kigali, January 1, 2026 The Rwanda Investigation Bureau (RIB) has confirmed the arrest of journalist Ndahiro Emmanuel, also known as ‘Taikun’, following an incident at a New Year concert organized by the City of Kigali at the Kigali Convention Centre. According to RIB, Ndahiro al
body_en:
Kigali, January 1, 2026
The Rwanda Investigation Bureau (RIB) has confirmed the arrest of journalist Ndahiro Emmanuel, also known as ‘Taikun’, following an incident at a New Year concert organized by the City of Kigali at the Kigali Convention Centre.
According to RIB, Ndahiro allegedly assaulted a security guard, causing injury, property damage, and using threatening language. He is currently being held at the RIB Kimihurura Station while investigations continue.
Dr. Murangira B. Thierry, spokesperson for RIB, emphasized that under Rwandan law, anyone who intentionally injures or assaults another person may face imprisonment and fines. Penalties vary depending on the severity of the injury:
Minor injuries: 6 months to 1 year in prison, with fines between 100,000 and 300,000 Rwf.
Serious injuries causing incapacity: 3 to 5 years in prison, with fines between 500,000 and 1,000,000 Rwf.
Permanent disability or terminal illness caused: Higher penalties apply.
RIB reminded the public to exercise restraint during holidays and celebrations, warning that excessive drinking and reckless behavior can lead to criminal charges and imprisonment. Authorities called for tolerance and adherence to the law to ensure public safety.

Kamanzi Dalaus - former High Court judge

Nsengiyumva Jean Claude - President of the High Court, Rusizi Chamber

Byukusenge Marie Claire - Advisor, Office of the Vice President of the Supreme Court
Bandora Jean Baptiste & Murererehe Saouda - Court Inspectors

body_en:
The Nyarugenge High Court has confirmed that Uzabakiriho Cyprien, known as Djihad, along with Ishimwe Patrick, Ishimwe François Xavier, and Kwizera Nestor, also known as Pappy Nesta, will remain in detention pending trial. The decision was issued during an appeal hearing held on January 5, 2026.
The court ruled that the grounds for appeal presented by Djihad were unfounded and upheld the earlier decision ordering his continued detention.
Regarding Ishimwe Patrick, also known as Pazzo Man, the court found that the reasons cited by the Kicukiro Primary Court to place him in provisional detention were justified, and therefore rejected his request for immediate release on bail.
For Ishimwe François Xavier, the judges concluded that there were serious grounds to suspect his involvement in the sale of pornographic videos. As a result, the court upheld the decision to keep him in temporary detention.
The court also dismissed the arguments raised by Kwizera Nestor (Pappy Nesta), finding them without merit.
However, Kalisa John, widely known as K. John, who is also implicated in the same case, was released on bail and will stand trial while out of custody.
The four detainees are accused of distributing explicit videos involving Yampano and his girlfriend. All had previously expressed dissatisfaction with the ruling of the Kicukiro Primary Court, arguing that it failed to take into account certain elements presented during earlier proceedings.

body_en:
On January 7, 2026, the Rwanda National Police in the Eastern Province reported that Dukuzumuremyi Eric, a suspect wanted for the robbery and murder of a motorcyclist in Kirehe District, was shot dead after attempting to flee from law enforcement.
According to Eastern Province Police Spokesperson SP Hamdun Twizeyimana, Dukuzumuremyi had previously ambushed a motorcyclist on January 2, 2026, killing him and stealing his motorcycle. Following the attack, the police launched a search with help from local residents, eventually locating the suspect in Nyagatare District.
On the morning of January 7, Dukuzumuremyi was being escorted by officers to reveal the locations where he had hidden stolen items. During the process, he attempted to escape, prompting the police to open fire, resulting in his death.
SP Twizeyimana urged the public to refrain from theft, reminding citizens that security forces remain vigilant and that stealing is a serious crime with legal consequences.
