title: Zero Tolerance for Corruption Drives Indian Investment in Rwanda
excerpt: New Delhi/Kigali, January 13, 2026 - Rwanda’s strong stance against corruption and its business-friendly environment are key factors behind the surge in Indian investment, according to Rwanda’s Ambassador to India, Jacqueline Mukangira. Speaking to the Indian news agency IANS on
title_en: Zero Tolerance for Corruption Drives Indian Investment in Rwanda
excerpt_en: New Delhi/Kigali, January 13, 2026 - Rwanda’s strong stance against corruption and its business-friendly environment are key factors behind the surge in Indian investment, according to Rwanda’s Ambassador to India, Jacqueline Mukangira. Speaking to the Indian news agency IANS on
body_en:
New Delhi/Kigali, January 13, 2026 - Rwanda’s strong stance against corruption and its business-friendly environment are key factors behind the surge in Indian investment, according to Rwanda’s Ambassador to India, Jacqueline Mukangira.
Speaking to the Indian news agency IANS on January 11, 2026, during the Vibrant Gujarat Regional Conference, Ambassador Mukangira said Rwanda’s stable legal framework, ease of doing business, and strict anti-corruption policies continue to attract investors from India, particularly from the state of Gujarat.
“Rwanda is a good place to invest because investors are facilitated in many ways, including tax incentives and other business-friendly measures,” she said. “Another important factor is that both local and foreign investors operate in an environment of zero tolerance for corruption.”
She noted that Rwanda and India maintain strong diplomatic and economic relations, with Indian businesses playing a major role in Rwanda’s economy.
“Rwanda and India have excellent relations, and many Indians are doing business in Rwanda, especially from Gujarat,” Mukangira said. “India is the second-largest investor in Rwanda and also ranks second in terms of trade.”
Rwanda imports a wide range of goods from India, including medicines, technological equipment, clothing, rice, and sugar, much of which originates from Gujarat.
According to the Rwanda Development Board (RDB), India was Rwanda’s second-largest investor in 2024, after China. That year, China invested $460 million (14.1% of total investment), while India invested $445.1 million (13.6%).
Diplomatic ties between the two countries have deepened in recent years. Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi paid his first official visit to Rwanda in 2018, following visits by President Paul Kagame in 2017 and 2018. During Prime Minister Modi’s visit, several agreements were signed, including a $200 million grant and support for Rwanda’s Girinka Munyarwanda program, through which he donated 200 cows.

title: Rwanda Introduces Demerit Point System for Drivers; Cross-Border Drivers Exempt

title_en: Rwanda Introduces Demerit Point System for Drivers; Cross-Border Drivers Exempt
excerpt_en: Kigali, January 14, 2026 - Rwanda is set to implement a new electronic demerit point system to monitor drivers’ behavior on the roads, but drivers of cross-border vehicles will not be affected. According to Alfred Byiringiro, Senior Technical Advisor in charge of transport at the
body_en:
Kigali, January 14, 2026 - Rwanda is set to implement a new electronic demerit point system to monitor drivers’ behavior on the roads, but drivers of cross-border vehicles will not be affected.
According to Alfred Byiringiro, Senior Technical Advisor in charge of transport at the Ministry of Infrastructure, the system will apply only to driving licenses issued in Rwanda and those issued abroad but held by permanent residents. Drivers temporarily transiting through Rwanda, such as those transporting goods across borders, will not be registered in the system.
“We have drivers who transit Rwanda temporarily, making multiple trips with cross-border vehicles. It is not possible to register these people. However, if someone chooses to stay in Rwanda, their license is registered and the points system is applied,” Byiringiro explained.
The new law, pending presidential approval, will be accompanied by a ministerial decree defining traffic offenses, penalties, and the number of points deducted for each violation.
Key provisions of the system include:
Every licensed driver starts with 15 points, which are deducted depending on the severity of offenses.
Minor offenses may result in 2 to 6 points being deducted, while serious offenses such as hit-and-run may incur an additional six-point penalty.
Points are reset annually, with deductions applied for offenses committed during the year.
If a driver cannot be immediately identified, points will be assigned to the vehicle number and applied to the driver once identified.
Drivers with suspended or revoked licenses are prohibited from driving in Rwanda, even with a foreign-issued license. Suspended licenses are reinstated after the period expires, while revocations are carried out by a court upon request from road safety authorities.
Byiringiro noted that the government hopes neighboring countries will adopt similar systems to harmonize cross-border road safety regulations.

title: RDB Raises Alarm Over Surge in Poaching at Volcanoes National Park
excerpt: Kigali, January 18, 2026 - The Rwanda Development Board (RDB) has expressed serious concern over the sharp increase in poaching at Volcanoes National Park, warning that the trend threatens both wildlife conservation and national development. According to RDB figures, the number o
title_en: RDB Raises Alarm Over Surge in Poaching at Volcanoes National Park
excerpt_en: Kigali, January 18, 2026 - The Rwanda Development Board (RDB) has expressed serious concern over the sharp increase in poaching at Volcanoes National Park, warning that the trend threatens both wildlife conservation and national development. According to RDB figures, the number o
body_en:
Kigali, January 18, 2026 - The Rwanda Development Board (RDB) has expressed serious concern over the sharp increase in poaching at Volcanoes National Park, warning that the trend threatens both wildlife conservation and national development.
According to RDB figures, the number of animal traps has risen steadily in recent years. In 2023, about 2,200 traps were recorded, increasing to over 2,300 in 2024, and reaching 2,336 by October 2025, compared to just 446 in 2019.
The Commander of the 505th Brigade operating in Musanze, Gakenke, and Burera Districts, Col. Steven Kayigumire, said poaching has become widespread and costly for the country.
“There is a serious problem of poaching, and it is causing significant losses. If we are not vigilant, we could lose more than 500 million Rwf,” he warned.
The Director of Conservation at Rwanda Parks, Ngoga Télesphore, also expressed concern, noting that poaching is increasing despite ongoing efforts to support communities around the park.
“It is worrying that people who benefit from the park are involved in its destruction. The rate of poaching in the last 10 months is higher than in the previous year,” he said.
While the causes of the increase are still under investigation, authorities have called on the public to actively participate in conservation efforts.
“Those who understand the benefits of the park should help sensitize others to respect and protect it. Everyone should be an eye for their neighbor,” Télesphore added.
The Governor of the Northern Province, Mugabowagahunde Maurice, said the issue is being addressed by multiple institutions, describing the situation as alarming.
Authorities revealed that in 2025, six gorillas were caught in poachers’ traps. The most affected sectors include Kinigi with over 800 traps, Bugeshi with more than 500, Kabatwa with over 300, and Gataraga with 287.
So far, 38 poachers have been arrested and imprisoned for activities that endanger wildlife. Local leaders and residents say the exact causes of the surge remain unclear but confirm that measures are being taken to address the problem.

title: Rwanda Launches Private Sector Procurement Platform ‘e-Bid’
excerpt: Kigali, January 19, 2026 - A new private sector procurement platform has been launched in Rwanda, aiming to modernize how companies manage tenders and submit bids. The platform, called e-Bid, was developed by Orion Systems & Design, a Rwandan technology company known for building
title_en: Rwanda Launches Private Sector Procurement Platform ‘e-Bid’
excerpt_en: Kigali, January 19, 2026 - A new private sector procurement platform has been launched in Rwanda, aiming to modernize how companies manage tenders and submit bids. The platform, called e-Bid, was developed by Orion Systems & Design, a Rwandan technology company known for building
body_en:
Kigali, January 19, 2026 - A new private sector procurement platform has been launched in Rwanda, aiming to modernize how companies manage tenders and submit bids.
The platform, called e-Bid, was developed by Orion Systems & Design, a Rwandan technology company known for building mobile banking applications used across Rwanda and other African countries. It was unveiled at a private sector software conference held in Kigali on January 16, 2026.
Software engineer Muhire Victor, the project’s lead developer, said the idea was inspired by the government’s procurement platform, Umucyo, after observing how it addressed long-standing challenges in public procurement.
“In the past, tenders were submitted manually, and documents were sometimes lost, causing bidders to lose opportunities,” Muhire explained. “We realized there was an electronic solution, but it was only available to government tenders. The private sector had no such platform.”
As a result, e-Bid was created to serve private companies, and more than 50 private tenders have already been submitted through the platform.
Muhire said the system allows tender announcements, online submission of bid documents, and selection of winners without requiring physical meetings. “The tender issuer can choose to receive bids electronically and select the winning contractor directly through the platform,” he said.
He added that bidder information remains confidential between the bidder and the tender issuer, with platform administrators having no access to the content of submissions.
On the government platform umucyo.gov.rw, contractors can already find tender notices, submit bid documents, and have winners selected without public opening sessions - a model e-Bid aims to replicate for the private sector.
Founded in 2013, Orion Systems & Design operates in Rwanda and four other African countries. The company is among the few Rwandan firms to have received the Digital Trust Seal, a certification awarded by the Software Testing Qualifications Board, with only 16 Rwandan software companies holding the distinction so far.
Rwanda is one of 73 countries worldwide offering the Digital Trust Seal, reflecting its growing technological capacity and international credibility.
Muhire said investment in software development in Rwanda is both demanding and profitable, citing government programs that support the sector. Since its founding, Orion Systems & Design has developed multiple software solutions used by banks and financial institutions across the region.
He encouraged young innovators to pursue technology development, noting that Rwanda offers strong opportunities for those with the skills to create digital solutions.

title: Senator Murigande: “It Is Incomprehensible That People Are Dying of Hunger in Rwanda”
excerpt: Kigali, January 19, 2026 - Senator Dr. Charles Murigande has expressed concern that people are dying of hunger in Rwanda, a country with favorable rainfall and strong agricultural potential, calling for intensified research to boost food production. He made the remarks on January
title_en: Senator Murigande: “It Is Incomprehensible That People Are Dying of Hunger in Rwanda”
excerpt_en: Kigali, January 19, 2026 - Senator Dr. Charles Murigande has expressed concern that people are dying of hunger in Rwanda, a country with favorable rainfall and strong agricultural potential, calling for intensified research to boost food production. He made the remarks on January
body_en:
Kigali, January 19, 2026 - Senator Dr. Charles Murigande has expressed concern that people are dying of hunger in Rwanda, a country with favorable rainfall and strong agricultural potential, calling for intensified research to boost food production.
He made the remarks on January 19, 2026, during a session of the Rwandan Senate with the Minister of Agriculture and Livestock, who presented the current state of the sector.
Dr. Murigande stressed that greater investment in agricultural research is essential to determine which crops are best suited to Rwanda, how yields can be increased, and how the sector can be modernized.
He noted that Rwanda has a limited land area for farming, making research the main driver of growth in both agriculture and livestock.
“Rwanda’s land is small and we cannot expand it. What will save us is putting more effort into research,” he said.
Drawing a comparison with Israel, Dr. Murigande said it was unacceptable that people in Rwanda face hunger despite having more favorable natural conditions.
“Israel has little land, much of it sandy, yet it produces a great deal because of research. It is incomprehensible that in Rwanda we would starve,” he said.
He added that even when rainfall is uneven, it remains sufficient nationwide and should be better harnessed through scientific methods.
Dr. Murigande also emphasized that research could improve animal feed, seed quality, and overall agricultural productivity.
“Everything will come from sustained research. I want the Minister to tell us about the plans to strengthen research in collaboration with other institutions,” he said.
He further urged the government to leverage the country’s skilled graduates, suggesting that individuals with master’s degrees and advanced training be employed to conduct research, develop suitable seeds, and promote food self-sufficiency.
His remarks come amid ongoing drought in parts of Kayonza District, where residents in the sectors of Ndego, Mwiri, Kabare, and Rwinkwavu continue to face severe food shortages. The crisis contributed to the dismissal of district leaders late last year.
Responding to the concerns, Minister of Agriculture and Livestock Dr. Ndabamenye Telesphore said the government is prioritizing research to guide investment and technology adoption.
He warned that if current farming practices continue, Rwanda will struggle to achieve food self-sufficiency by 2050, when the population is projected to reach 22 million. Under traditional methods, the country would need 10.3 million hectares of arable land-an impossible target.
However, with improved agricultural methods, only 3.4 million hectares would be required, and with international best practices, just 1.4 million hectares would suffice-an achievable goal given that Rwanda currently has more than 1.3 million hectares of arable land.

title_en: Rwanda Highlights Expected Benefits from World Economic Forum in Davos
excerpt_en: Kigali, Rwanda - January 20, 2026 - Rwanda is aiming to capitalize on participation in the World Economic Forum (WEF) Annual Meeting, currently taking place in Davos, Switzerland from January 19-23, 2026. The event marks the 56th edition of the forum and brings together over 3,00
body_en:
Kigali, Rwanda - January 20, 2026 - Rwanda is aiming to capitalize on participation in the World Economic Forum (WEF) Annual Meeting, currently taking place in Davos, Switzerland from January 19-23, 2026. The event marks the 56th edition of the forum and brings together over 3,000 participants from 130 countries, including 65 heads of state, 400 senior officials, business leaders, civil society actors, and researchers.
Rwanda’s delegation is led by Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation Amb. Nduhungirehe Olivier, alongside Minister of Technology and Innovation Ingabire Paula and Director General of the National Development Agency Jean-Guy Afrika.
The theme of this year’s summit focuses on promoting dialogue in problem-solving, offering a platform to explore solutions to global challenges without resorting to conflict.
Minister Nduhungirehe emphasized Rwanda’s unique contributions, citing the country’s achievements in economy and technology. “Rwanda has a Center for the Fourth Industrial Revolution (C4IR) that promotes advanced technologies,” he said, highlighting the country’s growing technological expertise.
He added that the summit presents opportunities to engage with world leaders on development cooperation and to discuss how Africa can leverage its population of 1.4 billion, predominantly young people, for economic growth.
“This meeting is a chance to study how long-standing global conflicts can be resolved through dialogue and to exchange ideas on economic development and population well-being,” Nduhungirehe said.
The World Economic Forum provides Rwanda and Africa a platform to explore collaboration on economic development, technology, and innovation. Since 2022, Rwanda has been one of the few countries to host a C4IR center, affiliated with WEF, promoting artificial intelligence, digital governance, and data management in Africa.
Rwanda previously hosted the WEF Africa Summit in 2016, becoming the fifth African country to do so, reinforcing its position as a hub for innovation and economic dialogue on the continent.

Rwanda previously hosted the WEF Africa Summit in 2016, becoming the fifth African country to do so, reinforcing its position as a hub for innovation and economic dialogue on the continent.

title: DRC Submits List of Minerals for U.S. Investment Under Strategic Partnership
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - January 21, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has sent a list of minerals to the United States, detailing those it is authorized to mine and process under the December 2025 peace and economic cooperation agreement involving Rwanda and supported by Wash
title_en: DRC Submits List of Minerals for U.S. Investment Under Strategic Partnership
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - January 21, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has sent a list of minerals to the United States, detailing those it is authorized to mine and process under the December 2025 peace and economic cooperation agreement involving Rwanda and supported by Wash
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - January 21, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has sent a list of minerals to the United States, detailing those it is authorized to mine and process under the December 2025 peace and economic cooperation agreement involving Rwanda and supported by Washington.
Two DRC officials, speaking on condition of anonymity, confirmed that the list was sent to Washington, D.C., last week.
The agreement includes the establishment of a joint DRC-U.S. committee tasked with overseeing the mineral exploration and investment process. Congolese members include representatives from the economy, foreign affairs, and finance ministries, along with the head of the mining regulator, ARECOMS.
A DRC official explained that the list, which includes manganese, gold, lithium, copper, and cobalt, was prepared after an in-depth analysis of the country’s strategic resources and the U.S. demand for these minerals, especially for electric vehicle batteries and electronic devices.
The list designates specific mining sites where U.S. investors can operate, including Kisenge and Mutoshi mines in Lualaba Province, Moto in Haut-Uélé, Kilo in Ituri, as well as locations in the two Kivus and Maniema.
Following the submission, the United States is expected to review the list, after which the joint committee will begin discussions to plan the implementation of the agreement.

excerpt_en: Islamabad, January 22, 2026 - The Rwandan Embassy in Pakistan, in collaboration with the National Agriculture Export Board (NAEB), has announced the organization of the Rwanda Coffee Festival 2026, scheduled for January 29, 2026, at the Mövenpick Hotel in Islamabad. The festival
body_en:
Islamabad, January 22, 2026 - The Rwandan Embassy in Pakistan, in collaboration with the National Agriculture Export Board (NAEB), has announced the organization of the Rwanda Coffee Festival 2026, scheduled for January 29, 2026, at the Mövenpick Hotel in Islamabad.
The festival aims to promote Rwandan coffee internationally, with a particular focus on expanding trade and investment opportunities in the Pakistani market. Rwanda is renowned for its high-quality highland coffee, recognized for its unique flavor and aroma.
The event will bring together Rwandan delegations, ambassadors, coffee experts, traders, processors, investors, and other stakeholders. Activities will include demonstrations of professional coffee production and preparation, a documentary showcasing the journey of Rwandan coffee from farm to cup, and guided visits to Rwandan coffee export operations.
Coffee remains one of Rwanda’s key economic crops. According to NAEB, Rwandan coffee exports generated over Rwf 216 billion in 2025, up from Rwf 129 billion in 2024, reflecting a significant increase in international demand.

title: MINEDUC Launches ‘Fresheri ku Ishuri’ Campaign to Promote Cleanliness in Schools
excerpt: Kigali, January 12, 2026 - Rwanda’s Ministry of Education (MINEDUC) has launched a nationwide campaign dubbed “Fresheri ku Ishuri” aimed at promoting hygiene and cleanliness among students, both at home and in school environments. The initiative was rolled out across various educ
title_en: MINEDUC Launches ‘Fresheri ku Ishuri’ Campaign to Promote Cleanliness in Schools
excerpt_en: Kigali, January 12, 2026 - Rwanda’s Ministry of Education (MINEDUC) has launched a nationwide campaign dubbed “Fresheri ku Ishuri” aimed at promoting hygiene and cleanliness among students, both at home and in school environments. The initiative was rolled out across various educ
body_en:
Kigali, January 12, 2026 - Rwanda’s Ministry of Education (MINEDUC) has launched a nationwide campaign dubbed “Fresheri ku Ishuri” aimed at promoting hygiene and cleanliness among students, both at home and in school environments.
The initiative was rolled out across various educational institutions on January 12, 2026, with the national launch held at GS Karembure in Kigali. The campaign will run throughout the current academic semester and targets all schools nationwide.
Speaking at the launch, Minister of Education Joseph Nsengimana said the program seeks to instill a culture of cleanliness at an early age, given the large proportion of Rwandans enrolled in school.
“One third of Rwandans are in school. It is therefore necessary to have a special hygiene program related to schools so that cleanliness becomes a long-standing culture among all Rwandans,” he said. “We deliberately chose to start with this semester so that students, school leaders, teachers, and parents can all take part.”
Minister Nsengimana emphasized the critical role of parents in ensuring children maintain good hygiene, noting that a child’s day begins at home.
“When a child leaves home, parents must first ensure the child has bathed, is well-groomed, and is wearing clean, intact clothes before going to school,” he said. “Their role is essential because we cannot succeed without their support.”
He also stressed that a clean and orderly school environment contributes positively to learning, adding that parents should ensure school uniforms are clean and repaired when necessary.
Meanwhile, the Minister of Gender and Family Promotion, Consolée Uwimana, speaking from Notre Dame de Fatima School Center in Musanze, said the campaign will help children develop habits that will shape both their future families and communities.
“When children become familiar with good practices, they internalize them,” she said. “Our country still faces challenges that threaten family well-being, including poor hygiene in the places where we live, study, and work. Starting with children in schools is the best way to build a lasting culture of cleanliness.”
As part of the campaign launch, trees were also planted in several schools to promote clean air and environmental sustainability, reinforcing the broader public health goals of the initiative.

title: Karongi District Launches Census of Unemployed Youth
excerpt: Karongi, January 13, 2026 - Authorities in Karongi District have begun a comprehensive census of unemployed youth in a bid to reduce joblessness and improve access to employment opportunities. The announcement was made by the Deputy Mayor in charge of Social Affairs, Pascasie Umu
title_en: Karongi District Launches Census of Unemployed Youth
excerpt_en: Karongi, January 13, 2026 - Authorities in Karongi District have begun a comprehensive census of unemployed youth in a bid to reduce joblessness and improve access to employment opportunities. The announcement was made by the Deputy Mayor in charge of Social Affairs, Pascasie Umu
body_en:
Karongi, January 13, 2026 - Authorities in Karongi District have begun a comprehensive census of unemployed youth in a bid to reduce joblessness and improve access to employment opportunities.
The announcement was made by the Deputy Mayor in charge of Social Affairs, Pascasie Umuhoza, during a ceremony marking the graduation of 20 young people who completed a six-month training program in cooking and meal preparation.
The training, conducted at Bethel Hotel in Rubengera Sector, forms part of the Rwandan government’s broader initiative to equip unemployed youth with practical skills for the labor market.
According to Vice Mayor Umuhoza, the census will record each unemployed person’s educational background to ensure that job opportunities can be matched more effectively to suitable candidates.
“We are enumerating unemployed youth, and this process is ongoing and will be completed soon,” she said. “In about two weeks, we will have a comprehensive list of all unemployed youth in the district.”
The census is being conducted across all 13 sectors of Karongi District.
Sister Marie Louise Niyonsenga, a leader in the Presbyterian Church in Rwanda (EPR), also known as the Servants of Christ, said the training initiative specifically targets youth because of their central role in national development.
“The skills they learned in cooking and meal preparation will help them secure employment or become self-reliant,” she said. “When young people are unemployed, they lose hope and may turn to drugs or prostitution.”
One of the graduates, Liliane Ukwishana from Nyaruguru District, said she enrolled in the program after spending five years studying history, economics, and social sciences without finding employment.
“I have been saving the money they gave us, and I plan to start a restaurant that will create jobs for other young people,” she said. “I will also share the knowledge I have gained here.”
District leaders emphasized that vocational training remains a key strategy for reducing unemployment among school leavers and recent graduates.

title: Rwanda Hosts African Handball Championship, Focuses on Winning and National Pride
excerpt: Kigali, January 22, 2026 - Rwanda has demonstrated its ability to host major sports competitions while also prioritizing victory, according to Minister of Sports Nelly Mukazayire. Speaking to RBA on January 21, the day the African Handball Championship began in Rwanda, Minister M
title_en: Rwanda Hosts African Handball Championship, Focuses on Winning and National Pride
excerpt_en: Kigali, January 22, 2026 - Rwanda has demonstrated its ability to host major sports competitions while also prioritizing victory, according to Minister of Sports Nelly Mukazayire. Speaking to RBA on January 21, the day the African Handball Championship began in Rwanda, Minister M
body_en:
Kigali, January 22, 2026 - Rwanda has demonstrated its ability to host major sports competitions while also prioritizing victory, according to Minister of Sports Nelly Mukazayire. Speaking to RBA on January 21, the day the African Handball Championship began in Rwanda, Minister Mukazayire emphasized that the country is not only preparing to organize events but also to field competitive teams that make the nation proud.
The tournament, held from January 21 to 31, 2026, brought together 16 teams from across the continent, including Algeria, Angola, Benin, Cameroon, Cape Verde, the Republic of Congo, Egypt, Gabon, Guinea, Kenya, Morocco, Nigeria, Rwanda, Tunisia, Uganda, and Zambia. Rwanda faced Zambia in the opening match, winning decisively 30-19.
Minister Mukazayire highlighted that hosting international competitions enhances the country’s image while also contributing to the development of Rwanda’s tourism sector, a key source of foreign exchange. She stated:
“We are preparing our teams not only to host but to play and to win. We no longer want to be mere hosts; we want to compete at the highest level and bring victory home.”
The championship provided a platform for Rwanda to showcase organizational capacity, national talent, and the growing competitiveness of its athletes, reinforcing the country’s ambition to become a prominent hub for sports in Africa.

title: UN Court Rejects Alfred Musema’s Request for Early Release
excerpt: The International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals (IRMCT) has rejected a request for early release filed by Alfred Musema, a former Rwandan tea factory director convicted for his role in the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi. Musema, 76, was arrested in Switzerland on Feb
title_en: UN Court Rejects Alfred Musema’s Request for Early Release
excerpt_en: The International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals (IRMCT) has rejected a request for early release filed by Alfred Musema, a former Rwandan tea factory director convicted for his role in the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi. Musema, 76, was arrested in Switzerland on Feb
body_en:
The International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals (IRMCT) has rejected a request for early release filed by Alfred Musema, a former Rwandan tea factory director convicted for his role in the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi.
Musema, 76, was arrested in Switzerland on February 11, 1995, and later transferred to the custody of the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda (ICTR). He was found responsible for leading and participating in multiple massacres in Kibuye Prefecture between April and May 1994, including attacks on Gitwa Hill, Muyira, Rwirambo Hill, Mataba, and the Nyakavumu Cave, where more than 300 Tutsis were killed and burned.
On January 27, 2000, the ICTR convicted Musema of genocide, extermination, and rape, sentencing him to life imprisonment. Although the Appeals Chamber later overturned the rape conviction in November 2001, it upheld his life sentence for other crimes against humanity.
After serving part of his sentence in Mali and later in Benin, Musema has made several attempts to secure early release. His first request in August 2019 was rejected because he had not yet served two-thirds of his sentence, based on international standards that equate a life sentence with 45 years of imprisonment. A subsequent appeal was dismissed in January 2020.
In January 2025, Musema again petitioned for early release, citing more than 30 years of detention, good conduct in prison, positive relations with fellow inmates, and acknowledgment that the genocide occurred. He also indicated that he intended to live with his family in Switzerland if released.
In a decision dated January 12, 2026, IRMCT President Graciela Gatti Santana acknowledged Musema’s good behavior and recognition of the genocide but ruled that these factors were insufficient given the gravity of his crimes. The court noted that Musema has neither confessed nor expressed remorse, a key requirement for early release.
The judge further emphasized that Musema was a powerful figure in Kibuye who could have prevented the killings but instead stood by and, in many cases, actively participated. Medical reports also indicated that he is in good health, eliminating humanitarian grounds for release.
As a result, Musema will remain in prison.

title: Kabila’s Party Vice President Aubin Minaku Arrested in Kinshasa
excerpt: Kinshasa, January 18, 2026 - Security forces in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) have arrested Aubin Minaku, the Vice President of former President Joseph Kabila’s PPRD party, during a late-night operation at his home in Kinshasa. The authorities have not disclosed the reas
title_en: Kabila’s Party Vice President Aubin Minaku Arrested in Kinshasa
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, January 18, 2026 - Security forces in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) have arrested Aubin Minaku, the Vice President of former President Joseph Kabila’s PPRD party, during a late-night operation at his home in Kinshasa. The authorities have not disclosed the reas
body_en:
Kinshasa, January 18, 2026 - Security forces in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) have arrested Aubin Minaku, the Vice President of former President Joseph Kabila’s PPRD party, during a late-night operation at his home in Kinshasa.
The authorities have not disclosed the reason for his arrest, but it comes amid ongoing accusations by the Tshisekedi administration against former figures of the Kabila regime, who are suspected of supporting the AFC/M23 coalition.
On March 7, 2025, the DRC government announced that senior leaders of the PPRD were suspected of working with AFC/M23, which is fighting the DRC government. Following these accusations, several PPRD leaders were arrested after President Félix Tshisekedi accused Joseph Kabila of backing the group - claims the PPRD has denied.
Those implicated include the PPRD Permanent Secretary, Emmanuel Ramazani Shadary, the Vice President, Aubin Minaku, and the Deputy Permanent Secretary, Ferdinand Kambere.
The location of Minaku’s detention remains unknown. Sources said his residence was surrounded by FARDC special forces at the time of his arrest.
The PPRD has not yet issued a statement regarding the arrest.
The development follows the recent arrest and detention of Emmanuel Ramazani Shadary, who is being held at an undisclosed location.
This comes as part of broader legal actions against senior PPRD leaders, after the Military Court tried Joseph Kabila in absentia, accusing him of treason and collaboration with AFC/M23, and sentenced him to death.

title: Mother and Son Arrested on Suspicion of Killing Family Patriarch
excerpt: Ruhango, Rwanda - January 19, 2026 - The Rwanda National Police (RNP) have arrested a 60-year-old woman and her 26-year-old son on suspicion of killing her husband and the young man’s father, Birasamasha Donath, aged 70. The incident occurred on January 19, 2026, in Kivomo Villag
title_en: Mother and Son Arrested on Suspicion of Killing Family Patriarch
excerpt_en: Ruhango, Rwanda - January 19, 2026 - The Rwanda National Police (RNP) have arrested a 60-year-old woman and her 26-year-old son on suspicion of killing her husband and the young man’s father, Birasamasha Donath, aged 70. The incident occurred on January 19, 2026, in Kivomo Villag
body_en:
Ruhango, Rwanda - January 19, 2026 - The Rwanda National Police (RNP) have arrested a 60-year-old woman and her 26-year-old son on suspicion of killing her husband and the young man’s father, Birasamasha Donath, aged 70.
The incident occurred on January 19, 2026, in Kivomo Village, Murama Cell, Bweramana Sector, Ruhango District.
According to preliminary information, the woman allegedly asked her son to help her kill the victim following a family dispute, reportedly over property. Responders found Birasamasha’s body covered in blood at the scene.
The RNP Southern Province spokesperson, Chief Inspector of Police (CIP) Kamanzi Hassan, said that local authorities confirmed the family had an ongoing property conflict.
“It is true, it is suspected that this 70-year-old man was killed by his wife and child. The two were immediately arrested and detained at the Kabagari Police Station while investigations continue,” he said.
CIP Kamanzi urged residents to avoid domestic conflicts, promote a culture of dialogue, and seek support from family members, mediators, and local authorities when disputes arise.
The victim’s body was taken to Gitwe Hospital for an autopsy.
Under Rwandan law, intentional homicide is a criminal offense punishable by life imprisonment if convicted.

title: RIB Arrests University Professor Suspected of Child Sexual Abuse
excerpt: Kigali, January 19, 2026 - The Rwanda Investigation Bureau (RIB) has arrested a university professor suspected of sexually abusing minors and deceiving them with promises of money. In a statement released on January 19, 2026, RIB said preliminary investigations indicate that the
title_en: RIB Arrests University Professor Suspected of Child Sexual Abuse
excerpt_en: Kigali, January 19, 2026 - The Rwanda Investigation Bureau (RIB) has arrested a university professor suspected of sexually abusing minors and deceiving them with promises of money. In a statement released on January 19, 2026, RIB said preliminary investigations indicate that the
body_en:
Kigali, January 19, 2026 - The Rwanda Investigation Bureau (RIB) has arrested a university professor suspected of sexually abusing minors and deceiving them with promises of money.
In a statement released on January 19, 2026, RIB said preliminary investigations indicate that the suspect abused several secondary school girls in Bugesera District on different occasions.
The professor, who holds a PhD, is currently being held at the RIB Rwezamenyo Station in Nyarugenge District, and his case has been forwarded to the Prosecution Service.
In its statement, RIB emphasized that rape of a child constitutes a grave violation that destroys the victim’s future, affects families, and harms society as a whole.
The agency warned that sexual abuse of children will not be tolerated and urged minors to avoid individuals who lure them with money or gifts for sexual exploitation.
The issue of child sexual violence remains a serious concern in Rwanda. In February 2025, the Minister of Gender and Family Development, Uwimana Consolée, reported that 22,454 adolescents were raped and impregnated in 2024.
Official statistics indicate that 19,701 adolescents were impregnated in 2020, rising to 23,111 in 2021, 24,472 in 2022, before declining slightly to 22,055 in 2023.
Under Article 14 of Law No. 059/2023 of December 4, 2023, amending Law No. 68/2018, the crime of child rape carries a prison sentence of 20 to 25 years upon conviction.

title: Rwanda Submits Human Rights Progress Report to the UN Highlighting Major Achievements
excerpt: Kigali, Rwanda - January 21, 2026 - The Rwandan Ministry of Justice has submitted a comprehensive report to the United Nations Human Rights Office, detailing the country’s progress on 160 recommendations regarding the protection of human rights. These recommendations, drawn from
title_en: Rwanda Submits Human Rights Progress Report to the UN Highlighting Major Achievements
excerpt_en: Kigali, Rwanda - January 21, 2026 - The Rwandan Ministry of Justice has submitted a comprehensive report to the United Nations Human Rights Office, detailing the country’s progress on 160 recommendations regarding the protection of human rights. These recommendations, drawn from
body_en:
Kigali, Rwanda - January 21, 2026 - The Rwandan Ministry of Justice has submitted a comprehensive report to the United Nations Human Rights Office, detailing the country’s progress on 160 recommendations regarding the protection of human rights. These recommendations, drawn from a broader set of 260 proposals received in 2021, have been implemented at an estimated rate of 97%, according to Minister of Justice and Attorney General Dr. Ugirashebuja Emmanuel.
The report, presented alongside Rwanda’s UN Ambassador Urujeni Bakuramutsa, the Director General of the National Institute of Statistics, Murenzi Ivan, and the Director General of RGB, Dr. Doris Uwiceza, covers all aspects of national life conducted in compliance with human rights standards.
Over the past five years, the Ministry of Justice (MINIJUST) trained about 3,000 security and justice sector personnel, including 673 leaders and judges, on expediting charges, fair trial rights, and combating torture. The National Human Rights Commission conducted inspections in 40 prisons and 103 detention centers, while over 9,300 vulnerable people and 7,000 victims of gender-based violence received free legal aid.
The report highlights good governance, with service delivery improvements via the Irembo platform, increasing from 89 to 220 services, and citizen satisfaction rising from 76.2% to 89.6% by 2024. Rwanda also created over 900,000 jobs from 2022 to 2025, while the number of households with electricity reached 84%, and mobile phone ownership rose from under 10% to 86%, improving access to information. Access to clean water stands at 94%.
In health, the under-five mortality rate fell from 45 per 1,000 children in 2020 to 36 in 2025, hospitals were upgraded to teaching level, and Marburg epidemic response programs were launched, alongside initiatives to quadruple health workforce numbers. Rwanda’s National Agency for Food and Drug Safety attained WHO Category III compliance, becoming the eighth African country to do so.
The report also highlights progress in unity and genocide prevention, including establishing the Ministry of Rwandan Unity and Civic Responsibility and having four Genocide sites listed as UNESCO World Heritage Sites in 2023. Poverty rates fell from 39.8% to 27.4%, lifting 1.5 million people out of extreme poverty, supported by programs like VUP.
In education, Rwanda built 20,781 classrooms, 650 new schools, expanded disability-inclusive centers, and increased teacher capacity, while continuing to raise the education budget. Women’s representation in leadership also increased, with female senior officials in key positions including the Chief Justice, Prosecutor General, and Ombudsman.
Rwanda has hosted refugees from countries such as Afghanistan and Sudan, and advanced environmental protection through the Green Fund, investing over $277 million in 64 projects that created over 100,000 jobs and launching a Carbon Market to mitigate climate change.
Countries including Mexico, Mauritius, Montenegro, Morocco, Mozambique, Nepal, the Netherlands, Niger, Nigeria, Norway, Oman, Paraguay, the Philippines, Portugal, Qatar, Korea, Russia, Senegal, Sierra Leone, Singapore, Somalia, South Africa, South Sudan, Spain, Sudan, Sweden, Togo, and many others recognized Rwanda’s achievements and offered recommendations on NGOs, freedom of expression, and press freedom.
Dr. Ugirashebuja emphasized that Rwanda respects freedom of expression, noting no journalists have been imprisoned or prosecuted in the country. The law governing non-governmental organizations was revised in 2024 to improve compliance and functionality.
Rwanda joined the UN human rights review process in 2011, receiving 67 recommendations, followed by 50 in 2015 and 160 in 2021, on which this report is based, demonstrating significant progress in human rights protection, governance, social development, and economic inclusion.

Rwanda has hosted refugees from countries such as Afghanistan and Sudan, and advanced environmental protection through the Green Fund, investing over $277 million in 64 projects that created over 100,000 jobs and launching a Carbon Market to mitigate climate change.
Countries including Mexico, Mauritius, Montenegro, Morocco, Mozambique, Nepal, the Netherlands, Niger, Nigeria, Norway, Oman, Paraguay, the Philippines, Portugal, Qatar, Korea, Russia, Senegal, Sierra Leone, Singapore, Somalia, South Africa, South Sudan, Spain, Sudan, Sweden, Togo, and many others recognized Rwanda’s achievements and offered recommendations on NGOs, freedom of expression, and press freedom.
Dr. Ugirashebuja emphasized that Rwanda respects freedom of expression, noting no journalists have been imprisoned or prosecuted in the country. The law governing non-governmental organizations was revised in 2024 to improve compliance and functionality.
Rwanda joined the UN human rights review process in 2011, receiving 67 recommendations, followed by 50 in 2015 and 160 in 2021, on which this report is based, demonstrating significant progress in human rights protection, governance, social development, and economic inclusion.

title: Civilian Concerns Mount in Uvira Following AFC/M23 Withdrawal
excerpt: Uvira, South Kivu DRC, January 21, 2026 - After the AFC/M23 rebel group withdrew its fighters from the city of Uvira, civilians remain on edge amid reports of looting and violence. Human Rights Watch (HRW) highlighted that some residents have been targeted by Congolese army (FARD
title_en: Civilian Concerns Mount in Uvira Following AFC/M23 Withdrawal
excerpt_en: Uvira, South Kivu DRC, January 21, 2026 - After the AFC/M23 rebel group withdrew its fighters from the city of Uvira, civilians remain on edge amid reports of looting and violence. Human Rights Watch (HRW) highlighted that some residents have been targeted by Congolese army (FARD
body_en:
Uvira, South Kivu DRC, January 21, 2026 - After the AFC/M23 rebel group withdrew its fighters from the city of Uvira, civilians remain on edge amid reports of looting and violence. Human Rights Watch (HRW) highlighted that some residents have been targeted by Congolese army (FARDC) and Wazalendo militias allegedly demanding valuables, including mobile phones, and in some cases firing on the population.
Starting the morning of January 18, pro-government forces, including FARDC and Wazalendo units, entered the city to restore state authority. However, HRW reports indicate that despite the military presence, residents are facing intimidation and theft, raising concerns about their safety.
“The community fears for its security. Soldiers and Wazalendo are going door to door, demanding phones and firing shots,” a local resident told HRW.
The organization further noted that homes, shops, and places of worship belonging to Banyamulenge residents were heavily looted following the rebel withdrawal, and several civilians sustained injuries. Wazalendo forces reportedly blocked residents from seeking refuge in the surrounding highland areas connecting Uvira, Fizi, and Mwenga territories.
Clémentine de Montjoye, HRW’s Great Lakes researcher, emphasized that the presence of FARDC troops alone is insufficient to protect civilians while Wazalendo continue to operate with impunity.
HRW called on the Congolese government to deploy well-trained forces to disarm Wazalendo and hold accountable those responsible for crimes against civilians, ensuring the safety of the population.

title_en: DRC: Family of AFC/M23 Leader Faces Arrests, Death Sentences Amid Anti-Rebel Operations
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, January 22, 2026 - Several members of Corneille Nangaa Yobeluo’s family, the leader of the AFC/M23 rebel group, have been detained, while others have fled the Democratic Republic of Congo. Among the first arrested was Nangaa’s younger brother, Baseane Nangaa Putters, cu
body_en:
Kinshasa, January 22, 2026 - Several members of Corneille Nangaa Yobeluo’s family, the leader of the AFC/M23 rebel group, have been detained, while others have fled the Democratic Republic of Congo.
Among the first arrested was Nangaa’s younger brother, Baseane Nangaa Putters, currently held at Ndolo Military Prison. Several family members, including Nangaa’s wife, Yvette Lubanda, and his brother-in-law, Fabrice Lubala, have reportedly been sentenced to death.
The latest arrest involves another younger brother, Didier Ilaani Nangaa, who spent over ten days in an intelligence facility in Isiro, Haut-Uélé province, suspected of supporting the AFC/M23 through mining operations.
Another brother, Christophe Baseane Nangaa, a former Governor of Haut-Uélé and senator, fled to Dubai after learning security forces were searching for him. The government subsequently seized all his assets, accusing him of collaborating with the rebel group, despite his claims of loyalty to President Félix Tshisekedi’s administration.
Family members indicate that around ten other relatives remain imprisoned in separate facilities on accusations of supporting AFC/M23, while others have sought refuge in various countries in Africa and the Americas over the past two years.
The arrests and escapes are part of ongoing security operations in the Wamba area of Haut-Uélé, where authorities suspect hidden weapons caches linked to the rebel group.

title: DRC Soldier Sentenced to 20 Years of Community Service for Battlefield Videos
excerpt: Ituri, January 23, 2026 - The Ituri Military Court has sentenced Captain Buba Ambwa Jean Denis, a DRC army officer, to 20 years of community service and dismissal from the military for filming and sharing videos on the battlefield. Captain Ambwa, who commanded troops on Lake Albe
title_en: DRC Soldier Sentenced to 20 Years of Community Service for Battlefield Videos
excerpt_en: Ituri, January 23, 2026 - The Ituri Military Court has sentenced Captain Buba Ambwa Jean Denis, a DRC army officer, to 20 years of community service and dismissal from the military for filming and sharing videos on the battlefield. Captain Ambwa, who commanded troops on Lake Albe
body_en:
Ituri, January 23, 2026 - The Ituri Military Court has sentenced Captain Buba Ambwa Jean Denis, a DRC army officer, to 20 years of community service and dismissal from the military for filming and sharing videos on the battlefield.
Captain Ambwa, who commanded troops on Lake Albert, filmed his soldiers on October 8, 2025, while traveling by speedboat to the Nyamamba area to confront the CRP rebel group, founded by Thomas Lubanga. He posted the videos on social media, in defiance of orders prohibiting battlefield recordings.
The military court ruled on January 21, 2026, that Ambwa disobeyed direct orders from his superiors, justifying the sentence.
“The posting of battlefield videos violated operational security and the chain of command,” military authorities stated.
Ambwa’s lawyers expressed dissatisfaction with the ruling and immediately filed an appeal, challenging the court’s decision.
The case has sparked debate within military circles about the use of social media by soldiers and the enforcement of operational discipline in active conflict zones.

title: Burundi Accused of Abusing Congolese Refugees as Death Toll Rises
excerpt: Bujumbura, January 12, 2026 - The Burundian government is facing serious accusations of deliberately blocking the voluntary return of Congolese refugees, despite reports that security has improved in parts of eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), particularly in AFC/M23-con
title_en: Burundi Accused of Abusing Congolese Refugees as Death Toll Rises
excerpt_en: Bujumbura, January 12, 2026 - The Burundian government is facing serious accusations of deliberately blocking the voluntary return of Congolese refugees, despite reports that security has improved in parts of eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), particularly in AFC/M23-con
body_en:
Bujumbura, January 12, 2026 - The Burundian government is facing serious accusations of deliberately blocking the voluntary return of Congolese refugees, despite reports that security has improved in parts of eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), particularly in AFC/M23-controlled areas of Uvira territory.
More than 101,000 Congolese refugees are currently crowded into makeshift camps across Burundi, including in Muyinga, Cibitoke, Rumonge, Gatumba, and Bubanza, where access to food, healthcare, and basic services remains critically inadequate.
Zakari Moluh, coordinator for Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) at the Ndava camp in Cibitoke, described the situation as dire.
“The camp is overcrowded. Families are forced to live in tents, the ground is muddy, and people are sharing a two-liter bottle of water. Food is practically nonexistent,” Moluh said.
On January 5, 2026, the Coalition for Peace and Human Rights (CPCC) reported that 105 Congolese refugees had died in Burundian detention camps within a two-week period. According to the organization, most deaths were caused by lack of shelter, medical care, and severe malnutrition. Some fatalities, however, were allegedly the result of attacks by Burundian civilians armed with traditional weapons, including arrows.
To date, Burundian authorities have not issued an official response or announced any investigations into the reported deaths.
Sources also allege that Burundian security forces beat and killed up to 20 Congolese refugees who refused transfer to the Ruyigi camp, located near the border.
Critics accuse the Burundian government of maintaining harsh camp conditions in support of the DRC government’s narrative that AFC/M23-controlled areas remain insecure and that the group is responsible for civilian displacement. However, multiple reports indicate that civilians have returned to these areas and are resuming normal activities such as farming, herding, and trade.
While Burundian authorities claim they are protecting refugees from insecurity, humanitarian organizations warn that the rising death toll could worsen if border crossings at Gatumba and Vugizo are not reopened to allow voluntary returns.
Some refugees have reportedly crossed back into the DRC illegally, including by swimming across the Rusizi River, while others have allegedly bribed security officials to facilitate their passage.
Human rights activist Gentil Mulume said many refugees are eager to return home but are being blocked.
“Many of our compatriots have expressed their desire to return voluntarily but have been prevented from leaving the camps, in violation of basic humanitarian principles and refugee protection law,” Mulume said. “We call on the Burundian government to open the way for Congolese refugees to return safely. Our compatriots are not prisoners of war, criminals, or people sentenced to death.”
Observers increasingly describe the crisis not as a humanitarian emergency alone, but as a political crisis, alleging that the policies of Burundian President Évariste Ndayishimiye and Congolese President Félix Tshisekedi are endangering civilian lives and may constitute crimes against humanity.

title: AFC/M23 Confirms Joseph Kabila Is in the DRC
excerpt: Goma, January 13, 2026 - The leader of the AFC/M23 coalition, Corneille Nangaa Yobeluo, has confirmed that former Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) President Joseph Kabila Kabange is currently in the country. Speaking on January 12, 2026, during a meeting between AFC/M23 leaders
title_en: AFC/M23 Confirms Joseph Kabila Is in the DRC
excerpt_en: Goma, January 13, 2026 - The leader of the AFC/M23 coalition, Corneille Nangaa Yobeluo, has confirmed that former Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) President Joseph Kabila Kabange is currently in the country. Speaking on January 12, 2026, during a meeting between AFC/M23 leaders
body_en:
Goma, January 13, 2026 - The leader of the AFC/M23 coalition, Corneille Nangaa Yobeluo, has confirmed that former Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) President Joseph Kabila Kabange is currently in the country.
Speaking on January 12, 2026, during a meeting between AFC/M23 leaders and community peace representatives from North Kivu Province, Nangaa announced that Kabila would eventually meet them.
“We have a guest here, the former President of the Republic, Joseph Kabila. Do you know he is here? One day we will bring him to meet you,” Nangaa said. He added that although Kabila holds the constitutional status of senator for life, he was removed from the Senate.
Kabila was last seen publicly in June 2025 in areas under AFC/M23 control, where he reportedly held discussions with citizens from various backgrounds on pathways to restoring peace in the country. During that period, he established a temporary office at his residence in the Kinyogote area, west of Goma.
Following those activities, Kabila was prosecuted in Kinshasa’s High Military Court and sentenced to death in absentia, after being convicted of crimes including treason and membership in an illegal armed group.
After June 2025, Kabila traveled to several African countries, including Kenya, where he founded a political coalition known as “Sauvons le DRC”, aimed at addressing the country’s ongoing political and security challenges.

title: AFC/M23 Claims Stability in Goma After One Year of Control
excerpt: Goma, January 12, 2026 - The AFC/M23 coalition says the city of Goma has seen a significant reduction in violence after one year under its control. Corneille Nangaa, coordinator of the coalition, made the announcement during a meeting with representatives from Lubero, Walikale, M
title_en: AFC/M23 Claims Stability in Goma After One Year of Control
excerpt_en: Goma, January 12, 2026 - The AFC/M23 coalition says the city of Goma has seen a significant reduction in violence after one year under its control. Corneille Nangaa, coordinator of the coalition, made the announcement during a meeting with representatives from Lubero, Walikale, M
body_en:
Goma, January 12, 2026 - The AFC/M23 coalition says the city of Goma has seen a significant reduction in violence after one year under its control. Corneille Nangaa, coordinator of the coalition, made the announcement during a meeting with representatives from Lubero, Walikale, Masisi, Nyiragongo, Rutshuru, and South Kivu.
“A year has passed since this city was liberated from the clutches of murderers,” Nangaa said. “Now, by the grace of God and the dedication of our troops, but especially by the contribution of everyone, we now sleep and sleep. The so-called 40 bandits are no longer there. The endless killings and shootings are now history.”
He praised the coalition’s security forces for maintaining order and protecting residents and their property, despite what he described as interference from the Kinshasa government, including salary suspensions, bank closures, and disruptions to electricity and communications.
“Kinshasa has stopped our salaries, closed banks, stolen our savings, and continues to seize resources. Yet we have shown that we are citizens who can find solutions and are committed to fighting for change until it is complete,” Nangaa said.
The AFC/M23 captured Goma and Bukavu at the end of January 2025 and has maintained control over the cities since then. The coalition emphasizes that security has improved for residents, marking a shift from the widespread violence reported before their takeover.
body_fr:
Goma, January 12, 2026 - The AFC/M23 coalition says the city of Goma has seen a significant reduction in violence after one year under its control. Corneille Nangaa, coordinator of the coalition, made the announcement during a meeting with representatives from Lubero, Walikale, Masisi, Nyiragongo, Rutshuru, and South Kivu.
“A year has passed since this city was liberated from the clutches of murderers,” Nangaa said. “Now, by the grace of God and the dedication of our troops, but especially by the contribution of everyone, we now sleep and sleep. The so-called 40 bandits are no longer there. The endless killings and shootings are now history.”
He praised the coalition’s security forces for maintaining order and protecting residents and their property, despite what he described as interference from the Kinshasa government, including salary suspensions, bank closures, and disruptions to electricity and communications.
“Kinshasa has stopped our salaries, closed banks, stolen our savings, and continues to seize resources. Yet we have shown that we are citizens who can find solutions and are committed to fighting for change until it is complete,” Nangaa said.
The AFC/M23 captured Goma and Bukavu at the end of January 2025 and has maintained control over the cities since then. The coalition emphasizes that security has improved for residents, marking a shift from the widespread violence reported before their takeover.

title: Brig. Gen. Charles Simuyuni Nakeempa Appointed Head of Great Lakes Regional Border Security Mechanism
excerpt: Livingstone, Zambia, January 13, 2026 - Brigadier General Charles Simuyuni Nakeempa of the Zambian army has been appointed as the new head of the Great Lakes Africa Regional Joint Border Security Mechanism (MCVE/EJVM). The decision was made during a meeting of regional defense mi
title_en: Brig. Gen. Charles Simuyuni Nakeempa Appointed Head of Great Lakes Regional Border Security Mechanism
excerpt_en: Livingstone, Zambia, January 13, 2026 - Brigadier General Charles Simuyuni Nakeempa of the Zambian army has been appointed as the new head of the Great Lakes Africa Regional Joint Border Security Mechanism (MCVE/EJVM). The decision was made during a meeting of regional defense mi
body_en:
Livingstone, Zambia, January 13, 2026 - Brigadier General Charles Simuyuni Nakeempa of the Zambian army has been appointed as the new head of the Great Lakes Africa Regional Joint Border Security Mechanism (MCVE/EJVM). The decision was made during a meeting of regional defense ministers held on January 10, 2026, in Livingstone, Zambia. Rwanda’s Defence Minister Juvenal Marizamunda attended the meeting.
The regional council also announced that Colonel Arlindo Sebastiao Vandunem Fernandes from Angola will serve as deputy head of the EJVM.
Established in September 2012, the EJVM was created to manage and resolve border security disputes between member countries through investigation and military expertise. The body is headquartered in Goma and has played a key role in de-escalating regional conflicts and assisting in operations involving cross-border security incidents.
The EJVM has been involved in numerous border security interventions, including the July 20, 2021 operation when Rwanda handed over 19 fighters of the RED Tabara armed group captured in Nyungwe Park to Burundi, with EJVM personnel participating in the process.

title: DRC Army Accused of Drone Strike on Kalundu Bridge in Uvira
excerpt: The AFC/M23 coalition has accused the Democratic Republic of Congo’s army of carrying out a major drone attack in Uvira, South Kivu province, on the afternoon of January 14, 2026. According to AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, the Congolese armed forces used unmanned aerial
title_en: DRC Army Accused of Drone Strike on Kalundu Bridge in Uvira
excerpt_en: The AFC/M23 coalition has accused the Democratic Republic of Congo’s army of carrying out a major drone attack in Uvira, South Kivu province, on the afternoon of January 14, 2026. According to AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, the Congolese armed forces used unmanned aerial
body_en:
The AFC/M23 coalition has accused the Democratic Republic of Congo’s army of carrying out a major drone attack in Uvira, South Kivu province, on the afternoon of January 14, 2026.
According to AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, the Congolese armed forces used unmanned aerial vehicles to bomb the Kalundu bridge in Uvira territory, causing extensive damage and putting civilian lives at risk. Photographs shared by Kanyuka on social media show a large residential building severely damaged by the strike.
“In the face of these serious acts, AFC/M23 calls on citizens and the international community to bear witness to the actions of the Kinshasa government that ignore its commitments, especially the Doha principles,” Kanyuka said.
The alleged strike follows another drone attack attributed to the Congolese army on January 12 in the Mukoko area of Minembwe commune and other border zones, which reportedly claimed the lives of several civilians.
These developments come amid ongoing peace talks in Doha between the Congolese government and AFC/M23. The coalition accuses the government of undermining the negotiations through continued military operations.
Meanwhile, President Félix Tshisekedi is reportedly working to launch a new national dialogue in Kinshasa, bringing together Congolese from all ethnic groups-a move that critics say could sideline the Doha process and its outcomes.

title: Jamaica Welcomes Rwandan Army Team to Support Disaster Recovery Efforts
excerpt: Kingston, January 15, 2026 - The Government of Jamaica has officially welcomed a team of Rwandan Army construction personnel deployed to assist in the recovery and rehabilitation of infrastructure damaged by the disaster. The welcoming ceremony took place at the Royal Jamaican Mi
title_en: Jamaica Welcomes Rwandan Army Team to Support Disaster Recovery Efforts
excerpt_en: Kingston, January 15, 2026 - The Government of Jamaica has officially welcomed a team of Rwandan Army construction personnel deployed to assist in the recovery and rehabilitation of infrastructure damaged by the disaster. The welcoming ceremony took place at the Royal Jamaican Mi
body_en:
Kingston, January 15, 2026 - The Government of Jamaica has officially welcomed a team of Rwandan Army construction personnel deployed to assist in the recovery and rehabilitation of infrastructure damaged by the disaster.
The welcoming ceremony took place at the Royal Jamaican Military Academy in Kingston on 15 January 2026, and was presided over by the Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Trade, Senator Kamina Johnson Smith.
Senator Johnson Smith expressed gratitude to the Government of Rwanda, particularly President Paul Kagame and the people of Rwanda, for their support. She noted that the team’s experience would make a significant contribution to Jamaica’s recovery efforts and praised Rwanda’s partnership and brotherhood in responding to the increasing impacts of climate change-related disasters.
Speaking on behalf of the Rwanda Defence Forces (RDF), Col. Claudien Bizimungu conveyed Rwanda’s solidarity with the Government and people of Jamaica. He delivered a message from the RDF leadership, emphasizing Rwanda’s commitment to standing with Jamaica throughout its rebuilding and repair process.
Col. Bizimungu also highlighted that the deployment reflects Rwanda’s broader vision in international cooperation and relief efforts, underscoring the RDF’s experience in reconstruction and community-based activities.
The Commander of the RDF Reconstruction Team, Col. Moses Kayigamba, stated that the team will work closely with the Jamaican Armed Forces and other government agencies as part of the cooperation agreement between the two countries. He added that the deployment aligns with President Paul Kagame’s decision to cooperate with the Republic of Jamaica, announced during his visit in April 2022.

title: AFC/M23 Hands Over Uvira to International Forces
excerpt: The AFC/M23 coalition fighting the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has announced that it has handed over the city of Uvira to the international community, calling on it to ensure the safety of residents. On December 16, 2025, AFC/M23 said it would withdraw its fighters from th
title_en: AFC/M23 Hands Over Uvira to International Forces
excerpt_en: The AFC/M23 coalition fighting the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has announced that it has handed over the city of Uvira to the international community, calling on it to ensure the safety of residents. On December 16, 2025, AFC/M23 said it would withdraw its fighters from th
body_en:
The AFC/M23 coalition fighting the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has announced that it has handed over the city of Uvira to the international community, calling on it to ensure the safety of residents.
On December 16, 2025, AFC/M23 said it would withdraw its fighters from the city. Two days later, the group claimed it had withdrawn, though the DRC government denied this.
In a letter to the United Nations Secretary-General dated January 15, 2026, AFC/M23 stated that it had requested three days earlier that the UN Mission in the DRC (MONUSCO) protect the city’s population. The request was addressed to the Special Representative of the UN Secretary-General for the DRC and Acting Head of MONUSCO, Vivian Van de Perre.
“Our community, AFC/M23, has decided today to place the city of Uvira under the full responsibility of the international community,” said AFC/M23 leader Corneille Nangaa Yobeluo.
Nangaa explained that the city had been temporarily occupied by a group of AFC/M23 fighters tasked with monitoring the area while awaiting the arrival of an impartial military force, but that they too had withdrawn on January 15.
AFC/M23 informed the United Nations that the Burundian army, the FDLR terrorist group, Wazalendo groups, and the Cancuru are threatening the security of Uvira’s residents.
“Their presence and activities are not only a threat to the security of civilians, but also to the ongoing peace process and the security of the region,” the group said.
The coalition urged the international community to urgently deploy neutral forces to Uvira to prevent a repeat of the suffering experienced when the city was under DRC government control.
AFC/M23 captured Uvira on December 9, 2025, after a week-long battle in parts of the Ruzizi Valley in South Kivu Province. It said the withdrawal was made at the request of the United States to allow peace talks to continue. According to the group, the U.S. asked it to return to its former positions, within 75 kilometers of Uvira, assuring that only then could the international community ensure the protection of civilians.
When the UN Security Council voted to extend MONUSCO’s mandate for another year, it assigned the mission new responsibilities, including monitoring the peace process in South Kivu Province, suggesting that troops may soon be deployed to Uvira.
Twirwaneho Shoots Down DRC Army Drone
The MRDP-Twirwaneho armed group fighting the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has announced that it has shot down one of the DRC army drones, which it accuses of targeting Banyamulenge civilians in South Kivu Province.
Twirwaneho’s spokesman, Col. Kamasa Ndakize Welcome, said that on January 15, 2026, forces from the DRC, Burundi, the FDLR, and Wazalendo groups carried out attacks in the Point-Zéro area, located about 10 kilometers from Minembwe commune.
“This operation included ground and drone attacks, which deliberately targeted residents of the Rwitsankuku center and surrounding areas, destroying civilian infrastructure, forcing residents to flee, and putting the lives of innocent civilians in grave danger,” Col. Kamasa said.
He added that these attacks prompted Twirwaneho fighters to intervene, shoot down the coalition’s drone, and capture key areas, including Mount Baruta, which he said had long been used by opposing forces.
“In response to these actions, MRDP-Twirwaneho fighters immediately moved to defend civilians, shot down the enemy drone that was firing on civilian areas, repelled the ground attack, destroyed enemy positions, and captured key areas, including Mount Baruta, which had long been used to fire at civilians,” he said.
Twirwaneho declared that it would not tolerate the atrocities committed by the coalition of DRC government forces and said it would continue to fulfill its duty to protect civilians and their property.

title: Twirwaneho Captures Point-Zéro from DRC Government Forces
excerpt: On January 16, 2026, MRDP-Twirwaneho announced that it had captured Point-Zéro from the DRC government forces, marking a significant development in the conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. The armed group, which is fighting the DRC government, seized Point-Zéro, a st
title_en: Twirwaneho Captures Point-Zéro from DRC Government Forces
excerpt_en: On January 16, 2026, MRDP-Twirwaneho announced that it had captured Point-Zéro from the DRC government forces, marking a significant development in the conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. The armed group, which is fighting the DRC government, seized Point-Zéro, a st
body_en:
On January 16, 2026, MRDP-Twirwaneho announced that it had captured Point-Zéro from the DRC government forces, marking a significant development in the conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
The armed group, which is fighting the DRC government, seized Point-Zéro, a strategic area for the coalition of DRC forces, Burundian troops, Wazalendo groups, and the FDLR terrorist group. The capture came on the morning of January 16, a day after Twirwaneho had taken other key positions in Fizi territory, including Mount Baruta, and shot down a drone belonging to the DRC government forces.
The Twirwaneho leadership said that after losing Point-Zéro, Mount Baruta, and Isumo, coalition forces fled toward the Mulima and Mutambala areas.
Point-Zéro had served as a key base for the DRC government forces, blocking the road connecting Minembwe commune with other parts of Fizi and Uvira territories. The base was also used to plan and launch major attacks on Minembwe areas inhabited by the Banyamulenge, as well as other locations where they had sought refuge, including Mikenke.
Analyst Dr. Alex Mvuka, who closely monitors the situation in the DRC, said that Point-Zéro was one of three key locations for government forces.
“They used Point-Zéro as a base to launch indiscriminate attacks on the Banyamulenge villages in the highlands in general and in the Minembwe area in particular,” Dr. Mvuka said.
Supporters of the DRC government have expressed concern that following the fall of Point-Zéro, Twirwaneho fighters could advance further into Fizi, including Mulima, Fizi center, and the town of Baraka.

title_en: 47 Officers Complete Training at Police College
excerpt_en: Musanze District, January 16, 2026 - Forty-seven police officers and other security personnel at the level of junior officers have successfully completed a five-month training course on leadership and conflict resolution at the Police College (NPC) in Musanze District. The 13th P
body_en:
Musanze District, January 16, 2026 - Forty-seven police officers and other security personnel at the level of junior officers have successfully completed a five-month training course on leadership and conflict resolution at the Police College (NPC) in Musanze District.
The 13th Police Junior Command and Staff Course (PJCSC) included 36 Rwanda National Police officers, five officers from the National Correctional Service (RCS), five officers from the National Bureau of Investigation (RBI), and one officer from the National Intelligence and Security Service (NISS).
The Deputy Inspector General of Police (DIGP) for Administration and Personnel, DCG Jeanne Chantal Ujeneza, highlighted the purpose of the training, describing it as a foundation for developing leadership and professionalism among junior officers.
“This training aims to enhance leadership skills in junior officers. In today’s world, security challenges are evolving due to technological developments, not just job experience. Effective leadership requires forward-thinking, planning, coordination, and decision-making that provide solutions to current challenges,” she said.
She added, “We hope that the knowledge and skills gained from this training will help you address security threats, both conventional and technological.”
DIGP Ujeneza emphasized that leadership is not defined solely by rank, but also by integrity, responsibility, fairness, and the ability to make decisions that protect the public, uphold the law, and promote national interests. She reminded graduates to exercise their authority professionally and responsibly.
The Commissioner of Police (CP) Rafiki Mujiji, head of the Police Academy, said the course focused on professional conduct and ethics, reinforced through practical exercises, collaboration, teamwork, and field trips that helped students apply knowledge in real-world contexts.
CP Mujiji encouraged graduates to make full use of the skills gained in their work assignments, noting that their role extends beyond following instructions. Officers are expected to think strategically, provide sound advice, lead effectively, uphold ethics and values, and utilize modern methods and tools to improve performance and deliver efficient and timely services.

title: DRC Army Accused of Supplying Ammunition to FDLR and Allied Armed Groups
excerpt: January 17, 2026 ; The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) are accused of providing additional tons of ammunition to the FDLR and other allied armed groups to support their fight against the AFC/M23 coalition. Reports from North Kivu Province indicate that on
title_en: DRC Army Accused of Supplying Ammunition to FDLR and Allied Armed Groups
excerpt_en: January 17, 2026 ; The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) are accused of providing additional tons of ammunition to the FDLR and other allied armed groups to support their fight against the AFC/M23 coalition. Reports from North Kivu Province indicate that on
body_en:
January 17, 2026 ; The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) are accused of providing additional tons of ammunition to the FDLR and other allied armed groups to support their fight against the AFC/M23 coalition.
Reports from North Kivu Province indicate that on January 14, 2026, weapons, ammunition, and funds were delivered to leaders of the FDLR, CMC/Domi, and ANCDH/Nyatura Abazungu.
The operation reportedly took place at the DRC military base of Pinga in Walikale Territory and involved several Abanye-Congolese officers. Among those present were Col. Mokoko, responsible for operations in the 34th Military Region; Col. Salomon Tokolonga, commander of the 3402nd Regiment and acting head of forces in Pinga; and the North Kivu Wazalendo coordinator, Col. Cyprien Semivumbi.
Although the DRC government maintains that any collaboration between its soldiers and the FDLR is carried out on an individual basis, the organization and execution of the operation in Pinga suggest a coordinated effort within a broader state program.
Following the delivery, the FDLR and allied groups reportedly transported the weapons and ammunition to active conflict zones, including Bashali-Mokoto, Malemo, and Buhimba in Masisi Territory, as well as Jardin Théicole de Ngeri (JTN) and Katsiro in Rutshuru Territory.
Additional reports indicate that on January 13, more than 50 Blackwater mercenaries were deployed to Pinga to assist the DRC army and allied groups in operations along the Masisi-Walikale border.
Previously, on November 28, 2025, the DRC government reportedly delivered three tons of ammunition to Pinga, intended for the FDLR, NDC-R, and other Nyatura groups, following instructions from Col. Tokolonga.
The continued support for the FDLR and other armed groups, as well as the alleged use of mercenaries, raises questions about the DRC government’s commitment to the peace agreement signed with Rwanda on June 27, 2025, brokered by the United States. Under the agreement, the DRC had pledged to dismantle the FDLR, but the reported actions suggest that implementation remains uncertain.
